# MMLAW Law Firm (mmlaw.ge)

> MMLAW is a criminal defence law firm in Georgia (office in Tbilisi) with more than 10 years of practice. Criminal law is its main practice: it defends accused and convicted persons, witnesses and victims at every stage — from the first contact with the investigating authority, through interviews and questioning, investigative actions, preventive measures and trial (including jury trials) to the final decision of the Supreme Court. Areas include drug, property, economic, corruption, violent and cyber crimes, and juvenile cases. The firm also handles civil, administrative, labour, corporate, real estate, family, inheritance and intellectual property matters. Consultations in Georgian, English and Russian; the first consultation is free.

- Lawyer: Mariam Madzgharashvili (მარიამ მაძღარაშვილი). Lawyer, member of the Georgian Bar Association, specialising in criminal law, and a member of the Association's Jury Trial Committee. She focuses on criminal law, juvenile justice and children's rights, and holds a doctorate in law. Works in Georgian, English and Russian. She is a mentor in the Bar Association's Professional Adaptation Programme. Education: Doctor of Law (PhD), Georgian American University (2025); LLM in Criminal Law, Ilia State University. ## About the firm

We represent individuals and companies in criminal, civil, administrative, labour, corporate, real estate, family and intellectual property matters — in negotiations, before public authorities and in courts of every instance in Georgia.
Our approach is simple: every client works directly with an attorney, gets an honest assessment of their case and a clear plan of action. We work in Georgian, English and Russian, so foreign clients and companies can get legal help in a language they understand.

- Uncompromising integrity: We operate with complete transparency. Our reputation is our most valuable asset.
- Relentless excellence: Good enough is never enough. We dig deeper, prepare harder and think further ahead.
- Client stewardship: We don't just handle cases — we champion people.

## How we work

1. Free consultation — Call or send a request. We listen and explain your options.
2. Case analysis — We review documents and evidence and assess the risks.
3. Legal strategy — A clear plan of action, agreed with you before we proceed.
4. Representation — We protect your interests in negotiations and in court.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I choose a lawyer in Georgia?
Choose a lawyer with experience in your type of case, who gives you an honest assessment of the risks and agrees the fee in advance and in writing. At MMLAW the first consultation is free, so you can meet the lawyer before deciding.

### How much does the initial consultation cost?
The initial consultation is free. We review your situation, explain your options and, if needed, propose terms for our engagement.

### What documents should I bring?
Bring everything related to your case: ID, contracts, court decisions, notices, police or official reports and correspondence. If you don't have the documents, contact us anyway — we can help obtain them.

### How long will my case take?
Every case is different. Some matters are settled through negotiation within weeks; court disputes can take months or longer. We give you a realistic estimate at the first consultation.

### Do you work on a success-fee basis?
In certain categories of cases — yes. The fee structure and amount are agreed in advance and in writing, so there are no hidden costs.

### Which languages do you work in?
We provide consultations and representation in Georgian, English and Russian — including for foreign nationals and international companies.

### Where do you represent clients?
We represent clients before courts of all instances in Georgia — district (city) courts, courts of appeal and the Supreme Court — as well as before administrative bodies and investigative authorities.

## Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/criminal-defense-lawyer/

MMLAW criminal defense lawyers represent accused and convicted persons, witnesses and victims at every stage of a criminal case in Georgia — from the first contact with the investigating authority to the final decision of the Supreme Court.

Criminal defense requires experience, strategic thinking and relentless dedication to the client. MMLAW defends clients in all types of criminal cases.
We handle serious and particularly serious offences, economic crime, cybercrime, drug-related cases and other categories of cases.

### What a criminal defense lawyer does

A criminal defense lawyer protects your rights at every stage of a criminal case: assists you during questioning, attends investigative actions, gathers evidence for the defense, challenges unlawful decisions and defends you in court. The goal is a fair outcome — with your rights respected at every step.

### When you need a criminal defense lawyer

- When you are summoned for questioning — as a witness or an accused
- When your home or workplace is being searched
- When you or a relative has been arrested
- When you have been charged or offered a plea agreement
- When you are a victim of a crime and want your interests protected

### Stages of a criminal case in Georgia

1. Arrest and charge — a person must be charged within 48 hours of arrest and brought before a court within the following 24 hours.
2. First appearance hearing — the court decides on a preventive measure (for example bail or detention).
3. Pre-trial hearing — the court decides which evidence will be admitted at trial.
4. Trial — the court hears both sides, examines the evidence and delivers a verdict.
5. Appeal — the verdict can be appealed to the Court of Appeals and then, by cassation, to the Supreme Court.

Involving a lawyer as early as possible — ideally from the first contact with the investigating authority — often decides the outcome.

### If a relative has been arrested — what to do

1. Find out where they are and which authority arrested them.
2. Contact a lawyer as quickly as possible — a detained person has the right to a lawyer and the right not to give a statement.
3. Don't discuss the details of the case by phone or in messengers.
4. Prepare documents the court may consider when choosing a preventive measure: a letter from their employer, information about family, children and health.
5. A detained person has the right to ask for a free medical examination — this matters if there are signs of violence.

### After an arrest — the first 72 hours

- Immediately — rights explained, the right to a lawyer, the right to remain silent and a free medical examination
- Within 48 hours — the charge; if no charge is brought, the person must be released
- Within the next 24 hours — the court appearance, where the preventive measure is decided: bail, detention or another measure
- Meanwhile, the lawyer prepares arguments and documents so the court chooses a lighter measure

### Free or private lawyer

If you can't afford a lawyer, in some cases the state pays for your defence through the Legal Aid Service. A private lawyer is someone you choose yourself: their experience, specialisation and how much time they give your case. You can hire a private lawyer at any stage of the case.

### Cases we handle

We defend clients in cases of serious and particularly serious crimes, economic and financial crime, cybercrime, drug-related offences and other categories — acting for accused and convicted persons, witnesses and victims.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Giving statements without a lawyer — you have the right to remain silent
- Signing a record or document you don't understand
- Discussing the case by phone, in messengers or on social media
- Contacting witnesses or the victim yourself
- Missing appeal deadlines — they are short

Our services:
- Defence from the first contact with the investigating authority
- Representation during investigation and at pre-trial hearings
- Challenging preventive measures, including detention
- Plea agreement negotiations
- Defense at trial
- Jury trials — full service from jury selection to the verdict (our lawyer Mariam Madzgharashvili is a member of the Georgian Bar Association's Jury Trial Committee)
- Appeals and cassation complaints
- Protecting witnesses' rights during questioning
- Representation of victims

### When do I have the right to a lawyer in Georgia?
From the moment of arrest or of being charged — and before any questioning. You have the right to remain silent and to insist on your lawyer being present.

### How long can I be held without a court decision?
A person must be charged within 48 hours of arrest and brought before a court within the following 24 hours. If this doesn't happen, they must be released immediately.

### What is a plea agreement?
An agreement between the prosecution and the accused on guilt and sentence, which must be approved by the court. A defense lawyer's participation is mandatory. Never sign anything without independent legal advice.

### When should I contact a criminal defense lawyer?
As early as possible — ideally as soon as you are summoned for questioning, or during a search or arrest. Involving a lawyer early often decides the outcome: your lawyer helps you avoid mistakes when giving statements and protects your rights while evidence is gathered.

### How much does a criminal defense lawyer cost?
It depends on the complexity, stage and scope of the case. The first consultation is free — we assess the case and agree the fee with you in advance and in writing.

### Can I refuse to give a statement?
Yes. The accused has the right to remain silent — you can decline to answer questions and speak to a lawyer first.

### Can a relative hire a lawyer for me?
Yes. When someone is detained, it is often family members who find the lawyer. Call us or message us on WhatsApp — we'll tell you what to do first.

### Am I entitled to a free lawyer?
If you can't pay, or your case is one of mandatory defence (for example a minor or a jury trial) and you have no private lawyer, the state pays for your defence through the Legal Aid Service.

## Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/drug-crime-lawyer/

Drug crime lawyer in Georgia: we defend accused and convicted persons, witnesses and victims in drug-related criminal and administrative cases — from the first minute of an arrest or search.

Drug offences are covered by Chapter XXXIII of the Criminal Code of Georgia. The penalty depends mainly on the act (buying and possession, making and transporting, sale, import) and on the amount — small, large or especially large. The amounts are set in an annex to the law.
In these cases the outcome often turns on whether the search was lawful, how the substance was seized and stored, and what the forensic examination shows. That is why a lawyer should be involved as soon as you are arrested or a search begins.

### When you need a lawyer

- You or a family member were arrested over drugs
- You are summoned for questioning — as a witness or an accused
- Your home or car was searched and something was seized
- You were taken for, or asked to take, a drug test
- You received a fine or administrative detention
- You are contacted about a parcel sent by post

### If you are arrested

1. Stay calm and don't resist.
2. Use your right to remain silent — give no statement without a lawyer.
3. Don't sign a record you disagree with — you can add a note.
4. Ask for a lawyer and for a family member to be informed.
5. Remember who was present at the search and what was taken.

A person must be charged within 48 hours of arrest, and within the following 24 hours a court must decide on a preventive measure.

### What we check in your defence

- Whether the search and seizure were lawful
- How the substance was packed, stored and sent for examination
- The forensic report — what the substance is and how much
- Whether there was police entrapment
- Whether the act is classified under the right article

Our services:
- Defence against possession charges
- Defence in sale and supply cases
- Defence in import, export and parcel cases
- Defence in cultivation cases
- Administrative cases — fines and administrative detention
- Checking the search and forensic examination
- Appealing a preventive measure
- Plea agreements and appeals

### Is using drugs a crime in Georgia?
The first time, in a small amount — as a rule, no. It is an administrative offence: a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or administrative detention of up to 60 days. If it happens again after an administrative penalty, it becomes a criminal offence.

### What is the penalty for buying or possessing drugs?
Under Article 260 of the Criminal Code — imprisonment of up to 6 years; for a large amount or other aggravating circumstances, 5 to 8 years; for an especially large amount or by an organised group, 8 to 20 years or life. Much depends on the amount and the evidence.

### Is marijuana punished?
Buying or possessing a small amount of marijuana is an administrative offence — a GEL 500 fine. Using it in public places, in front of minors or near schools carries higher fines. Large amounts and sale are criminal offences.

### Can I refuse a drug test?
Avoiding a test is itself an administrative offence — a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or administrative detention of up to 60 days. Call a lawyer before you decide.

### If I hand drugs over voluntarily, am I liable?
By law, a person who voluntarily hands over the substance is released from criminal liability, unless the act contains another crime. It counts as voluntary only if declared before an investigation starts and the person actively helps with the seizure.

### What other consequences can there be?
Besides a criminal record, a court may take away certain rights, including the right to drive, under the Law on Combating Drug Crime.

## Cybercrime lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/cybercrime-lawyer/

We defend accused persons and witnesses in cybercrime cases in Georgia and help victims of online fraud, account hacking, blackmail and other digital harm.

Cybercrime covers unauthorised access to computer systems, unlawful use or damage of data, and the use of tools designed for such acts. Traditional crimes — fraud, extortion, threats and invasion of privacy — are also increasingly committed online.
In these cases, digital evidence decides everything — phones, computers, accounts and transactions. That's why a lawyer should be involved as early as possible: for victims, to preserve the evidence; for the accused, to check whether the digital evidence was obtained lawfully.

### When you need a cybercrime lawyer

- You were defrauded online and lost money
- Your account, email or social media was hacked
- You're being threatened or blackmailed with private photos or information
- Someone created a fake profile or acts in your name
- You've been summoned for questioning in a cybercrime case
- Your phone or computer was seized and you don't know what happens next

### If you are a victim

1. Don't delete anything — save messages, links, transactions and dated screenshots.
2. Contact your bank immediately if money was taken or you shared card details.
3. Change your passwords and turn on two-factor authentication.
4. If you're being blackmailed, don't pay and stop communicating with the offender.
5. Contact a lawyer — they'll prepare the complaint to the police and protect your interests throughout.

### If you are accused

- Don't give statements without a lawyer — you have the right to remain silent
- Talk to your lawyer before giving out device passwords
- Your lawyer checks whether the digital evidence was obtained lawfully
- If needed, the defense brings in an independent expert

### Mistakes to avoid

- Deleting messages and evidence
- Paying a blackmailer
- Trusting unknown "money recovery" services
- Sharing case details on social media
- Signing a device seizure record without reading it

Our services:
- Defense against cybercrime charges
- Representing victims of online fraud
- Account hacking and personal data cases
- Help for victims of online blackmail and threats
- Cryptocurrency fraud cases
- Review of digital evidence and expert analysis

### What counts as cybercrime?
Unauthorised access to a computer system, unlawful use or damage of data, and using tools designed for such acts. Fraud, extortion and threats committed online are criminal offences too.

### I was scammed online. Can I get my money back?
Sometimes, yes — especially if you act fast: contact your bank, keep all the evidence and talk to a lawyer. Don't trust services that promise to recover money for an upfront fee.

### I'm being blackmailed with private photos. What should I do?
Don't pay and stop replying, but don't delete anything. Contact a lawyer right away — blackmail and sharing private images are criminal offences.

### Can the police take my phone?
As a rule, seizing a device and examining its contents requires a court order. Talk to your lawyer before signing any record or giving out passwords.

## Property crime lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/property-crime-lawyer/

Property crime lawyer in Georgia: we defend accused and convicted persons, witnesses and victims in cases of theft, robbery, fraud, extortion, embezzlement and misappropriation.

Property crimes are covered by Chapter XXIV of the Criminal Code. The penalty depends mainly on the amount: over GEL 150 counts as significant damage, over GEL 10,000 as a large amount.
In these cases it often comes down to how the property was valued, whether there was an intent to appropriate, and what video footage or identification shows. Sometimes what is presented as a crime is really a civil dispute.

### Cases we handle

- Theft — secret taking (Article 177)
- Open theft (ძარცვა, Article 178): 3 to 5 years, up to 11 with aggravating circumstances
- Robbery with violence dangerous to life or health (Article 179): 5 to 7 years, up to 15 with aggravating circumstances
- Fraud — taking by deception (Article 180)
- Extortion — demands backed by threats (Article 181): 2 to 4 years, up to 9 with aggravating circumstances
- Misappropriation or embezzlement of entrusted property (Article 182): 3 to 5 years, up to 11 with aggravating circumstances

### What we check in your defence

- The valuation of the property — it decides which part of the article applies
- Whether the act is classified correctly: theft, open theft or robbery
- Whether identification, search and seizure were lawful
- Whether the case is really a civil dispute

### Compensating the damage

Compensating the damage and reaching agreement with the victim can affect the sentence and the preventive measure. When and how to do it is something to decide with your lawyer.

Our services:
- Defence against theft charges
- Defence against robbery charges
- Defence against fraud charges
- Defence against extortion charges
- Defence against embezzlement charges
- Checking damage valuations
- Representing victims

### What is the difference between theft, open theft and robbery?
Theft is secret taking; open theft (ძარცვა) is taking openly, in front of others; robbery is an attack with violence dangerous to life or health, or the threat of it. Penalties get stricter in that order.

### What counts as significant damage and a large amount?
For property crimes, significant damage is a value over GEL 150, and a large amount is over GEL 10,000. Both make the penalty stricter.

### I couldn't repay a debt. Is that fraud?
Not necessarily. Fraud requires an intent to deceive from the start. If an obligation simply wasn't met, it is often a civil dispute.

### If I compensate the damage, will the case be dropped?
Compensation doesn't end the case automatically, but it can affect the sentence, the preventive measure or the terms of a plea agreement.

## Economic crime lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/economic-crime-lawyer/

Economic crime lawyer in Georgia: we defend company directors, business owners and individuals against tax evasion, money laundering, customs violations and other economic charges.

Economic crime cases often start with a tax audit, a bank report or a customs check. The right steps at that stage often decide whether the case becomes a criminal one at all.
The evidence in these cases is mostly documents — accounts, contracts, bank statements. So a lawyer prepares the defence together with the financial and tax details.

### Cases we handle

- Tax evasion (Article 218) — where the tax due exceeds GEL 100,000: 3 to 5 years; over GEL 150,000 or by a group — 5 to 8 years
- Money laundering (Article 194): 3 to 6 years, up to 12 with aggravating circumstances
- Customs violations — moving large amounts of goods past customs control (Article 214)
- Misappropriation and embezzlement within a company
- Liability of directors and accountants

### Important: 45 working days

By law, there is no criminal liability for tax evasion if, within 45 working days of receiving a tax demand after an audit, the principal amount is paid, deferred or adjusted. So contact a lawyer as soon as you receive a tax demand.

### What we check

- Whether there was intent — a mistake is not a crime
- Whether the amount was calculated correctly
- Who actually made decisions in the company
- Whether seized documents and bank data were obtained lawfully

Our services:
- Defence against tax evasion charges
- Defence against money laundering charges
- Defence in smuggling and customs cases
- Defence against embezzlement charges in a company
- Defence during tax audits
- Defending company directors

### Is any tax debt a crime?
No. Criminal liability arises for intentional tax evasion where the amount exceeds GEL 100,000. Most disputes are resolved with the tax authority and in court.

### I received a tax demand. What should I do?
Contact a lawyer immediately. If within 45 working days of the demand the principal amount is paid, deferred or adjusted, there is no criminal liability.

### What is money laundering?
Giving illegal or unexplained property a lawful appearance to hide its real origin. The penalty is 3 to 6 years, up to 12 with aggravating circumstances.

### I'm a company director. Am I liable?
That depends on who made which decisions and what they knew. A lawyer checks whether responsibility has been assigned correctly.

## Corruption crime lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/corruption-crime-lawyer/

Corruption crime lawyer in Georgia: we defend public officials, business owners and individuals in cases of bribery, trading in influence and abuse or excess of official power.

Corruption and official crimes are in Chapter XXXIX of the Criminal Code. These are serious charges: taking a bribe carries at least 6 years and often a ban from holding office.
Evidence in these cases is often obtained through covert investigative actions — secret recordings, controlled handovers. So whether it was obtained lawfully is decisive for the defence.

### Cases we handle

- Taking a bribe (Article 338): 6 to 9 years; a large amount (over GEL 10,000) — 7 to 11 years; an especially large amount (over GEL 30,000) or by extortion — 11 to 15 years
- Giving a bribe (Article 339): up to 3 years; to obtain an unlawful act — 4 to 7 years
- Trading in influence (Article 339¹)
- Abuse of official power (Article 332) and exceeding it (Article 333)

### Release of the bribe-giver

By law, a bribe-giver is released from criminal liability if they voluntarily report it to the authority conducting criminal proceedings. That authority makes the decision — so this step must be planned with a lawyer.

### What we check

- Whether covert investigative actions were lawful and authorised by a court
- Whether there was entrapment
- Whether the person is an "official" in the legal sense
- Whether it really was a bribe and not, say, a loan or a gift

Our services:
- Defence against bribe-taking charges
- Defence against bribe-giving charges
- Defence against trading-in-influence charges
- Defence against abuse-of-office charges
- Defence against exceeding-authority charges
- Checking covert evidence

### I was asked for a bribe. What should I do?
Don't pay, and contact a lawyer immediately. A bribe-giver is released from liability if they report it voluntarily — this step must be taken correctly.

### What is the penalty for taking a bribe?
6 to 9 years' imprisonment; for a large amount (over GEL 10,000) 7 to 11 years; for an especially large amount (over GEL 30,000), repeatedly or by extortion, 11 to 15 years.

### Who counts as an official?
Public servants and persons treated as such, including employees of public-law legal entities who exercise public powers.

### I was secretly recorded. Is that evidence?
Only if it was obtained in the way the law requires, with the necessary authorisation. Checking this is one of the main tasks of the defence.

## Violent crime lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/violent-crime-lawyer/

Violent crime lawyer in Georgia: we defend accused and convicted persons, witnesses and victims in cases of bodily injury, violence, threats and homicide, and we help victims.

Violent crimes are acts against life and health — from beating to homicide. The penalty depends on how serious the injury is, which a medical examination establishes, and on aggravating circumstances.
These cases often start from a fight or conflict where both sides used force. So a lawyer should assess early whether it was self-defence.

### Cases we handle

- Beating or other violence causing physical pain (Article 126)
- Intentional minor bodily injury (Article 120): 1 to 3 years
- Intentional less serious bodily injury (Article 118): 2 to 4 years
- Intentional serious bodily injury (Article 117): 4 to 7 years
- Threats (Article 151)
- Intentional homicide (Article 108): 10 to 15 years; with aggravating circumstances (Article 109) — 16 to 20 years or life

### Self-defence

By law, a person who harms an attacker while defending themselves or others against an unlawful attack does not act unlawfully. This right exists even if they could have avoided the attack or called for help. The key is that the defence must not be clearly disproportionate to the attack.

### What we check

- The medical report — the severity of the injury decides the article
- Who started the conflict and whether it was self-defence
- Video footage and witness statements
- Whether intent has been assessed correctly

Our services:
- Defence against assault charges
- Defence against bodily harm charges
- Defence against threat charges
- Defence in murder and attempted murder cases
- Proving self-defence
- Representing victims

### I was defending myself. Am I liable?
If it was lawful self-defence, the act is not unlawful. The question is whether the defence was clearly disproportionate to the attack. A lawyer proves this with evidence.

### How is the severity of an injury decided?
By a medical examination. Minor, less serious and serious injuries fall under different articles — 1 to 3 years, 2 to 4 years and 4 to 7 years.

### There was a fight and we were both hurt. What happens?
In such cases both sides can be both victim and accused. It is important that your version and evidence are recorded correctly from the start.

### What is the penalty for homicide?
Intentional homicide carries 10 to 15 years; with aggravating circumstances, 16 to 20 years or life imprisonment.

## Juvenile lawyer in Georgia: legal help for minors
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/juvenile-justice-lawyer/

We defend children and young people in criminal and related proceedings under Georgia's Juvenile Justice Code, with a focus on rehabilitation and the child's best interests.

Juvenile justice requires a special approach. MMLAW attorneys defend young people's rights in specialised proceedings, focusing on their future and rehabilitation.
We work closely with parents and legal representatives so that the child goes through the process with as little stress as possible.

### What a juvenile justice lawyer does

A juvenile justice lawyer protects a child's rights in criminal proceedings — from questioning to court. The aim is for the child to go through the process with as little stress as possible and for the case to be decided with their future in mind.

### What parents should know

- A minor must have a lawyer during questioning and, as a rule, a parent or legal representative
- Specialised lawyers, prosecutors and judges work on juvenile cases
- In some cases diversion is possible — without criminal prosecution
- Juvenile cases are, as a rule, heard behind closed doors

### A minor's rights in a criminal case

- A free lawyer at any stage of a criminal case — for an accused minor and a minor victim alike, if they have no private lawyer
- Questioning only in the presence of a legal representative (for example a parent) and a lawyer, with a psychologist where needed
- The case is handled only by an investigator, prosecutor, judge and lawyer specialised in juvenile justice
- Information in a form suited to the child's age, and a free interpreter if needed
- Free legal aid also applies to accused and convicted persons aged 18 to 21

### Diversion — resolving the case without a trial

If a minor is accused of a less serious or serious crime, the law requires diversion to be considered first: the prosecutor can decide not to start, or to end, the prosecution if that better serves the child's rehabilitation and prevents new offences. A lawyer assesses this option from the very start of the case.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Agreeing to the child being questioned without a lawyer
- Not using the possibility of diversion
- Sharing case details on social media
- Pressuring the child to "confess"

Our services:
- Defense of minors in criminal cases
- Diversion and mediation
- Representation of minor victims and witnesses
- Protecting the child's rights on arrest
- Advice to parents and guardians

### Is my child entitled to a free lawyer?
Yes. An accused minor and a minor victim are entitled to free legal aid at any stage of a criminal case if they have no private lawyer. A minor witness is entitled if unable to pay or in certain cases defined by law.

### From what age is a person criminally liable in Georgia?
From 14. Special rules of the Juvenile Justice Code apply to persons under 18.

### What is diversion?
Diversion allows a minor to avoid criminal prosecution by meeting certain conditions — for example mediation, community service or a rehabilitation programme. The decision is made by the prosecutor.

### Can any lawyer defend a minor?
No. Under the Code, lawyers, judges, prosecutors and investigators working on juvenile cases must be specialised.

## Civil litigation lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/civil-litigation-lawyer/

We represent individuals and companies in civil disputes in Georgia — from pre-trial negotiation through all three court instances.

Civil disputes cover a wide spectrum — from property disputes to breaches of contract. MMLAW's civil litigation team provides complete legal support at every stage of the process.
We first assess whether the dispute can be resolved faster and at lower cost through negotiation or mediation. If not, we build a strong position for court.

### What a civil litigation lawyer does

A civil litigation lawyer assesses your claim and evidence, tries to settle the dispute by negotiation, prepares the lawsuit if needed and represents you at every court instance — through to enforcement of the judgment.

### When you need a civil litigation lawyer

- Someone won't repay a debt
- A contract has been breached
- You suffered damage and want compensation
- You have a property or neighbour dispute
- You've been sued and need to defend yourself
- A court decision isn't being enforced

### Stages of a civil dispute

1. Assessing the case and gathering evidence.
2. Pre-trial claim and negotiation — many disputes end here.
3. Filing the lawsuit with the district (city) court.
4. Hearing and judgment.
5. Appeal to the Court of Appeals and then to the Supreme Court.
6. Enforcement of the judgment through the National Bureau of Enforcement.

### Documents to prepare

- Contracts and annexes
- Correspondence — emails, messages
- Proof of payments and receipts
- Photos, expert reports, certificates
- Letters received from the court or the other side

### Mistakes to avoid

- Relying only on a verbal agreement
- Deleting or not keeping correspondence and receipts
- Missing the limitation period
- Ignoring court notices
- Signing a document from the other side that you don't understand

Our services:
- Contract disputes and debt recovery
- Property and ownership disputes
- Compensation for damage, including moral damage
- Inheritance disputes
- Enforcement of court decisions
- Mediation and settlement

### How are civil courts organised in Georgia?
First instance — district (city) courts; second instance — the Tbilisi and Kutaisi Courts of Appeal; the final, cassation instance — the Supreme Court of Georgia.

### Can a dispute be resolved without going to court?
Yes — through negotiation, mediation or arbitration. For some categories of disputes (for example certain family, inheritance and neighbour disputes) court mediation may be mandatory.

### How long do I have to file a claim?
It depends on the type of claim. Under the Civil Code of Georgia the general limitation period is 10 years, 3 years for contractual claims and 6 years for claims related to immovable property. Some claims have shorter periods, so it is best to act early.

## Administrative law lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/administrative-law-lawyer/

We help individuals and businesses challenge unlawful decisions of public authorities and navigate licensing, permit and regulatory procedures in Georgia.

Administrative law covers relations with government agencies, licensing, permits and regulatory matters. MMLAW helps you manage bureaucratic processes effectively.
Deadlines in administrative disputes are short, so it matters to contact a lawyer as early as possible — ideally as soon as you receive the decision.

### What an administrative law lawyer does

An administrative law lawyer helps you challenge decisions of public authorities — from fines to permits and tax disputes. We check whether the decision is lawful, prepare the complaint and lawsuit, and represent you in court.

### When you need one

- You were fined and consider it unfair
- A permit, licence or registration was refused
- You have a dispute with the tax or customs authority
- A public body doesn't respond or delays your case
- You were dismissed from the civil service

### Stages of an appeal

1. Note the date you received the decision — the deadline runs from that day.
2. Administrative complaint to the superior body, where the law requires it.
3. Administrative lawsuit in court.
4. Appeal to the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Missing the appeal deadline — it's usually short
- Losing proof of when the decision was delivered
- Ignoring letters from the authority
- Filing a complaint without evidence

Our services:
- Administrative complaints to the superior body
- Administrative lawsuits in court
- Fines and administrative offences
- Licences and permits
- Tax and customs disputes
- Public service (civil service) disputes

### What is the deadline to challenge an administrative act in court?
As a rule, one month from the date the act was officially delivered to you. Some cases have different statutory terms, so check the exact deadline immediately.

### Do I have to file an administrative complaint first?
In some cases the law requires a complaint to the superior body before going to court; in others you may go straight to court. We assess which route is faster and stronger.

### Can a fine be appealed?
Yes. A decision on an administrative offence can be appealed to the superior body or to the court within short statutory deadlines.

## Employment and labour lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/employment-lawyer/

We represent employees and employers in labour disputes under the Labour Code of Georgia — from unlawful dismissal to drafting contracts and workplace policies.

Labour disputes are increasingly relevant in Georgia. MMLAW offers qualified legal support in disputes between employers and employees.
For employers, we help prevent risk by bringing contracts, internal regulations and policies into line with the law.

### What an employment lawyer does

An employment lawyer protects the interests of employees or employers: reviews the contract and the grounds for dismissal, negotiates, prepares complaints and represents you in court.

### When you need an employment lawyer

- You were dismissed and consider it unfair
- Your salary or compensation isn't being paid
- You face discrimination or harassment at work
- You're offered a contract whose terms you don't understand
- You're an employer and want to prevent disputes

### What to do if you are dismissed

1. Ask for the written grounds of your dismissal.
2. Keep every document — contract, dismissal order, correspondence, salary statements.
3. Contact a lawyer immediately — appeal deadlines are short.
4. If needed, challenge the dismissal in court, asking for reinstatement or compensation.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Signing a "voluntary resignation" under pressure
- Not asking for the written grounds
- Missing the appeal deadline
- Working without a written contract

Our services:
- Challenging unfair dismissal and reinstatement
- Recovery of unpaid salary and compensation
- Protection from discrimination and harassment at work
- Employment contracts and internal regulations
- Collective disputes and negotiations
- Compliance advice for employers

### What can I do if I was dismissed unlawfully?
You can ask your employer for the written grounds of dismissal and challenge it in court, seeking reinstatement or compensation. Deadlines are short (as a rule, 30 calendar days), so contact a lawyer immediately.

### Is an oral employment contract valid?
An oral contract is possible, but a contract concluded for more than one month must be in writing.

### Do you represent employees or employers?
Both. We help employees restore their rights, and help employers prevent disputes and represent them in court.

## Corporate lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/corporate-lawyer/

Strategic legal support for businesses in Georgia — from company registration to mergers and acquisitions, compliance and restructuring.

Corporate law covers every stage from company formation to restructuring. MMLAW helps businesses minimise legal risk and stay compliant.
We work with Georgian and foreign companies and investors — in Georgian, English and Russian.

A corporate lawyer helps you set up a company, draft the charter and shareholder agreement, prepare and review contracts and reduce your business's legal risks.

1. Choose the legal form and company name.
2. Prepare the charter and, if needed, a shareholder agreement.
3. Secure a legal address in Georgia.
4. Register the company with the Public Registry — it is registered as a taxpayer at the same time.
5. Open a bank account.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Working without an agreement between partners
- Leaving share transfers and exit rules out of the charter
- Mixing personal and company money
- Choosing the wrong tax regime
- Signing contracts without legal review

- Shareholder agreements and corporate governance

### How long does it take to register a company in Georgia?
With properly prepared documents, registering an LLC with the National Agency of Public Registry usually takes one business day.

### Can a foreigner own 100% of a Georgian company?
Yes. Foreign individuals and companies can be the sole founders of a Georgian LLC.

### Which law governs companies in Georgia?
The Law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs (new version in force since 2022).

## Real estate lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/real-estate-lawyer/

Full legal support for real estate in Georgia — checking the property, structuring and signing the deal, registering ownership and resolving disputes.

Legal support in real estate is critically important. MMLAW offers a full service — from purchase agreements to construction permits.
A lawyer's check before the deal costs far less than fixing a disputed transaction afterwards.

### What a real estate lawyer does

A real estate lawyer checks the property and the seller, drafts and reviews contracts, completes the transaction and registration with the Public Registry, and represents you in court if a dispute arises.

### Buying property, step by step

1. Get a Public Registry extract — check the owner, mortgage, seizures and prohibitions.
2. Check the seller's authority and, for new builds, the developer and permits.
3. If needed, sign a preliminary agreement with clear terms on the deposit.
4. Sign the sale contract and pay through a safe channel.
5. Register ownership with the Public Registry.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Paying a deposit before checking the property
- Trusting a developer without checking permits
- Paying cash without proof of payment
- Not checking utility and other debts
- Signing a contract in a language you don't understand

Our services:
- Legal due diligence of property
- Purchase, lease and mortgage agreements
- Registration with the Public Registry
- Construction permits
- Property disputes and eviction
- Advice for foreign buyers

### Where is property ownership registered?
At the National Agency of Public Registry (NAPR). Ownership of real estate arises upon registration. A registry extract shows the owner and any encumbrances (mortgage, seizure).

### Can foreigners buy property in Georgia?
Yes. Foreigners can freely buy apartments, houses and non-agricultural land. Purchase of agricultural land by foreigners is restricted by law.

### What should I check before buying?
The registry extract (owner, mortgage, seizure, prohibitions), the seller's authority, permits for new construction, and any utility or other debts.

## Family and divorce lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/family-lawyer/

Discreet, professional representation in divorce, child residence, alimony and division of marital property in Georgia.

Family law is an emotionally difficult field. MMLAW attorneys protect your and your family's interests in divorce, custody and property division cases with sensitivity and professionalism.
Where possible, we work towards agreement — the least painful path for children and for both parties.

### What a family lawyer does

A family lawyer helps with divorce, child residence and alimony, and dividing marital property. We try to reach an agreement first — if that isn't possible, we represent you in court.

### When you need a family lawyer

- Your spouse doesn't agree to the divorce
- You can't agree where the child will live or how the other parent will see them
- You need alimony set, increased or reduced
- Property acquired during the marriage has to be divided
- You want to sign a marriage contract
- Paternity needs to be established

### Divorce in Georgia: two routes

If both spouses agree and there is no dispute about children or property, the divorce can be registered at the Public Service Hall. If one spouse disagrees or there is a dispute, the court decides.

### Documents to prepare

- ID documents of both spouses
- Marriage certificate
- Children's birth certificates
- Property documents (registry extracts, contracts)
- Proof of income — for alimony

### Mistakes to avoid

- Relying on a verbal agreement — it should be put in writing
- Selling joint property while the dispute is ongoing
- Drawing the child into the dispute
- Taking the child abroad without the other parent's consent
- Ignoring court notices

Our services:
- Divorce by agreement or through court
- Child residence and contact arrangements
- Alimony (child support)
- Division of marital property
- Marriage (prenuptial) contracts
- Adoption and guardianship

### Can we divorce without going to court?
Yes — if both spouses agree and there is no dispute over children or property, the divorce can be registered with the Civil Registry (through the Public Service Hall). Otherwise the divorce is decided by a court.

### How is property divided?
Property acquired during the marriage is the spouses' joint property and is, as a rule, divided equally unless a marriage contract says otherwise. Property owned before marriage, gifts and inheritance remain personal property.

### How is alimony determined?
Parents must support their minor children. The amount depends on the child's needs and the parents' financial situation — set by agreement or by the court.

## Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/inheritance-lawyer/

We help you accept an inheritance in Georgia, obtain the certificate of inheritance and register the property in your name — and represent you in disputes between heirs.

You can inherit under a will or by law. When there is no will, the first-line heirs are the deceased's children, spouse and parents; if there are none, the inheritance passes to the next lines.
An inheritance must be accepted within 6 months of its opening — by applying to a notary or by actually taking possession of the property. The notary then issues a certificate of inheritance, on the basis of which the property is registered in your name with the Public Registry.

### What an inheritance lawyer does

An inheritance lawyer helps you accept the inheritance on time, gather the documents, obtain the certificate of inheritance and register the property in your name. If the heirs can't agree, we represent you in court.

### When you need an inheritance lawyer

- A family member has died and left property
- The heirs can't agree how to divide the property
- You consider the will unfair
- You missed the 6-month deadline
- You live abroad and can't come to Georgia
- The property isn't registered with the Public Registry

### Accepting an inheritance, step by step

1. Gather the documents — death certificate, proof of kinship and property documents.
2. Within 6 months, apply to a notary to accept the inheritance (or actually take possession of the property).
3. The notary issues a certificate of inheritance.
4. With the certificate, the property is registered in your name with the Public Registry.

### Documents you'll need

- Death certificate
- Your ID document
- Proof of kinship (birth and marriage certificates)
- Property documents or a Public Registry extract
- The will, if there is one

### Mistakes to avoid

- Missing the 6-month deadline
- Accepting the inheritance without checking the deceased's debts
- Relying on a verbal agreement with the other heirs
- Trying to sell the property before getting the certificate of inheritance
- Putting off old, unregistered property

Our services:
- Accepting an inheritance and the certificate of inheritance
- Registering the property in the heir's name
- Drafting and challenging wills
- Disputes between heirs and division of shares
- Restoring a missed 6-month deadline
- Accepting an inheritance from abroad by power of attorney

### How long do I have to accept an inheritance?
6 months from the opening of the inheritance — as a rule, the date of death. You can accept it by applying to a notary or by actually taking possession of the property.

### Who are the first-line heirs?
The deceased's children (including adopted children), spouse and parents. They inherit in equal shares unless a will provides otherwise.

### What if I missed the 6-month deadline?
If you missed it for a valid reason, a court can extend it. Whether you actually took possession of the property also matters. We'll assess your case.

### Can a will be challenged?
Yes — for example if the will's form was not respected or the testator was not aware of their actions when making it. Certain close relatives may also be entitled to a compulsory share regardless of the will.

### Am I liable for the deceased's debts?
As a rule, an heir is liable for debts only up to the value of the property inherited. It's worth checking the debts before accepting — if needed, you can renounce the inheritance.

### Is there inheritance tax in Georgia?
There is no separate inheritance tax. First- and second-order heirs — children, spouse, parents, siblings — pay no tax on property received by inheritance or gift. Third- and fourth-order heirs (grandparents, uncles, aunts) are exempt up to GEL 150,000 a year. Otherwise the value is taxed as income at 20%.

## Intellectual property lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/intellectual-property-lawyer/

We protect brands, creative works and inventions — from registration with Sakpatenti to disputes with infringers.

Intellectual property protection is fundamental to modern business. MMLAW offers trademark registration, copyright protection and patent consultation.
Registering your brand early is the cheapest way to avoid disputes later.

### What an IP lawyer does

An intellectual property lawyer helps you search and register trademarks, protect copyright, draft licence agreements and take action against infringers.

### Registering a trademark, step by step

1. Check that no similar mark is already registered.
2. Choose the classes of goods and services.
3. File the application with Sakpatenti.
4. Go through examination and obtain registration.
5. Monitor the market and renew the registration on time.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Using a brand without checking it first
- Registering only the domain, not the trademark
- Having no written agreement transferring rights from your designer or developer
- Missing the renewal deadline

Our services:
- Trademark search and registration
- Copyright protection and licensing
- Patents and designs (consultation)
- Licence and IP agreements
- Infringement disputes
- Brand and domain protection online

### Where are trademarks registered in Georgia?
With Sakpatenti — the National Intellectual Property Center of Georgia. International registration is possible through the Madrid system.

### How long does trademark protection last?
10 years from the filing date, renewable every 10 years.

### Does copyright need to be registered?
No — copyright arises automatically when a work is created. Depositing the work with Sakpatenti helps prove authorship.

## Fraud lawyer in Georgia — defence and recovery
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/fraud-lawyer/

In fraud cases we defend the accused and help victims get their money back — investment schemes, loans, online and crypto fraud, and business deals.

Fraud is taking someone else's property or obtaining a property right by deception, in order to keep it (Article 180 of the Criminal Code). The key question is whether there was intent to deceive from the start — if an obligation simply wasn't met, it is often a civil dispute.
Since 2025, a person convicted of large-scale fraud is ordered to pay the victim compensation and is banned from leaving Georgia until the damage is paid. That gives victims a real chance of getting their money back.

### Penalties under Article 180

- Basic offence — a fine, community service, corrective labour, house arrest, or 2 to 4 years in prison
- By a group by prior agreement, or causing significant damage (over GEL 150) — a fine or 4 to 7 years
- By abusing one's position, on a large scale (over GEL 10,000) or repeatedly — a fine or 6 to 9 years
- By an organised group or by a person convicted twice or more — 7 to 10 years

Our services:
- Defence against fraud charges
- Representing victims and recovering money
- Investment and pyramid scheme cases
- Loan and business-deal fraud cases
- Online and crypto fraud cases
- Assessing whether it is a crime or a civil dispute

### Is failing to repay a debt fraud?
Not necessarily. Fraud requires intent to deceive from the start. If an obligation simply wasn't met, it is often a civil dispute.

### I was scammed — can I get my money back?
The earlier you act, the better the chances: a police report, freezing the suspect's property and the compensation mechanism. In large-scale cases the convicted person is ordered to pay compensation.

### What is the penalty for fraud?
For the basic offence — from a fine up to 4 years in prison; with aggravating circumstances — up to 10 years.

## Victims of financial crime — getting the money back
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/financial-crime-victims/

Since 2025, victims of fraud, extortion, embezzlement and other financial crimes have a new, effective way to recover their losses. We use it for you — from the investigation to the money in your account.

In September 2025 a victim compensation procedure was added to the Criminal Procedure Code (Articles 165³–165⁸). A guilty verdict orders the convicted person to pay compensation if they are convicted of, for example, large-scale fraud, extortion or embezzlement, property damage over GEL 10,000, abuse of authority in a company or computer crime — and the victim has not waived compensation in writing.
Compensation is paid first from the convicted person's own property, then from property they gave to relatives or others for free or cheaply. The property is frozen, and the convicted person — a Georgian citizen or a person with status in Georgia — is banned from leaving the country until they pay or the victim waives it. Giving the convicted person benefits above the legal limit is itself a crime.

Our services:
- Victim status and representation
- Tracing property and requesting a freeze
- Claiming compensation in the verdict
- Requesting an exit ban for the convicted person
- A civil claim for the remaining loss
- Recovering property passed to relatives

### Which crimes does compensation cover?
For example: large-scale fraud, extortion and embezzlement, property damage over GEL 10,000, abuse of authority in a company and large-scale computer crime.

### What if the convicted person leaves the country?
If they are a Georgian citizen or a person with status in Georgia, they are banned from leaving until compensation is paid — unless you waive it in writing.

### Can I also file a civil claim?
Yes. Compensation doesn't take away your right to a civil claim — you just can't claim again the part you already received.

## Tax lawyer in Georgia — disputes and tax crimes
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/tax-lawyer/

We represent you before the Revenue Service — during audits, when appealing a tax demand, when reducing tax debt and, if needed, in a criminal tax evasion case.

A tax dispute has two stages: the complaint goes first to the Revenue Service, then to the Dispute Resolution Council at the Ministry of Finance or to court. The deadline to appeal is 30 days from receiving the decision — missing it almost rules out a dispute.
Intentional tax evasion is a crime if the amount exceeds GEL 100,000 (Article 218). But there is no criminal liability if, within 45 working days of receiving the tax demand, the principal amount is paid, deferred or adjusted — so timing is decisive.

### Penalties under Article 218

- Over GEL 100,000 — a fine or 3 to 5 years in prison
- Over GEL 150,000, repeatedly or as a group — 5 to 8 years
- Selling off property to evade tax — a fine or 2 to 3 years

Our services:
- Support during tax audits
- Appealing tax demands
- Disputes at the Revenue Service, the Council and in court
- Tax settlements — reducing tax debt
- Appealing fines and late-payment interest
- Defence in tax evasion cases

### How long do I have to appeal a tax decision?
30 days from receiving it. Complaints are usually filed electronically.

### Can tax debt be reduced?
Yes, in cases set by law a tax settlement can be signed with the Revenue Service to reduce part of the debt.

### Is any tax debt a crime?
No. The crime is intentional evasion of more than GEL 100,000. Even then there is no liability if within 45 working days the amount is paid, deferred or adjusted.

## Money laundering defence lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/money-laundering-lawyer/

A money laundering case often starts with a bank report or a frozen account. We defend individuals and companies — from proving the lawful origin of assets to the courtroom.

Money laundering (legalising illegal income) is giving illegal or unexplained property a lawful appearance in order to hide its origin (Article 194). Unexplained property is property for which there are no documents showing it was lawfully obtained — so documents and financial history decide these cases.
During an investigation a court can freeze property and bank accounts if there is information that the property may be hidden or was obtained through crime. A freeze can be challenged — and that is often the first step.

### Penalties under Article 194

- Basic offence — a fine or 3 to 6 years in prison
- As a group, repeatedly or on a large scale (GEL 30,000–50,000) — 6 to 9 years
- By an organised group, by abusing one's position or on an especially large scale (over GEL 50,000) — 9 to 12 years

Our services:
- Defence against money laundering charges
- Challenging freezes on accounts and property
- Proving the lawful origin of assets
- Help when a bank suspends a transaction
- Defending companies and internal reviews
- Reviewing financial expert reports

### My bank suspended a transaction — what should I do?
Ask for a written explanation and prepare documents proving where the money came from. If it reaches an investigation, involve a lawyer straight away.

### What is unexplained property?
Property for which the person or their relatives have no documents proving it was lawfully obtained.

### What is the penalty for money laundering?
For the basic offence — a fine or 3 to 6 years; on an especially large scale or by an organised group — up to 12 years.

### Is 'renting out' my account or card risky?
Yes. If someone else's money comes into your account and you transfer or withdraw it, you may end up accused as a participant in fraud or of money laundering — even if you only took a 'small fee'.

## Asset freezing and confiscation lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/asset-freezing-and-confiscation/

When the state freezes property or a bank account, or seeks confiscation, both business and family life stop at once. We challenge freezes, protect third parties' property and prove the lawful origin of assets.

In a criminal case a court can freeze the property of the accused or a connected person, including bank accounts, if there is information that the property may be hidden or spent, or was obtained through crime (Article 151 of the Criminal Procedure Code). A verdict can confiscate the object and instrument of the crime and property obtained through crime (Article 52 of the Criminal Code).
There is a separate civil procedure: certain people — for example, public officials or persons convicted of money laundering — and their connected persons can have unlawful and unexplained property confiscated. In these cases documents proving where the property came from are decisive.

Our services:
- Challenging freezes on property and accounts
- Protecting the property of third parties — family members, companies
- Proving the lawful origin of assets
- Defence against confiscation in a verdict
- Unlawful and unexplained property cases
- Requesting a freeze to secure the victim's compensation

### My account has been frozen — what should I do?
Find out in which case and on what grounds. The court order can be appealed — contact a lawyer straight away.

### Can a family member's property be frozen?
It can, if they are treated as a person connected to the accused. Then it is important to prove the property was obtained lawfully and independently.

### What is the difference between a freeze and confiscation?
A freeze is temporary — it restricts dealing with the property. Confiscation is final: the property passes to the state.

## Abuse of office and exceeding authority — lawyer
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/abuse-of-office-lawyer/

We defend public officials, employees of public legal entities and company managers charged with abuse of official authority, exceeding authority or negligence.

Abuse of official authority (Article 332) and exceeding authority (Article 333) by an official are crimes if they cause a substantial breach of a person's, society's or the state's lawful interests. For private company managers, Article 220 — abuse of authority in a company — and Article 220¹, negligence, apply.
In these cases it often comes down to what powers the person had, who made the decision, whether there was an aim of gain, and how 'substantial' the breach was. Many mistakes are administrative or disciplinary matters, not crimes.

### Penalties

- Articles 332 and 333, basic offence — a fine, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or up to 3 years in prison, with a ban on holding office for up to 3 years
- By a holder of a political state office — a fine or 3 to 5 years
- Repeatedly, with violence or a weapon, or insulting the victim's dignity — 5 to 8 years
- Article 220 (in a company, causing significant damage) — a fine, corrective labour, house arrest or 3 to 5 years

Our services:
- Defence against abuse-of-authority charges
- Defence against exceeding-authority charges
- Defending company managers under Article 220
- Defence against negligence charges
- Public procurement cases
- Reviewing covert investigative actions

### Who counts as an official?
Public servants and persons treated as such, including employees of public legal entities who exercise public authority.

### Can a private company director be liable?
Not under Article 332, but possibly under Article 220 — if they used their authority against the company's interests for gain and caused significant damage.

### Is every mistake at work a crime?
No. There must be a substantial breach of rights or interests, and for abuse of authority also an aim of gain or advantage.

## Smuggling and customs offences — lawyer in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/smuggling-and-customs-lawyer/

We defend individuals and companies in cases of breaking the rules for moving goods across Georgia's customs border — from ordinary goods to jewellery and cultural heritage.

Moving a large amount of goods across the customs border past customs control, secretly, with a false document or with false data in the customs declaration is a crime (Article 214). A large amount means a customs value over GEL 15,000, an especially large amount over GEL 25,000; for goods hidden in a cache or brought by crossing the border illegally, the thresholds are GEL 5,000 and GEL 15,000.
So in these cases the key is often the correct customs valuation of the goods: below the threshold, the act is usually no longer a crime.

### Penalties under Article 214

- Large amount — a fine or 3 to 5 years in prison
- Especially large amount — a fine or 5 to 7 years
- Cultural heritage, precious-metal jewellery — a fine or 4 to 7 years
- Weapons, explosives or other dangerous substances — 5 to 8 years
- Repeatedly, by an official, with violence or as a group — 8 to 11 years; by an organised group — 11 to 15 years

Our services:
- Defence against smuggling charges
- Checking the customs valuation
- False declaration cases
- Getting seized goods and vehicles back
- Cases involving jewellery and cultural heritage
- Customs disputes for companies

### Is every customs violation a crime?
No. Criminal liability requires a large amount — a customs value over GEL 15,000 (over GEL 5,000 for goods in a cache). Smaller violations are usually dealt with in a different way.

### I forgot to declare gold jewellery — what happens?
Moving precious-metal jewellery in breach of the rules is punished under a separate part of Article 214. The circumstances matter a lot — contact a lawyer straight away.

### What is the penalty for smuggling?
For a large amount — a fine or 3 to 5 years; with aggravating circumstances — up to 15 years.

## Director liability and company insolvency in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/director-liability-and-insolvency/

We defend company directors and partners — when the company is in debt, facing insolvency, or when a manager faces civil or criminal liability. We also protect creditors.

A director must manage the company's affairs in good faith and with reasonable care. If they breach this duty, they can be liable to the company for the damage, and in serious cases also criminally — for example, for abuse of authority in a company (Article 220), tax evasion or embezzlement.
When a company can no longer pay its debts, insolvency proceedings can be both a way out — rehabilitation — and a risk. A timely legal assessment protects both the manager and the creditor.

Our services:
- Assessing director and partner liability
- Disputes between the company and its director
- Insolvency: rehabilitation or liquidation
- Creditors' claims and their protection
- Criminal defence (Articles 220, 218, 182)
- Company liquidation and obligations

### Is a director personally liable for an LLC's debts?
Generally no — the company is liable with its own assets. But a director can be liable if they breached their duties and caused damage, or if a crime is established.

### The company can't pay its debts — what should I do?
Assess the situation with a lawyer as early as possible: rehabilitation or an agreement with creditors may be better than liquidation.

### I'm a creditor — how do I protect my claim?
Register the claim in the insolvency case on time and, if needed, ask the court for interim measures.

## Drug possession lawyer in Georgia — Article 260
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/drug-possession-lawyer/

Buying or keeping drugs is the most common drug case in Georgia (the country). Everything turns on the quantity, the lab report and whether the search was lawful — even a fraction of a gram changes the part of the article and the sentence.

Unlawfully buying or keeping a narcotic drug is punished under Article 260 of the Criminal Code of Georgia — if the amount exceeds the small amount. Buying, keeping or using a small amount is usually an administrative offence; repeating it becomes a crime under Article 273.
The amounts are set in an annex to the law and are counted as the pure substance — without fillers such as flour, sugar or medicine. That is why checking the lab report is often the core of the defence.

### Penalties under Article 260

- Part 1 — buying or keeping more than a small amount: up to 6 years in prison
- Part 2 — a large amount, as a group, by abusing one's position, repeatedly, or by a person convicted of a drug crime: 5 to 8 years
- Part 3 — an especially large amount or by an organised group: 8 to 20 years or life imprisonment

### Small amounts and personal use

- Buying, keeping or using a small amount (other than marijuana) — a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or up to 60 days of administrative detention
- Buying or keeping a small amount of marijuana — a GEL 500 fine
- The same after an administrative penalty or conviction — Article 273: a fine, community service or up to 1 year in prison
- Refusing a drug test — a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or up to 60 days of administrative detention

### Quantity thresholds (grams)

More than the small amount, up to and including the large amount, is the starting point for criminal liability (Article 260, Part 1). For example, more than 5 grams of dried marijuana is already a criminal case.

| Substance | Small (grams, up to and including) | Large — more than | Especially large — more than |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marijuana (dried) | 5 | 70 | 250 |
| Hashish (cannabis resin) | 0,05 | 0,5 | 5 |
| Cocaine | 0,06 | 0,6 | 2 |
| Heroin | 0,005 | 0,2 | 0,5 |
| Methadone | 0,005 | 0,2 | 1 |
| Buprenorphine (Subutex) | 0,0012 | 0,012 | 0,03 |
| Amphetamine | 0,005 | 0,1 | 1 |
| Methamphetamine | 0,005 | 0,1 | 1 |
| MDMA (ecstasy) | 0,05 | 0,5 | 1 |
| Mephedrone | 0,01 | 0,1 | 1 |
| Alpha-PVP | 0,001 | 0,2 | 1 |
| LSD | 0,00002 | 0,0002 | 0,001 |

Amounts are counted without fillers. The full list is in Annex 2 to the Law on Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances, Precursors and Narcological Assistance.

### Voluntary surrender

A person who voluntarily hands over the substance is released from criminal liability if there is no other crime in their conduct. It only counts as voluntary if it is reported before an investigation starts and the person actively helps with the seizure.

Our services:
- Defence against Article 260 charges
- Checking the lab report and the quantity
- Lawfulness of the search and seizure
- Preventive measure — bail instead of detention
- Administrative cases and appealing fines
- Assessing a plea agreement

### How many grams of marijuana is a crime in Georgia?
Up to and including 5 grams of dried marijuana is a small amount — a GEL 500 administrative fine. More than 5 grams is already a criminal case under Article 260; over 70 grams is a large amount, over 250 grams especially large.

### What is the penalty under Article 260, Part 1?
Up to 6 years in prison. Part 2 — 5 to 8 years; Part 3 — 8 to 20 years or life.

### Is the quantity counted with packaging or fillers?
No. By law the quantity is the pure substance, without fillers. That is why checking the lab report matters so much.

## Removing a criminal record in Georgia — lawyer
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/criminal-record-removal/

A criminal record gets in the way of jobs, visas, emigration and much more. By law it expires after a set period, and if you have behaved impeccably since serving your sentence, a court can remove it even earlier.

Under Article 79 of the Criminal Code, a person has a criminal record from the day the guilty verdict enters into force until the record expires or is removed. An expired or removed record is no longer taken into account. A person released from punishment is considered to have no criminal record (Article 79(2)).
Before the period ends, a court decides on removal at your request if you have behaved impeccably since serving the sentence. We prepare the application and the evidence — work, family, references — and represent you in court.

### When a criminal record expires

- Suspended sentence — when the probation period ends
- A sentence lighter than imprisonment — 1 year after serving it
- Imprisonment for a less serious crime — 3 years after serving it
- Imprisonment for a serious crime — 6 years after serving it
- Imprisonment for an especially serious crime — 8 years after serving it

A less serious crime is one punishable by no more than 5 years in prison; a serious crime is an intentional crime punishable by no more than 10 years (a negligent one — by more than 5 years); an especially serious crime is an intentional crime punishable by more than 10 years or life (Article 12). If you were released early or your sentence was replaced with a lighter one, the period runs from the sentence actually served or from serving the lighter sentence.

Our services:
- Calculating the expiry date in your case
- Application for early removal of the record
- Evidence of impeccable conduct
- Representation in court
- Advice on visas, jobs and emigration
- Appealing a refusal

### How do I get a criminal record certificate?
The certificate is issued by the MIA Service Agency — online on its website or app, or at a branch; GEL 20, 3 working days. For use abroad it usually needs an apostille. If the certificate still shows a conviction, we check whether it has expired and whether it can be removed early.

### When will my criminal record expire?
It depends on the sentence and the category of crime: for a suspended sentence — after the probation period; for a sentence lighter than imprisonment — 1 year after serving it; for imprisonment — 3, 6 or 8 years after serving it.

### Can a criminal record be removed early?
Yes. If you have behaved impeccably since serving the sentence, a court can remove the record at your request before the period ends.

### What does a removed record mean?
An expired or removed record is no longer taken into account — for example, when a new case is classified or a sentence is set.

## Early release on parole in Georgia — lawyer
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/early-release-on-parole/

A person sentenced to imprisonment can be released early on parole if they have served the required part of the sentence and it is found that serving the full term is no longer needed for their rehabilitation. We help prisoners and their families prepare the application and the evidence.

Under Article 72 of the Criminal Code, early release from a fixed-term prison sentence is decided by the local board of the Special Penitentiary Service; for community service, corrective labour or house arrest — by a court. The rule does not apply to prisoners held in a special-risk facility.
A released person can be given obligations, and the probation bureau supervises their conduct. If they persistently fail to meet them or commit a new crime, the release can be revoked.

### How much must be served

- Less serious crime — at least half of the sentence
- Serious crime — at least two-thirds
- Especially serious crime — at least three-quarters
- If an earlier parole was revoked — three-quarters
- In every case at least 6 months must actually be served

### What helps a positive decision

- Conduct in the facility and no disciplinary breaches
- Study, work, rehabilitation programmes
- Compensating the victim
- A home and a job to go to after release

Our services:
- Calculating when you can apply
- Preparing the application and the evidence
- Representation before the board or the court
- Replacing the rest of the sentence with a lighter one
- Appealing a refusal
- Advice for the family

### When is early release possible?
For a less serious crime — after half of the sentence, for a serious crime — two-thirds, for an especially serious crime — three-quarters. In every case at least 6 months must be served.

### Who decides?
For imprisonment — the local board of the Special Penitentiary Service; for other sentences — a court.

### Can the family hire a lawyer?
Yes. A family member can contact us; we meet the prisoner and prepare the case.

## Pyramid schemes and investment fraud in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/pyramid-schemes-investment-fraud/

Pyramid schemes and fake investment platforms always work the same way: promised high returns are paid with new participants' money until the scheme collapses. We help victims get their money back and defend people accused of taking part.

These schemes are usually charged as fraud (Article 180), and the money flows can also amount to money laundering (Article 194). Since 2025, a person convicted of large-scale fraud is ordered to pay the victim compensation and cannot leave Georgia until they pay.
Participants face risk too: anyone who recruited others or collected money can end up accused. The key question is whether they knew the scheme was a deception.

### Signs that a scheme is a pyramid

- Guaranteed or unusually high returns
- Bonuses for bringing in new participants
- No licence, office or transparent reporting
- Withdrawals get difficult or a 'fee' is demanded
- Pressure — 'time is running out', 'limited places'

### If you lost money

1. Don't send more money — including a 'fee' to withdraw your funds.
2. Keep everything: contracts, messages, the website address, transfer receipts.
3. Contact your bank about the transfer.
4. With a lawyer, file a report and request a freeze on the suspects' property.

Our services:
- Representing victims and recovering money
- Tracing and freezing property
- Compensation in the verdict and civil claims
- Defence for those accused of organising or taking part
- Crypto and forex platform cases
- Group cases — several victims

### I lost money in a pyramid scheme — can I get it back?
The earlier you act, the better the chances: a report, a freeze on property and the compensation mechanism. In large-scale fraud the convicted person is ordered to pay compensation.

### I brought friends into the scheme — am I liable?
If you didn't know the scheme was a deception, that is the core of your defence. Talk to a lawyer before giving a statement to investigators.

### The platform is abroad — what can be done?
A case can be opened in Georgia if the victim or the recipient of the money is here; international cooperation is used where needed. Contacting your bank quickly matters too.

## Blackmail with private photos in Georgia — lawyer
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blackmail-private-photos/

Blackmail with private photos or information is one of the hardest situations — people often tell no one out of shame. The law is strict here: demanding money is extortion, and spreading intimate images violates the secret of private life, with up to 10 years in prison. We act fast and in confidence.

Several crimes can be involved at once: extortion (Article 181) if money or property is demanded; violation of the secret of private life (Article 157¹); spreading personal data (Article 157); secretly recording a private conversation (Article 158).
The victim needs three things: the blackmail to stop, the content removed, and the offender held responsible. We prepare the report, work with investigators, use platforms' takedown tools and claim compensation for moral damage.

### What to do right now

1. Don't pay — paying rarely stops blackmail.
2. Don't delete the messages; take dated screenshots with the profile link.
3. Stop communicating with the offender.
4. Contact a lawyer and the police — the sooner, the better.

Our services:
- Report and representation of the victim
- Removing content from platforms
- Compensation for moral damage
- Extortion, Article 157 and 157¹ cases
- Personal data complaints
- Complete confidentiality

### If I pay, will they stop?
Often not. Paying shows the pressure works, and demands grow. It is better to keep the evidence and contact a lawyer and the police.

### The photo has already been posted — can it be removed?
Yes. We use platforms' takedown tools and, where needed, legal routes — while the criminal case continues.

### Will my name appear anywhere?
We work in complete confidence. There are also ways to protect a victim's private life during the investigation and in court — your lawyer will ask for them.

## Time-barred loans in Georgia: limitation period and defence
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/time-barred-loans/

An old loan — from a bank, a microfinance company or a private person — becomes time-barred after a period set by law. But nothing disappears automatically: the debtor must raise the time bar, and even one 'small' payment restarts the clock.

Under Article 129 of the Civil Code, the limitation period for contractual claims — including loans — is 3 years, and 6 years for contracts concerning real estate. For periodic (e.g. monthly) payments it is 3 years, counted separately for each payment. The period starts when the creditor learned or should have learned of the breach — for a loan, usually from the missed payment date.
Once the period has expired, the debtor may refuse to pay (Article 144). But the court does not check the time bar on its own — if you don't raise it when sued, the court may order you to pay even a time-barred debt. And if you pay after the period has expired, you cannot ask for the money back.

### What restarts the period

- Acknowledging the debt — paying part of it or interest, a guarantee, a letter or signature acknowledging it (Article 137)
- The creditor suing, applying to a state body, or taking an enforcement step (Article 138)
