- After an interruption the period starts again — time already passed no longer counts (Article 141)

### Court decisions and enforcement

If the debt has already been confirmed by a court decision that has entered into force, the limitation period for the claim is 10 years — even if the loan's own period was 3 years (Article 142).

There is a limit at the enforcement stage too: enforcement proceedings for a money claim end 10 years after they began — except in cases set by law, such as alimony (Law on Enforcement Proceedings, Article 34).

### If a collector calls you

- Don't pay a 'token' amount or sign an acknowledgment of the debt until you have checked the period with a lawyer
- Ask in writing: whose claim it is, on what basis it was transferred and when the last payment was made
- Keep records of calls and messages

Our services:
- Calculating the limitation period in your case
- Raising the time bar in court
- Defence when sued by a bank, microfinance company or collector
- Challenging a decision made in your absence
- Enforcement and debtors' register issues
- Negotiating with the creditor

### How long until a loan is time-barred?
The limitation period for a loan claim is 3 years, 6 years for contracts concerning real estate. If a court has already confirmed the debt — 10 years.

### Is a time-barred loan cancelled automatically?
No. After the period expires the debtor may refuse to pay, but must raise it in court themselves. The court does not apply the time bar on its own initiative.

### A collector asked me to pay a small amount — what should I do?
Check the period before you pay. Paying part of the debt or interest, or acknowledging it, restarts the limitation period.

### Does a time-barred loan stay in my credit history?
According to the National Bank's financial education portal, a time-barred debt stays in the credit history for 5 years, after which you can ask for it to be removed.

## Restraining and protective orders in Georgia — lawyer
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/restraining-protective-orders/

Restraining and protective orders are the main tools against domestic violence and violence against women in Georgia. We help victims obtain an order and defend the person it was issued against — through an appeal, cancellation, or when accused of a breach.

A restraining order is issued by the police for up to 1 month and takes effect immediately. A protective order is issued by a court for up to 9 months; if the threat continues, it can be extended by no more than 3 months. An order can bar the abuser from the shared home, from approaching the victim, or from using weapons, or impose electronic monitoring.
An order can be requested by the victim, a family member, or — with the victim's consent — a social worker or someone helping the victim. The police can also issue a restraining order on their own initiative. Breaching an order is a crime (Article 381¹).

### The key rules

- Restraining order — police, up to 1 month; it can be appealed within 3 days of receipt
- Protective order — court, up to 9 months; extension — no more than 3 months more
- After reconciliation an order can be cancelled on a joint application — if there is no longer a threat
- A protective order requires the abuser to take a mandatory training course

### Breaching an order — Article 381¹

- Breaching an order or evading electronic monitoring — a fine, 180–240 hours of community service, or up to 1 year in prison
- Repeatedly — 1 to 3 years in prison

Our services:
- Requesting a restraining or protective order
- Appealing an order within 3 days
- Cancelling an order or changing its term
- Defence against a breach charge (381¹)
- Housing, contact with children and weapons issues
- Representing the victim in the criminal case

### How long does a restraining order last?
Up to 1 month. A protective order is issued by a court for up to 9 months and can be extended by 3 more.

### Can a restraining order be appealed?
Yes. Both the victim and the person it was issued against can appeal within 3 days of receiving it. The deadline is very short — contact a lawyer immediately.

### What happens if an order is breached?
Breaching an order is a crime: a fine, community service or up to 1 year in prison; repeatedly — 1 to 3 years.

### Is the order cancelled after reconciliation?
Not automatically. It can be cancelled on a joint application if the victim or other family members are no longer at risk.

## Removing a seizure on bank accounts and property in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/removing-seizure-on-account/

A seizure on an account or property often appears out of nowhere — because of an old debt, a court decision or a fine. We find out what it is based on and the fastest way to lift it.

A seizure is usually imposed in enforcement proceedings — to enforce a court decision, a notary's writ or a fine. How to lift it depends on its basis and how long ago enforcement started.
Enforcement ends — and every measure, including the seizure, is cancelled — if, for example, the creditor waives it, the parties settle, the decision is quashed, or 10 years have passed since enforcement proceedings for a money claim began (5 years for fines). By law the 10-year rule does not apply to, for example, alimony, employment claims, damage caused by a crime, or cases in favour of the state budget.

### What cannot be seized

- Targeted state assistance
- Income below the subsistence minimum
- Personal and household items needed for daily life and professional work
- Property of a member of a family registered as socially vulnerable — within the limit set by law

Disputes over whether property or income is protected from seizure are decided by a court.

### How we challenge it

1. An enforcement officer's action can be appealed to the head of the National Bureau of Enforcement within 15 calendar days.
2. If needed — in court.
3. At the same time — negotiating with the creditor: a payment plan or settlement, which ends enforcement.

### Tax collection orders („inkaso“)

If the Revenue Service is taking money from your account, it is usually a collection order. Under Article 243 of the Tax Code, it is sent to the bank for a confirmed tax debt — tax, interest and fines; it does not apply to term deposit accounts. The decision is sent to the person electronically.

If you disagree with the debt and appeal, the obligation to pay is suspended while the dispute lasts (Article 254). A freeze can be lifted with a bank guarantee, a surety or a mortgage, and if the dispute ends in your favour, every measure is cancelled.

Our services:
- Checking the basis of the seizure and the enforcement case
- Appealing an enforcement officer's action within 15 days
- Releasing protected income and property
- Ending enforcement after the 10-year limit
- Settlement and payment plans with the creditor
- Releasing a third party's property from seizure

### My account was seized — how do I find out why?
A seizure is imposed within an enforcement case. We can check the case, the creditor and the amount, and tell you the fastest way to lift it.

### The tax office put an „inkaso“ on my account — what does it mean?
It is a collection order: the Revenue Service takes the amount of a confirmed tax debt from your account. If you disagree with the debt, you can appeal — while the dispute lasts, the obligation to pay is suspended.

### Can my salary be seized too?
By law money can be collected from salary and other income, but income below the subsistence minimum and targeted state assistance are protected from seizure.

### A seizure from an old case is still active — what can I do?
If 10 years have passed since enforcement proceedings for a money claim began, enforcement must end and the seizure be lifted — except in cases set by law, such as alimony.

### How long do I have to appeal an enforcement officer's action?
15 calendar days from the action — to the head of the National Bureau of Enforcement.

## Presidential pardon and amnesty in Georgia — how to apply
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/pardon-and-amnesty/

A pardon and an amnesty are two different ways of being fully or partly released from a sentence. We help convicted people and their families find out which applies to them and prepare the request.

A pardon is an individual act: under the Constitution, convicted persons are pardoned by the President of Georgia. Requests are first reviewed by the Pardon Commission, and the President makes the final decision. The criteria and procedure are set by the President and change from time to time.
An amnesty is declared by Parliament through a law and applies to everyone who meets its criteria — without an individual request. So the key question is whether the amnesty law in force covers the specific article and sentence.

### What to know

- A pardon can release a person fully or partly from a sentence or reduce it
- A pardon request can be made by the convicted person or a family member
- Conduct, compensating the victim, health and family situation all matter in a request
- An amnesty needs no request — but whether it applies can be disputed in a case
- Alternatives: early release on parole or replacing the rest of the sentence with a lighter one

Our services:
- Assessing whether an amnesty applies to your case
- Preparing the pardon request and documents
- References and evidence
- Parole as an alternative
- Advice for the family
- Removing the criminal record after the sentence

### What is the difference between a pardon and an amnesty?
A pardon is granted by the President to a specific person on request. An amnesty is declared by Parliament through a law and applies to everyone who meets its conditions.

### Who can request a pardon?
The convicted person or a family member. The Pardon Commission reviews the request and the President decides.

### Is there an amnesty in 2026?
An amnesty can only be declared by a law passed by Parliament. If such a law is adopted, we will check whether it covers your article and sentence.

## Driving licence suspension in Georgia: 6 months, 1, 3 years
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/driving-licence-suspension/

For many people, losing their licence means losing their job. We check whether the test was done lawfully and the record properly drawn up, and appeal the decision within the 10-day deadline.

Under Article 116 of the Code of Administrative Offences, drink-driving at 0.3–0.7‰ leads to a 6-month suspension, and over 0.7‰ or refusing the test to a 1-year suspension. If it also causes minor damage to a vehicle, property or health — a GEL 2,000 fine and a 3-year suspension.
A licence is also suspended for unpaid fines: a traffic fine must be paid within 30 days, then you have 30 more days with a surcharge; if it is still unpaid, the licence is suspended for the term set by the relevant article.

### When the licence is suspended

- 0.3–0.7‰ — 6 months
- Over 0.7‰ or refusing an alcohol test — 1 year
- Refusing a drug test — GEL 1,000 and 1 year (taxi, bus or truck drivers — GEL 2,000 and 2 years)
- Drink-driving with minor damage — GEL 2,000 and 3 years
- Drink-driving while suspended — GEL 2,000, 5–15 days of administrative detention and the suspension extended by 1 year
- Unpaid traffic fine — suspension under the relevant article

When the suspension ends, the licence is restored — for a suspension on this basis no new exam is required.

Our services:
- Lawfulness of the alcohol or drug test
- Checking the record and video
- Appeal within 10 days
- Unpaid fines and suspension
- Defence if it becomes a criminal case (Article 276)
- Advice on getting the licence back

### How long will I lose my licence for drink-driving?
At 0.3–0.7‰ — 6 months; over 0.7‰ or refusing the test — 1 year. With minor damage — 3 years and a GEL 2,000 fine.

### Will my licence be suspended for an unpaid fine?
Yes. If a traffic fine isn't paid within 30 days, and then within another 30 days with a surcharge, the licence is suspended.

### Can I appeal?
Yes. The decision can be appealed within 10 days of receiving it. A lawyer checks the test procedure, the record and the video.

### Do I need to retake the exam afterwards?
After a suspension for an unpaid fine, the licence is restored when the term ends and no exam is required. In other cases the rule needs to be checked.

## Appealing a fine in Georgia: camera, patrol, parking
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/appealing-fines/

Camera and patrol fines aren't always right: sometimes someone else was driving, a sign wasn't visible or the record was drawn up incorrectly. We assess whether an appeal is worth it and file it on time.

Under the Code of Administrative Offences, a decision imposing a fine can be appealed within 10 days of being received. A deadline missed for a valid reason can be restored. A decision by an authority or official is usually appealed first to the higher authority, and its decision then to court.
An appeal pauses the deadline for paying the fine until it is decided. This matters because unpaid traffic fines end in a driving licence suspension.

### Which fines we appeal

- Camera fines — speed, red light, road markings
- Patrol police fines
- Driving or stopping in a bus lane
- Parking fines, including in Tbilisi (Article 125²)
- Other administrative fines

### Common grounds for appeal

- Someone else was driving the car
- A road sign or marking wasn't visible or was wrongly placed
- The photo or video doesn't clearly show the offence
- The record or decision has defects
- The decision was not properly served

### Deadlines

- Appeal — 10 days from receipt
- Payment — 30 days, then 30 more with a surcharge (for traffic offences)
- An appeal pauses the payment deadline

Our services:
- Appealing patrol, camera, bus-lane and parking fines
- Complaint to the higher authority
- Lawsuit in court
- Restoring a missed deadline for a valid reason
- Avoiding a licence suspension
- Other administrative fines

### How long do I have to appeal a fine?
10 days from receiving the decision. If you missed it for a valid reason, you can ask for the deadline to be restored.

### Can a parking or bus-lane fine be appealed too?
Yes. These are administrative offences too — for example, breaking parking rules in Tbilisi falls under Article 125² — and the decision can be appealed within 10 days of receipt.

### Do I have to pay while appealing?
An appeal pauses the payment deadline until it is decided. If it is rejected, the fine must be paid.

### Someone else was driving my car — what should I do?
That is a common ground for appeal. Say who was driving and provide evidence.

## Compensation for moral damage in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/moral-damage-compensation/

Moral damage — pain, distress, damaged dignity — can't be measured exactly in money, but the law provides for compensation in certain cases. We assess how realistic your claim is and prepare the lawsuit.

Under Article 413 of the Civil Code, money for non-pecuniary (moral) damage can be claimed only in cases set by law — in a reasonable and fair amount. For bodily injury or harm to health, moral damage can always be claimed.
Other important cases are culpable harm to honour, dignity, business reputation or private life (Article 18), including publishing a photo or video without consent, and damage caused by the state through unlawful conviction or detention (Article 1005). A medical institution is liable unless it proves it was not at fault (Article 1007).

### What a court considers when setting the amount

- The severity and duration of the harm
- Pain, distress and changes to daily life
- The degree of fault of the person responsible
- How widely information was spread — for harm to reputation
- Court practice in similar cases

Our services:
- Compensation for moral damage after an injury
- Compensation for harm to dignity, reputation or private life
- Compensation when a photo or video was published without consent
- Compensation for medical errors
- Compensation for unlawful arrest, detention or conviction
- Claiming moral and material damage together

### When can I claim moral damage?
Only in cases set by law — for example, injury, culpable harm to honour, dignity or private life, or unlawful detention or conviction.

### How much will a court award?
There is no fixed rate. The court sets a 'reasonable and fair' amount based on the severity of the harm, fault and practice.

### I was unlawfully detained — am I owed compensation?
A rehabilitated person is compensated by the state for damage from unlawful conviction or detention — regardless of officials' fault.

## Establishing paternity in court in Georgia — lawyer
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/establishing-paternity/

When parents aren't married and don't make a joint declaration, a child's paternity is established in court. We prepare the claim, request a DNA test and protect the interests of the child or the parent.

Under Article 1190 of the Civil Code, the parentage of a child of unmarried parents is established by the parents' joint declaration. Without one, paternity is established in court — on the application of a parent, the child's guardian, the person supporting the child, or the child after reaching adulthood.
The court establishes paternity based on a biological (genetic) test. If that is impossible, it considers other evidence — living together, raising or supporting the child together, acknowledgment of paternity. Once paternity is established, the child has the same rights as a child of married parents — including child support and inheritance.

### An important deadline

A man with good reason to believe he is the child's father can challenge the civil registry record within 1 year of when he learned or should have learned of it.

A court may refuse to establish paternity if it is contrary to the child's interests.

Our services:
- Claim to establish paternity
- Requesting a DNA test
- Challenging the record of the father
- Claiming child support together with paternity
- Inheritance issues
- Defence for the respondent

### How is paternity established in court?
Mainly by DNA testing. If that's impossible, the court considers living together, raising or supporting the child together, and other evidence of acknowledgment.

### Who can apply to establish paternity?
A parent, the child's guardian, the person supporting the child, or the child after reaching adulthood.

### Can child support be claimed too?
Yes. Once paternity is established, the child has the same rights as a child of married parents — including the right to support.

## Taking a child abroad from Georgia: parental consent
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/taking-a-child-abroad/

Taking a child abroad is often disputed — especially when parents live apart. We find out what the law requires in your case and resolve the dispute — by agreement or in court.

Under Article 8 of the Law on the Rules for Georgian Citizens Leaving and Entering Georgia, a child under 16 can travel abroad temporarily with the permission of one legal representative (parent) and accompanied by an adult with legal capacity. From 16 to 18, if not married, with the consent of one legal representative.
For a passport, one parent's consent is enough only in cases set by law — for example, if the child is 16 or older, the other parent's parental rights have been removed or restricted, their whereabouts are unknown, or travel is needed for medical treatment. If parents can't agree on the child's travel, a court decides.

### If a child was taken unlawfully or isn't being returned

Georgia is a party to the Hague Convention on International Child Abduction. If a child was wrongfully taken to, or is being kept in, another member country, you can ask for the child's return — time is critical.

Our services:
- Advice on what consent is needed in your case
- Passport with one parent's consent
- Court claim when parents disagree
- Child's residence and contact arrangements
- Returning a child under the Hague Convention
- Drafting a parenting agreement

### Can I take my child abroad without the other parent's consent?
By law, for temporary travel of a child under 16, one parent's permission and an adult escort are enough. But a passport usually needs both parents' consent, and in a dispute a court decides.

### The other parent won't consent to a passport — what can I do?
In some cases one parent's consent is enough (e.g. the other parent's whereabouts are unknown or travel is needed for treatment). Otherwise you can go to court.

### The other parent took our child abroad and won't return them — what should I do?
If the child is in a Hague Convention country, you can ask for the child's return. Act quickly — time matters a lot in these cases.

## Unfair dismissal in Georgia — how to challenge it
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/unfair-dismissal/

Under the Labour Code, an employee can be dismissed only on grounds set by law. We check whether your dismissal was lawful and protect your interests — through reinstatement, compensation and back pay.

Under Article 47 of the Labour Code, an employment contract can be ended only on grounds listed in the law — for example, redundancy, a serious breach of duties, mutual agreement or the end of a fixed term. Dismissal on discriminatory grounds is prohibited, as is dismissal from notifying the employer of pregnancy until the end of maternity and childcare leave — with exceptions set by law.
If the employer dismisses someone for redundancy, lack of qualifications, long-term incapacity or another objective reason, it must give 30 days' written notice and pay at least 1 month's salary; with only 3 days' notice — at least 2 months' salary.

### Deadlines you must not miss

1. Within 30 days of receiving notice of dismissal, ask the employer in writing for the reasons.
2. The employer must give written reasons within 7 days.
3. Within 30 days of receiving the reasons, you can challenge the decision in court. If the employer doesn't reply within 7 days, you also have 30 days — and the burden of proof shifts to the employer.
4. If you didn't ask for reasons, the deadline for a lawsuit is 30 days from receiving the dismissal notice.

### What you can achieve in court

- Reinstatement to the same or an equivalent job — or compensation set by the court
- Back pay from dismissal until the judgment is enforced
- Pay for unused leave and the final settlement

Our services:
- Assessing whether the dismissal was lawful
- Drafting the request for written reasons
- Lawsuit for reinstatement
- Claiming back pay and compensation
- Negotiating and settling with the employer
- Advising employers on lawful dismissal

### How long do I have to challenge a dismissal?
The deadlines are very short: ask for written reasons within 30 days, then sue within 30 days of receiving them. If you didn't ask for reasons, you have 30 days from receiving the dismissal notice.

### Can a pregnant woman be dismissed?
Dismissal is prohibited from notifying the employer of pregnancy until the end of maternity and childcare leave — except in cases listed by law, such as the end of a fixed term, resignation or a serious breach of duties.

### What compensation do I get for redundancy?
With 30 days' written notice — at least 1 month's salary; with 3 days' notice — at least 2 months' salary. Pay for unused leave comes on top.

### Can I be dismissed during probation?
Yes. A probation period (up to 6 months) can be ended at any time and the Article 48 rules don't apply unless the contract says otherwise. The time worked must still be paid.

## Labour Code of Georgia: leave, maternity, salary
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/labour-code-leave-salary/

The main rules of the Georgian Labour Code in plain language — and help when an employer doesn't follow them: unpaid salary, overtime, leave or maternity leave.

Normal working time must not exceed 40 hours a week (48 in certain continuous-operation workplaces), and rest between working days must be at least 12 hours. Overtime is worked by agreement and paid at an increased hourly rate — or, by agreement, with extra time off.
Salary must be paid at least once a month. For every day of delay, the employer owes 0.07% of the late amount. On leaving a job, the final settlement must be made within 7 days unless the contract or the law says otherwise.

### Leave

- Paid leave — at least 24 working days a year
- Unpaid leave — at least 15 calendar days a year
- Heavy, harmful or hazardous work — 10 extra calendar days
- A contract clause giving up annual paid leave is void
- If the employer ends the contract, unused leave must be paid

### Maternity and childcare leave

- Pregnancy and childbirth — 126 calendar days (143 with complications or twins)
- Childcare — 604 days (587 with complications or twins); 57 of them are paid
- Childcare leave can be taken by the mother or the father; it is paid from the state budget
- Adopting a child under 1 — 550 days, 90 of them paid
- Plus 12 weeks unpaid, until the child turns 5
- A breastfeeding mother of a child under 1 gets at least 1 hour of paid feeding break a day

### If your rights are breached

1. Tell the employer in writing what was breached and what you want — it has 10 days to reply.
2. If there's no agreement within 14 days, you can go to court. If the employer avoided negotiating, the burden of proof is on it.
3. The deadline for a lawsuit is usually 1 year from learning of the breach (30 days for a dismissal dispute).
4. You can also complain to the Labour Inspection, which fines employers.

Our services:
- Recovering unpaid salary and late-payment interest
- Claiming overtime pay
- Help with leave and maternity leave
- Reviewing an employment contract before signing
- Letter to the employer and negotiation
- Complaint to the Labour Inspection and lawsuit

### How many days of leave am I entitled to?
At least 24 working days of paid leave and at least 15 calendar days of unpaid leave a year. A contract can give more, never less.

### How long is maternity leave?
126 days for pregnancy and childbirth (143 with complications or twins), then childcare leave. In total 183 days (or 200) are paid, by the state.

### My salary is late — what can I do?
For every day of delay the employer owes you 0.07% of the amount. Send a written demand; if there's no agreement within 14 days, you can go to court.

### Is overtime paid?
Yes — at an increased hourly rate agreed by the parties, or with extra time off by agreement. Pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, parents of children under 3 and minors can't be made to work overtime without their consent.

## Debtors' register in Georgia: checking and removal
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/debtors-register/

Being on the debtors' register means enforcement has started against you: selling property is restricted and bank accounts are frozen. We find out why you're on the register and how you can be removed.

Under Article 19¹ of the Law on Enforcement Proceedings, a person is entered on the debtors' register as soon as enforcement of a money claim starts against them. The register is kept by the National Bureau of Enforcement; its data are public, and an extract is issued no later than the next working day after the application, for a fee. A debtor whose debt is secured by a mortgage or pledge, for example, is not entered.
As soon as you're registered, selling or encumbering registered property — a flat, land, a car — is restricted, and banks freeze your accounts up to the amount of the claim, including newly opened ones. Being on the register doesn't cancel the debt — enforcement continues.

### When the entry is removed

- The debt is paid in full
- A fine has been replaced by another penalty
- Enforcement has ended — for example, the creditor waived it, the parties settled, the decision was quashed, or 10 years have passed since enforcement began (5 for fines)
- A court has ruled so

On removal, all restrictions are lifted.

### Selling property while on the register

Restricted property can be sold with the consent of the National Bureau of Enforcement, and in a private creditor's case with the creditor's consent too. The debt is often paid from the sale.

Our services:
- Checking which case and which creditor put you on the register
- Checking the basis and time limits of enforcement
- Removal after the 10-year enforcement limit
- Negotiating a payment plan with the creditor
- Selling property with the creditor's and Bureau's consent
- Appealing a judgment made in your absence

### How do I find out if I'm on the debtors' register?
The register's data are public. The National Bureau of Enforcement issues an extract no later than the next working day after the application, for a fee. We can check which case and which creditor you're registered for.

### I paid the debt — will I be removed automatically?
Paying in full is a ground for removal, and all restrictions are lifted on removal. If the entry hasn't been removed, you need to contact the enforcement officer — we can help.

### I'm on the register — can I sell my flat?
Only with consent: in cases for the state budget — the National Bureau of Enforcement's; in other cases — the Bureau's and the creditor's.

### I'm on the register for a very old debt — what can I do?
If 10 years have passed since enforcement of a money claim began, enforcement must end and you must be removed — except in cases set by law, such as alimony.

## Dividing marital property in a Georgian divorce
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/marital-property-division/

Property acquired during marriage is usually joint — even if registered in one spouse's name. We help divide it fairly — by agreement or in court.

Under Article 1158 of the Civil Code, property acquired during marriage is the spouses' joint property unless a marriage contract says otherwise — even if one spouse looked after the home and children and had no income of their own. On division the shares are equal unless agreed otherwise.
Separate property is what each spouse owned before marriage and what they received during it by inheritance or gift. But if its value grew significantly through joint spending during the marriage — for example, a flat was renovated or construction completed — a court may treat it as joint.

### What a court considers

- It can depart from equal shares in the interests of minor children or of one spouse — for example, if the children live with them or they can't work
- The share of a spouse who spent joint property against the family's interests can be reduced
- Items needed for one spouse's profession go to that spouse
- If one spouse gets more than their share, the other receives money or other compensation
- Joint debts — a mortgage, for example — are split in proportion to the shares

### The deadline

A 3-year limitation period applies to claims by divorced spouses to divide joint property. Property can also be divided during the marriage.

These rules apply to registered marriage. For couples living together without registration, disputes over property bought together are decided differently — by proving each person's contribution.

Our services:
- Separating joint and personal property
- Dividing a flat, land, a car or a business share
- Splitting joint debts and the mortgage
- Drafting a property division agreement
- Lawsuit to divide property
- Drafting a marriage contract

### The flat is in my spouse's name — is it still joint?
If it was bought during the marriage, yes — whoever it's registered to, unless a marriage contract says otherwise.

### Is a flat bought before marriage divided?
Usually not — it's personal property. But if its value grew significantly through joint spending during the marriage (renovation, completing construction), a court may treat it as joint.

### How long do I have to ask for division?
After divorce the limitation period is 3 years. When it starts running can be disputed, so don't delay.

### Who pays the mortgage after division?
Joint debts are split between the spouses in proportion to their shares of joint property. With the bank, though, the loan contract still applies — so this needs to be settled separately in the agreement or lawsuit.

## Wills in Georgia — making and challenging a will
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/wills-in-georgia/

With a will, you decide who gets your property. We help you make a will that no one can successfully contest — and we protect heirs when a will is unfair or was made in breach of the law.

A will can be made by an adult with legal capacity who, at that moment, can reasonably judge their own actions. A will must be made in person — it cannot be made through a representative. Only spouses can make a joint will, about inheriting from each other. You can change or revoke a will at any time.
You can leave property to relatives, to other people or to organisations. But the deceased's children, parents and spouse are entitled to a compulsory share regardless of the will — half of what they would have received without a will (Civil Code, Article 1371).

### Forms of a will

| Form | How it is made | What to know |
|---|---|---|
| Notarial will | The testator writes and signs it, a notary certifies it | The most reliable; a notarial will takes priority and cannot be revoked by a will in another form |
| Recorded by a notary | The notary writes down the testator's words with 2 witnesses present | The testator reads it and signs it in front of the notary and a witness |
| Handwritten will | The testator writes it by hand and signs it | Can be handed to a notary in a sealed envelope for safekeeping, with 3 witnesses present |

A witness cannot be a minor, an heir under the will or their close relatives — parents, children, siblings or spouse. The notary and witnesses may not disclose the content of the will before the inheritance opens.

### When a will can be challenged

- When making it, the testator could not understand the meaning of their actions — for example, because of a serious illness
- The will was made in breach of the legal rules — form, witnesses, signature
- The will was made through deception, coercion or another ground that makes a transaction void
- The provisions of the will are unclear or contradict each other
- The will ignores your compulsory share — in that case you claim the share separately

A claim to invalidate a will must be filed within 2 years of the inheritance opening — usually the day the person died. Once the will is invalidated, the estate is divided under the law.

Our services:
- Drafting a will and having it certified by a notary
- Joint will of spouses
- Reviewing and changing an existing will
- Lawsuit to invalidate a will
- Claiming the compulsory share
- Executing the will and registering property to the heir

### Is a handwritten will valid?
Yes — a handwritten will is valid if the testator wrote it by hand and signed it. But it is easier to contest, so we recommend a notarial will.

### Can I leave my child nothing at all?
Children, parents and the spouse are entitled to a compulsory share regardless of the will — half of their share under the law. The exception is when an heir has lost the right to inherit under the law, for example as an unworthy heir.

### How long do I have to challenge a will?
2 years from the inheritance opening. After that, the will can no longer be challenged.

### There are several wills — which one applies?
A newer will revokes the older one to the extent they conflict. A notarial will, however, takes priority and cannot be revoked by a will in another form.

## Debt recovery in Georgia — loans, IOUs, enforcement
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/debt-recovery-georgia/

A debt can be recovered through the courts or — if the contract was certified by a notary — even without going to court. We assess your documents, choose the fastest route and make sure the debtor doesn't dispose of their assets.

The limitation period for a claim to repay a loan is 3 years (Civil Code, Article 129) — usually from the day the money was due. So don't wait: once it has passed, the debtor can argue that the claim is time-barred.
The law doesn't always require a loan agreement to be in writing, but in a dispute documents decide: the contract, an IOU, bank transfers, messages. The effective annual interest rate on a loan must not exceed 50% — this applies to every loan, including between private individuals.

### Recovering a debt step by step

1. We gather evidence — the contract, IOU, transfers, messages, witnesses.
2. We send the debtor a written demand with a deadline — often this alone is enough.
3. If they don't pay, we file a lawsuit. The court fee is 3% of the amount claimed, but at least 100 GEL.
4. Together with the lawsuit we can ask the court to freeze the debtor's property or account so it isn't disposed of before the case is decided.
5. After the judgment, the National Bureau of Enforcement collects the debt and the debtor is entered into the debtors register.

### When you can skip the court

If the loan agreement was certified by a notary and the parties agreed in it to the issue of a writ of execution, once the debt is due the notary issues the writ (Law on Notaries, Article 38) and enforcement starts without a court case. That is why we recommend signing larger loans before a notary.

A claim based on a promissory note can be heard by the court under a simplified procedure — only documents and the parties' explanations are used as evidence.

Our services:
- Assessing the chances of recovery and the evidence
- Demand letter and negotiation with the debtor
- Lawsuit to recover the debt with interest and penalties
- Asking the court to freeze the debtor's property and accounts
- Obtaining a writ of execution from a notary
- Managing the enforcement process

### I lent money without an IOU — can I get it back?
Possibly. Evidence can be a bank transfer, messages, an audio recording or a witness. The sooner you contact us, the more evidence we can preserve.

### How long do I have to claim the debt?
The limitation period is 3 years — usually from the repayment date. After that the debtor can rely on the limitation period and the court will reject the claim.

### How much does a lawsuit cost?
The court fee is 3% of the amount claimed, but at least 100 GEL. If you win, the losing party usually reimburses the court costs.

### The debtor has no assets — what happens?
The judgment goes to enforcement and the debtor is entered into the debtors register: they can't register new property or a car without the enforcement bureau finding out. Money can also be deducted from their salary.

## Contract drafting and review in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/contract-drafting-review/

A good contract keeps you out of disputes; a bad one causes them. We draft contracts in your interest and review the other side's text before you sign: the risks, deadlines, penalties and what happens if something is not delivered.

A contract is concluded once the parties agree on all essential terms (Civil Code, Article 327). If the law or the parties themselves require a particular form, the contract takes effect only once that form is followed. For example, acquiring real estate requires a written contract and registration of ownership in the Public Registry.
Most problems are visible before signing: vague obligations, missing deadlines, a one-sided right to terminate, an excessive penalty or an unexpected place for resolving disputes. That is why we review a contract before you sign it.

### What we check in a contract

- The parties and their authority — who signs and whether they are entitled to
- Subject, price and payment terms — precise and unambiguous
- Deadlines and what happens if they are missed
- Penalties — they must be agreed in writing, and a court reduces an excessive penalty
- Deposit — if the party who paid it breaches the contract, the deposit stays with the recipient
- Termination, force majeure and where disputes are resolved — court or arbitration

### Contracts we draft most often

- Real estate sale and preliminary agreements
- Leases — flats, offices, commercial premises
- Loans and guarantees
- Services and works — renovation, construction, IT services
- Partners' agreements and share purchases
- Bilingual contracts with foreign partners

Our services:
- Drafting a contract in your interest
- Reviewing the other side's contract before signing
- Negotiating the terms
- Bilingual contracts — Georgian, English, Russian
- Amending and terminating contracts
- Claims and lawsuits for breach of contract

### Is a verbal agreement a contract?
Often — yes, if the law doesn't require a particular form. But a verbal agreement is hard to prove. Real estate, however, can only be acquired with a written contract and registration.

### Do I need to have a contract certified by a notary?
Not always. Notarisation is required by law in some cases and useful in others: for example, a debt under a notarised loan agreement can be recovered even without going to court.

### How high can a contractual penalty be?
The parties set it freely, but the agreement must be in writing. If the penalty is excessive, a court can reduce it; for loans, the law sets a cap.

### Is a contract in English valid?
Yes, a contract can be made in any language. You may need a Georgian translation for the Public Registry or a court, so we often prepare a bilingual text.

## Banning a family member from gambling in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/gambling-ban-family-member/

If a family member is addicted to gambling and harming the family, they can be placed on the list of gambling-dependent persons. For the next 5 years no casino, slot hall, betting shop or online casino can let them play. A family member files the application with the court — we prepare it and gather the evidence.

The list of dependent persons is kept by the Revenue Service. A person can be added in two ways: by their own application to the Revenue Service, or by a judge's order issued on a family member's application. A family member means a parent, spouse, child or someone who lives with the person permanently (Administrative Procedure Code, Articles 21⁸⁵–21⁸⁶).
For 5 years a listed person cannot enter a casino or slot hall, or bet or play online: operators check every player with the Revenue Service. Only Georgian citizens can be placed on the list.

### How the court case works

1. A family member files a written application with the magistrate or district (city) court where the person lives. The application is free of court fees.
2. It is accompanied by proof of the family relationship and evidence: bank statements, transfers to betting sites and casinos, loans, messages, witnesses.
3. The judge sends the application and materials to the person concerned; they have 48 hours from receipt to respond in writing.
4. The judge issues an order within 3–5 working days — with or without a hearing, behind closed doors if needed. The burden of proof is on the applicant.
5. The order takes effect immediately. It can be appealed to the Court of Appeal within 3 days; that court decides within 5 working days and its decision is final.

### What the judge considers

- How serious the addiction is — how often and for how much they gamble
- The financial harm to the family member — debts, sold belongings, family money
- The individual circumstances — for example, whether there were attempts at treatment or to stop

### Coming off the list

A person stays on the list for 5 years. Early removal is only possible on that person's own application, by court order, and no sooner than 3 years after being listed.

Our services:
- Court application to place a person on the dependent list
- Gathering evidence — bank records, debts, messages
- Representation in court and appeals
- Advice on self-exclusion with the Revenue Service
- Application for early removal from the list
- Protecting family property from gambling debts

### Who can apply to the court?
A parent, spouse, child or someone who lives permanently with the person.

### How much does it cost and how long does it take?
The application is free of court fees. The judge issues an order within 3–5 working days and it takes effect immediately.

### Does the ban cover online casinos?
Yes. It covers casinos, slot halls, betting and online gambling — when the operator holds a Georgian permit.

### Can a person ban themselves?
Yes — by applying to the Revenue Service. They are also listed for 5 years.

### Who is barred from gambling by law?
Georgian citizens under 25, foreigners under 18, people employed in public institutions, the National Bank and regulators, and family members registered in the database of socially vulnerable families.

## Gambling debts in Georgia — protecting family property
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/gambling-debts-georgia/

A loan taken for gambling is an ordinary debt — the bank or microfinance lender doesn't care what it was spent on. But one spouse's debt is not automatically the whole family's debt. We help you protect your share, deal with the debts and stop new ones.

Under Article 1170 of the Civil Code, one spouse's debt is collected from their personal property and their share of joint property. Joint marital property can be used only if a court finds that the borrowed money served the common interests of the whole family — and money lost gambling usually doesn't.
If a spouse spent joint property against the family's interests, a court can increase the other spouse's share on division (Article 1168). Joint property can be divided during the marriage too — protecting your share from new debts.

### What to do

1. Don't sign as a guarantor or co-borrower — then the debt is yours too.
2. Get the full list of debts: banks, microfinance lenders, private lenders, the debtors register.
3. Check whether a debt is time-barred and whether interest and penalties exceed the legal limits — the effective annual rate on a loan must not exceed 50%.
4. If the family flat or car faces enforcement, prove your share and ask for the property to be divided.
5. To stop new debts, ask the court to place the family member on the list of gambling-dependent persons.

### When the debt is a child's or parent's

Other family members are not liable for an adult child's or parent's debt unless they signed as guarantor or co-borrower. The debt is collected only from the debtor's property. The problem arises when the flat is in the debtor's name — so property matters should be settled early.

Our services:
- Assessing the debts — limitation, interest, penalties
- Negotiating restructuring with banks and microfinance lenders
- Defence in court and at enforcement
- Protecting the spouse's share when joint property is targeted
- Dividing joint property during the marriage
- Banning a family member from gambling

### Can my spouse's gambling debt be collected from our flat?
Only from their share. Joint property can be used only if a court finds the money served the family's common interests. Money lost gambling usually doesn't.

### Is a loan taken for gambling void?
No — the purpose of a loan doesn't affect its validity. But interest and penalties above the legal limits can be reduced, and you can refuse to pay a time-barred debt.

### Am I liable for my child's debt?
No, unless you are a guarantor or co-borrower. An adult child's debt is collected only from their own property.

### How do I stop new debts?
A family member applies to the court to place the person on the dependent list — after that they cannot gamble at any licensed casino or betting operator for 5 years.

## Living in a flat for a lump sum (girao) in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/girao-apartment-lump-sum-georgia/

Girao means you give the owner a lump sum, live in the flat rent-free and get the money back at the end. Legally it is a loan secured by a mortgage on the flat. If the contract isn't done properly and registered, getting your money back can be very hard. We check the flat, prepare the contract and protect you in a dispute.

Under Article 286 of the Civil Code, a private lender that isn't a supervised financial institution generally may not take real estate as security for a loan to an individual. Girao is the exception: when the mortgaged home is handed to the lender to live in. From the third mortgage in favour of the same person, the exception no longer applies.
A mortgage exists only once registered in the Public Registry, and a mortgage securing a loan must be notarised — the notary explains the consequences (Article 289). If a flat has several mortgages, the one registered first has priority (Article 290).

### Before you pay

1. Get a fresh Public Registry extract: who owns the flat and whether there is a mortgage, seizure or other restriction.
2. Check whether the owner is on the debtors register.
3. If the flat has several owners, all of them must sign.
4. Sign before a notary and register the mortgage in the Public Registry — before paying or on the same day.
5. Pay by bank transfer so the payment is documented.

### What the contract should say

- The amount, currency and exact repayment date
- Your right to live there and who pays utilities and repairs
- What happens if the owner wants to sell or mortgage the flat again
- What happens if the money isn't repaid on time — enforcement through the mortgage
- Early termination terms for both sides

If the owner doesn't repay when the term ends, your mortgage lets you recover the money from the flat through enforcement. The flat can pass into your ownership only on a joint application by owner and creditor (Article 300).

Our services:
- Checking the flat in the registry before girao
- Drafting the girao contract
- Notarisation and registration
- Claiming the money back
- Enforcement through the mortgage
- Disputes with the owner or the owner's creditors

### Is girao legal?
Yes — the law expressly allows a home to secure a loan when it is handed to the lender to live in. The key is a notarised contract and a mortgage registered in the registry.

### What if the owner doesn't give my money back?
If the mortgage is registered, you recover the money from the flat through enforcement. Without registration you are an ordinary creditor, in line with everyone else.

### Is a notary required?
Yes. A mortgage securing a loan must be notarised, and it takes effect only when registered in the Public Registry.

### The flat already has a bank mortgage — can I still do girao?
You can, but the bank has priority and gets paid first. We advise against it, or recommend extra protection terms.

## Renting an apartment in Georgia — the lease
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/apartment-lease-georgia/

A well-drafted lease protects both sides — the landlord and the tenant. We draft leases in Georgian and English or Russian, check the flat and help in disputes — from unpaid rent to eviction.

If a rented flat is sold after it was handed to the tenant, the new owner takes over the lease (Civil Code, Article 572) — the tenant doesn't have to leave because of the sale. A lease can also be registered in the Public Registry, which makes it visible to buyers and creditors — especially useful for long or commercial leases.
An individual renting out housing for living purposes, without claiming expenses, pays 5% on the rental income (Tax Code, Article 81).

### What the lease should say

- The parties and exact details of the flat — with its cadastral code
- Rent, currency, payment date and method
- Term and renewal
- Advance payment and deposit — when and on what terms it is returned
- Utilities and minor repairs — who pays
- Pets, subletting, registering at the address
- Early termination and notice period
- A condition report and photos at handover

### When registration is worth it

Registration needs a written contract with certified signatures, or both parties signing at the registry. For long or commercial leases we recommend it — it makes your right visible to everyone.

Our services:
- Drafting the lease
- Bilingual lease — Georgian and English or Russian
- Checking the flat in the Public Registry
- Registering the lease
- Claiming unpaid rent and damages
- Evicting a tenant through the courts

### Does a lease need a notary?
No. But to register the lease, signatures must be certified or both parties must sign at the registry.

### The flat was sold — do I have to move out?
No. If the flat was already handed to you, the new owner takes over the lease.

### What tax does the landlord pay?
An individual renting out housing for living purposes without claiming expenses pays 5% of the rent.

### Can the lease be in English or Russian?
Yes. We usually prepare a bilingual text — Georgian plus English or Russian — for the registry and courts.

## Mortgage in Georgia — contract, registration, enforcement
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/mortgage-georgia/

A mortgage is a debt secured by property — a bank loan, a private loan or girao. We check the contract before you sign, defend owners when a bank or private lender tries to auction a home, and act for creditors who aren't being repaid.

A mortgage exists only once registered in the Public Registry. A mortgage securing a private loan must be notarised — this doesn't apply to banks, microbanks, microfinance organisations or credit unions (Civil Code, Article 289). With several mortgages, the one registered first has priority.
Only a lender supervised or registered by the National Bank may secure a loan to an individual with real estate — the exception is girao, where the flat is handed to the lender to live in (Article 286). The effective annual interest rate on a loan must not exceed 50% (Article 625).

### What we check

- Whether the lender was allowed to make a loan secured by real estate
- Whether the contract was notarised where that is mandatory
- Interest, penalties and fees — within the legal limits
- Which property is mortgaged and to whom — it can be a third party's property
- The enforcement procedure and the chance to stop an auction or negotiate

For foreigners, each bank sets its own mortgage lending conditions. We check the contract and the property before you sign.

Our services:
- Reviewing the mortgage contract before signing
- Registering and removing a mortgage
- Checking whether a private lender's contract is lawful
- Challenging an auction or enforcement
- Negotiating restructuring with a bank
- Representing creditors in debt recovery

### Can I borrow from a private person against my flat?
As an individual, generally not — only a supervised or registered lender can make loans secured by real estate. Girao is the exception.

### Can the flat pass to the creditor automatically?
No. Ownership passes only on a joint application by owner and creditor; otherwise the money is recovered through enforcement.

### My loan has very high interest — what can I do?
The effective annual rate must not exceed 50%, and the law caps penalties and charges. You can refuse to pay the excess — we'll check the contract.

## Land registration in Georgia — sporadic and occupied land
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/land-registration-georgia/

The state's free systematic registration ended on 1 January 2026. Unregistered land is now registered on your own application — the sporadic procedure. We check your documents, prepare the application, resolve overlaps with neighbours and act for you if you are refused.

According to the Public Registry, more than 2 million plots were surveyed free of charge in the 2022–2025 reform. From 2026, registration is sporadic — on the owner's application, anywhere in the country. Applications filed before the reform ended are processed free.
Documents proving possession must date from before 20 September 2007: for example, a household book extract, a gardener's booklet, the 1992 land-reform distribution list, a land-tax list, a technical inventory record, an allocation act or a court act. Copies kept in an official archive are accepted too.

### What the law provides

- An unwritten sale can be confirmed by at least 3 owners in the same cadastral block
- If the fenced area is up to 15% larger than in the document, the plot is registered by its actual boundary (except household plots)
- Surveying by a certified surveyor or, since June 2026, by the Public Registry within 15 working days: agricultural plot up to 0.15 ha — GEL 300, 0.15–1 ha — 500, 1–5 ha — 700, over 5 ha — 1,000; non-agricultural — double
- Registration within 4 working days: agricultural land — GEL 50 (GEL 300 in Tbilisi and Batumi), non-agricultural — GEL 300

### Self-occupied land

Ownership can be recognised if a person occupied state land before 20 September 2007 and it has a house or other building (even unfinished or ruined), or it adjoins land they already own. Area — up to 1.25 ha in the lowlands, up to 5 ha in high-mountain settlements. Evidence can be a document or witness testimony. Until 1 January 2027, in all municipalities except self-governing cities, the Public Registry decides — within 3 months, for GEL 600. Pastures, forests, protected areas, roads and cemeteries can't be recognised.

### Overlap with a neighbour

- In a dispute, notary mediation is compulsory — within 3 weeks; a signed agreement is the basis for registration
- If the disputed strip is up to 30% of each plot, both are registered as claimed with a dispute note, and a court decides
- Above 30%, or if mediation fails, the dispute goes to court
- A Public Registry decision can be appealed within 30 calendar days

Our services:
- Finding and assessing documents
- Sporadic registration application
- Recognition of self-occupied land
- Resolving overlaps and boundary disputes
- Appealing a Public Registry refusal
- Registering inherited land

### Is systematic registration still free?
No. The systematic registration reform ended on 1 January 2026. Land is now registered on your own application, by the sporadic procedure.

### I have no documents — can I register my land?
Possibly. The law accepts many old documents — from household books to land-tax lists. For self-occupied land, witness testimony can also count.

### How much does land registration cost?
Agricultural land — GEL 50 (300 in Tbilisi and Batumi), non-agricultural — GEL 300, plus surveying. Self-occupied land — GEL 600.

### My neighbour's plot overlaps mine — what now?
First notary mediation, within 3 weeks. If you can't agree, a court decides. We prepare the boundary evidence and represent you.

## Building a house on agricultural land in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/building-on-agricultural-land-georgia/

Building an individual house on a privately owned agricultural plot is often allowed — if it fits the zone or the surrounding buildings. For other non-farm uses, the land's designation has to change first. We check what is and isn't allowed and prepare the application.

Under the Law on Land Designation and Sustainable Management, an agricultural plot may carry an individual house, farm buildings or auxiliary buildings. Under the Spatial Planning Code, a house on a private agricultural plot is allowed if it fits the zone or existing buildings; outside settlements, no permit is issued for housing.
Changes of designation are decided by the Public Registry and require a justified need. If an approved development plan changes the zone, the owner's application is enough. A commission gives its opinion within 15 days and the decision follows within 5; the registration fee is GEL 50.

### Compensation for a change of designation

- Only in special-regulation territories — GEL 100,000 per hectare
- In Tbilisi and Batumi — GEL 34,001 per hectare
- Elsewhere no compensation; state and municipal land is exempt
- Paid in proportion to the area, before the final decision

### Changing the category

Agricultural land can only move 'up' a category — e.g. pasture to hay meadow, arable or household plot, arable to household plot — on the owner's application. Building a house also needs a municipal building permit.

Our services:
- Checking the plot's zone and designation
- Application to change designation
- Changing the land category
- Municipal building permit
- Appealing a refusal
- Unauthorised construction cases

### Can I build a house on agricultural land?
On a private plot — often yes, if it fits the zone or surrounding buildings. Outside settlements, no permit is issued for housing. We'll check your plot.

### Who changes land designation?
The Public Registry — where there is a justified need, based on a commission's opinion.

### What does a change of designation cost?
The registration fee is GEL 50. Compensation applies only in Tbilisi and Batumi (GEL 34,001/ha) and special-regulation territories (GEL 100,000/ha).

## Bringing medication into Georgia — what is restricted
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/bringing-medication-into-georgia/

Many medicines that are ordinary elsewhere — Lyrica (pregabalin), tramadol, codeine products, ADHD medication, sleeping pills and sedatives — are under special control in Georgia. You can bring them in, but only with proper documents. Without them, a criminal case can start.

Under Article 19 of the Law on Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances, Precursors and Narcological Assistance, an individual — including someone in transit — may carry narcotic and psychotropic medicines for treatment with proper medical and customs documents. This is not treated as import. The detailed procedure is approved by the Health Ministry with the Revenue Service.
Bringing them in without documents is a serious risk: illegally importing a narcotic drug carries 6 to 9 years under Article 262, and a psychotropic or potent substance in a large amount 2 to 5 years under Article 263. Under a 2022 Constitutional Court decision, prison cannot be imposed for bringing in up to 9.68 g of dried marijuana for personal use.

### What to carry

- A doctor's prescription or medical certificate showing the diagnosis, medicine and dose — preferably with an English translation
- The medicine in its original packaging
- Only the quantity your treatment needs
- Declare it at customs if the medicine is controlled

### Which medicines are controlled

The controlled lists include, for example, pregabalin (Lyrica), tramadol, codeine, buprenorphine, methylphenidate, alprazolam and zolpidem. For pregabalin, the amount is counted by the full weight of the medicine — so even a few packs can count as a 'large amount'. Check your medicine before travelling — we can help.

Our services:
- Checking your medicine against the controlled lists before travel
- Preparing and translating documents
- Defence if you are detained at the border
- Getting seized medicine back
- Defence against charges under Articles 262 and 263
- Cases about medicine sent by post

### Can I bring Lyrica (pregabalin) into Georgia?
Yes, for treatment — with medical documents and a customs declaration. Without documents a criminal case can start, because pregabalin is controlled in Georgia.

### Customs took my medicine — what should I do?
Don't give a statement without a lawyer and keep all documents. We check which article applies and work to close the case if the medicine was for your treatment.

### I'm only in transit — does this apply to me?
Yes. The law covers people in transit too: carry the medicine with medical and customs documents.

## Lyrica (pregabalin) and tramadol in Georgia — Article 261
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/pregabalin-tramadol-georgia/

In Georgia, Lyrica (pregabalin) and tramadol are psychotropic and potent substances. Obtaining or keeping them without a prescription is a crime (Article 261), and selling them is far more serious. We defend the accused from the forensic examination to the courtroom.

The amounts are set in an annex to the law. Pregabalin: small amount up to 0.6 g, criminal-liability threshold up to 6 g, large amount up to 20 g. Tramadol: small up to 1 g, threshold up to 80 g, large up to 800 g. For pregabalin, tianeptine and ketamine the medicine form itself counts, not just the pure substance — so a few capsules can be enough.
Selling gabapentin, baclofen or cyclodol in any form is a crime (Article 260³).

### Penalties under Article 261

| Act | Penalty |
|---|---|
| Obtaining or keeping a psychotropic substance (e.g. pregabalin) | A fine, corrective labour up to 2 years or up to 3 years in prison |
| The same, in a large amount, as a group or repeatedly | Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years |
| The same, in an especially large amount or by an organised group | Imprisonment from 8 to 12 years |
| Obtaining or keeping a potent substance (e.g. tramadol) | A fine or corrective labour up to 1 year |
| The same, in a large amount, as a group or repeatedly | Imprisonment from 3 to 7 years |
| The same, in an especially large amount or by an organised group | Imprisonment from 7 to 12 years |

Our services:
- Defence against Article 261 charges
- Checking the forensic examination and amount
- Proving a prescription and treatment
- Lawfulness of the search and seizure
- Plea agreements
- Defence against selling charges

### How much Lyrica is a crime?
More than 0.6 g of pregabalin is already a criminal case; a large amount is over 6 g. The medicine form counts, so a few capsules can be enough.

### I have a prescription — is it still a crime?
Medicine prescribed by a doctor and lawfully obtained is not a crime. Keep the prescription and proof of purchase.

### What is the penalty for tramadol?
Basic — a fine or corrective labour up to 1 year; in a large amount — 3 to 7 years; especially large — 7 to 12 years.

## Drug dealing charges in Georgia — Articles 260²–260⁴
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/drug-dealing-charges-georgia/

Since the 2025 reform, drug dealing has moved out of Article 260 into separate articles: free transfer (260²), sale (260³) and assisting a sale (260⁴). The penalty depends on the substance and the amount — and can reach life imprisonment. In these cases you need a lawyer from the first minute.

Article 260 now covers only obtaining and keeping. Dealing has its own penalties — lighter for marijuana and psychotropic substances, much heavier for other narcotic drugs. Assisting a sale, such as packaging or acting as a go-between, is punished like the sale itself.
Besides the sentence, a person convicted of a drug crime loses rights: a dealer for 15 years, and the right to medical and pharmaceutical work for 20 years (Law on Combating Drug Crime, Article 3). A plea agreement can shorten or cancel this.

### Penalties

| Act | Basic | Aggravated / especially large amount |
|---|---|---|
| Sale (260³): marijuana or psychotropic | 5–10 years | Aggravated: 6–12 years; especially large amount: 12–17 years |
| Sale (260³): other narcotic drugs | 12–20 years or life | Aggravated: 14–20 years or life; especially large amount: 16–20 years or life |
| Free transfer (260²): marijuana | 3–8 years | Aggravated: 6–10 years; especially large amount: 7–12 years |
| Free transfer (260²): psychotropic | 3–6 years | Aggravated: 5–9 years; especially large amount: 10–14 years |
| Free transfer (260²): other narcotic drugs | 10–15 years | Aggravated: 12–17 years; especially large amount: 14–20 years or life |
| Assisting a sale (260⁴) | Same as sale | Same as sale |

Our services:
- Defence against dealing charges
- Keeping or dealing — the right classification
- Checking covert investigative actions and controlled purchases
- Checking the forensic examination and amount
- Plea agreements and restoring rights
- Challenging pre-trial detention

### I gave some to a friend for free — is that dealing?
Free transfer is a separate crime (Article 260²) — 3 to 8 years for marijuana, 10 to 15 years for other narcotic drugs.

### How is keeping different from dealing?
Keeping falls under Article 260 and is punished less severely; for dealing, the prosecution must prove a sale or transfer. That is often the key issue for the defence.

### What rights does a convicted person lose?
A dealer loses the listed rights for 15 years, and medical and pharmaceutical work for 20 years. A plea agreement can reduce this.

## Drug test in Georgia — can you refuse? Fines and rights
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/drug-test-georgia/

The police may take you for a test to check for drug use. Avoiding the test is itself an offence — with a fine or administrative detention. We explain your rights, how the test works and how to challenge the result.

Under Article 45 of the Administrative Offences Code, avoiding a drug-use test is punished exactly like drug use itself (other than marijuana): a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or up to 60 days' administrative detention. Marijuana use is covered by a separate article (45¹).
For drivers, avoiding the test is punished more harshly (Article 115²): GEL 1,000 and a 1-year suspension of driving rights; for taxi, bus or truck drivers, GEL 2,000 and 2 years. Driving under the influence of drugs is a crime (Criminal Code, Article 276(1)).

### How the test works

- The police may take you to the MIA forensic department; you can refuse to be taken, but then you must take a lab test yourself within 4 hours — otherwise it counts as avoiding the test
- If the result is positive, you can ask for an alternative test of the sealed control sample within 10 days
- Sign the record only after reading it; if you disagree, write your objection
- Someone who voluntarily hands over a small amount of drugs, or voluntarily seeks medical help for drug use, is released from liability

### Other consequences

A court takes away the driving licence of a person punished for drug use for 3 years, and other listed rights for 5 years. So challenging the fine is often about much more than the money.

Our services:
- Advice on your rights during a test
- Requesting an alternative test
- Appealing the administrative case in court
- Challenging a driving suspension
- Defence under Article 276
- Restoring rights

### Can I refuse a drug test?
Refusing is itself an offence — GEL 500–2,000 or up to 60 days' detention, the same as for use. For drivers — GEL 1,000 and a 1-year driving ban.

### The positive result is wrong — what can I do?
Within 10 days ask for an alternative test of the sealed control sample, and contact us — the result can also be challenged in court.

### Will I lose my driving licence?
A court takes away the driving licence of a person punished for drug use for 3 years.

## Cocaine, MDMA, amphetamine in Georgia — amounts and penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/cocaine-mdma-amphetamine-georgia/

In a cocaine, ecstasy or amphetamine case, the amount decides almost everything — and the thresholds are tiny: 0.6 g of cocaine is already a 'large amount'. Below is the law's official table and the penalties. In such a case you need a lawyer before the first interview.

Obtaining or keeping a narcotic drug is punished under Article 260: above the small amount — up to 6 years in prison; a large amount — 5 to 8 years; especially large — 8 to 20 years or life. A small amount and use are an administrative offence — a GEL 500–2,000 fine or up to 60 days' detention. Ketamine and GHB are psychotropic substances, punished under Article 261.
New psychoactive substances — including what is sold as 'spice' or 'bio' — are treated separately: under Article 260 any amount is a crime, with up to 6 years in prison.

### Amounts in grams

| Substance | Small | Large | Especially large |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cocaine | 0.06 | 0.6 | 2 |
| Ecstasy (MDMA) | 0.05 | 0.5 | 1 |
| Amphetamine | 0.005 | 0.1 | 1 |
| Methamphetamine | 0.005 | 0.1 | 1 |
| Mephedrone | 0.01 | 0.1 | 1 |
| 'Alpha' (α-PVP) | 0.001 | 0.2 | 1 |
| Hashish (cannabis resin) | 0.05 | 0.5 | 5 |
| LSD | 0.00002 | 0.0002 | 0.001 |
| Ketamine (psychotropic) | 0.1 | 1 | 3 |
| GHB (psychotropic) | 1 | 10 | 50 |

Up to the small amount — an administrative case; above it — a criminal case; the 'large' and 'especially large' columns mark the harsher penalty bands. The amount is set by a forensic examination — that is often where we find errors.

### At a club or party

- Handing drugs to a friend, even for free, is a transfer (Article 260²) — 10 to 15 years; selling — 12 to 20 years or life
- Searches and tests must follow the legal procedure — ask for a lawyer
- A person punished for drug use loses their driving licence for 3 years
- Anyone who voluntarily hands drugs over before an investigation starts, reporting it in writing or by phone, is released from criminal liability

Our services:
- Defence in cocaine, ecstasy and amphetamine cases
- Checking the forensic examination and amount
- Keeping or transfer — the right classification
- Lawfulness of the search and seizure
- New psychoactive substance cases
- Defending foreigners, with an interpreter

### How many grams of cocaine is a crime?
Up to 0.06 g is a small amount — an administrative case. Above 0.06 g it's a criminal case, above 0.6 g a large amount (5 to 8 years), above 2 g especially large (8 to 20 years or life).

### How many ecstasy pills count as a large amount?
A large amount is 0.5 g of MDMA, and the MDMA content of a pill varies — the forensic examination establishes it. So even a few pills can count as a large amount.

### How much 'spice' is a crime?
Any amount of a new psychoactive substance is a crime — up to 6 years in prison.

### I'm a foreigner — what happens?
The rules are the same. You have the right to an interpreter and a lawyer; don't sign anything you don't understand. We work in English and Russian.

## Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/freelancer-tax-georgia/

If you live in Georgia and work remotely for foreign clients or a foreign company, the money comes from abroad, but the income is taxed in Georgia. We help you choose the right route, register and file returns — without overpaying tax or penalties.

Under Article 104 of the Tax Code, services performed in Georgia and employment carried out in Georgia are Georgian-source income. It doesn't matter where the money arrives — on Upwork, Payoneer or a foreign bank. So money received from abroad is not tax-free.
A foreign company does not withhold tax in Georgia. If you are not registered, you must report the income in an annual return by 31 March of the following year and pay 20% (Articles 81 and 153). Registering as a sole trader with small business status — 1% — is often cheaper.

### Your options

| Option | Tax | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| Not registered | 20%, annual return by 31 March | No return — a penalty plus interest |
| Sole trader with small business status | 1% up to GEL 500,000, 3% above | A return every month, by the 15th of the following month |
| Employee of a foreign company (employment contract) | Salary — 20% | The 1% doesn't apply to salary |

### Small business status — what to watch for

- The 1% covers business income only, not salary (Article 90). If you work for one company with fixed hours and under its direction, it may be treated as salary
- Consulting, legal, medical, audit, architecture and some other activities can't use the 1% (Government Resolution No. 415)
- If annual income passes GEL 500,000, all income is taxed at 3% from that month until the end of the year
- Services to foreign businesses are generally outside Georgian VAT — the place of supply is where the client is (Article 162¹)
- Pensions: an employee of a foreign employer and a sole trader count as self-employed — joining the pension scheme is voluntary

### For companies: an employee who lives abroad

- An employment contract longer than 1 month must be in writing; state that the work is done remotely from abroad (Labour Code, Articles 12 and 14)
- Services a non-resident performs abroad are not Georgian-source income, so as a rule no tax is withheld; the exception is management and financial services — 10%
- How the salary of an employee working abroad is taxed depends on the details — we check it in advance, together with any double tax treaty
- A foreigner who never enters Georgia and works fully remotely doesn't need the right to work (Labour Migration Law, Article 1)
- The pension scheme doesn't cover foreigners without a permanent residence permit in Georgia

Our services:
- Assessing your tax — 20% or 1%
- Registering as a sole trader with small business status
- Choosing the right activity
- Monthly and annual tax returns
- For companies — contracts and tax for remote staff abroad
- Disputes with the Revenue Service

### Do I pay tax on money from Upwork or Fiverr?
Yes, if you do the work in Georgia. As a sole trader with small business status — 1%; unregistered — 20% through an annual return.

### How do I register as a sole trader?
At the Public Service Hall, with your ID and an address. Then you apply for small business status to the Revenue Service on rs.ge.

### What is the 1% limit?
GEL 500,000 a year. Above it, all income is taxed at 3% from that month to the end of the year; if you exceed it 2 years in a row, the status is cancelled.

### Can a foreign salary be taxed at 1%?
No. Salary is excluded from the 1%. If you genuinely provide services rather than work as an employee, the contract must show it — we review the contract.

### What if I don't file the annual return?
The penalty is 5% of the tax, 10% if more than 2 months late, plus interest of 0.05% per day.

### Do we withhold tax for a remote employee living abroad?
For services performed abroad, as a rule, no; for management and financial services — 10%. Salary depends on the details — contact us before signing the contract.

## Criminal record certificate in Georgia — fee, apostille
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/criminal-record-certificate-georgia/

Georgian criminal record certificates (police clearance) are issued by the Service Agency of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. You may need one for a job, a visa or abroad. We help obtain it, apostille it and — if it shows a conviction — have the record expunged or removed.

The certificate shows information on convictions and on whether the person is wanted (MIA Order No. 892, Article 15). It is issued to the person, to someone else with their written consent, or to a representative with a power of attorney. You can order it online on the Service Agency's website or app, or at any Agency branch.
The fee is GEL 20 and it takes 3 working days; in 1 day it costs GEL 40. An apostille costs GEL 20 (5 working days) or GEL 50 in 1 day; translation is GEL 20 per page. A separate certificate on expunged or removed convictions costs GEL 30.

### At a glance

| Service | Fee | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Criminal record certificate | GEL 20 | 3 working days |
| Certificate — urgent | GEL 40 | 1 working day |
| Apostille | GEL 20 | 5 working days |
| Apostille — urgent | GEL 50 | 1 working day |
| Translation | GEL 20 per page | — |
| Certificate on expunged or removed convictions | GEL 30 | — |

### Good to know

- The certificate is valid for 15 calendar days — order it when you actually need it
- For use abroad, it usually needs an apostille and a translation
- If you are abroad, a representative can collect it with a power of attorney
- If it shows a conviction, we check whether it has expired and whether it can be removed early

### For foreigners

The general residence permit rules (Government Resolution No. 520) don't require a criminal record certificate from your home country — the Agency checks the information itself. A permit can be refused if you are wanted or have a conviction in Georgia. If you lived in Georgia, you can get a Georgian certificate — for example, for a visa or a job in another country.

Our services:
- Requesting the certificate under a power of attorney
- Apostille and translation for use abroad
- Checking whether a conviction has expired
- Early removal of a conviction
