- Correcting errors in the certificate
- Certificates for foreigners — residence and visas

### How do I get a criminal record certificate online?
On the MIA Service Agency website or app, after registering. It costs GEL 20 and takes 3 working days.

### How long is the certificate valid?
15 calendar days.

### Can someone else get it for me?
Yes — with your written consent or a power of attorney.

### The certificate shows an old conviction — what can I do?
We check whether it has expired. If not, it may be possible to have it removed early through the court.

## Does Georgia extradite? Extradition lawyer in Tbilisi
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/extradition-from-georgia/

If another country asks for your extradition, the first days decide everything — the deadlines are 7 and 10 days. We defend people in extradition cases in Georgia from the moment of arrest to the Supreme Court and the Minister's decision — in English, Russian and Georgian.

A Georgian citizen cannot be handed over to another state except where an international treaty provides for it (Constitution, Article 32). A foreigner can be extradited if the act is a crime in both countries and carries at least 1 year in prison (Law on International Cooperation in Criminal Matters, Article 18).
A court first rules on whether extradition is allowed; the final decision is made by the Minister of Justice. Georgia does extradite in some cases, including to Russia — every case is decided on its own facts, so the defence must start on day one.

### Steps and deadlines

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Arrest | Within 48 hours the prosecutor asks a magistrate judge for a preventive measure |
| Appealing detention | Within 7 days to the Court of Appeals; decision within 5 days |
| Extradition detention | 3 months, extendable by 3 months twice — 9 months at most; bail is possible |
| Court ruling on whether extradition is allowed | City court, hearing within 7 days; appeal to the Supreme Court within 7 days |
| Final decision | The Minister of Justice — who can still refuse on humanitarian grounds |
| Asylum application | Within 10 calendar days of being informed; decided within 1 month |

### When extradition is refused

- Political or military offences (Articles 19 and 20)
- Persecution because of race, nationality, religion or political views
- A real risk of torture or inhuman treatment
- The death penalty in the requesting state
- A conviction in absentia without a guaranteed retrial
- Limitation period, amnesty or pardon
- A Georgian decision already exists on the same act
- Asylum or international protection in Georgia
- Humanitarian reasons — being a minor, health

### Treaties

Georgia is a party to the European Convention on Extradition, as are the UK, Ukraine and Russia; with Belarus and Kazakhstan the 1993 Minsk Convention applies. For a state with no treaty, such as the US, extradition needs a separate agreement for the individual case.

### Simplified extradition — be careful

If you consent to being handed over, it happens within weeks, consent cannot be withdrawn, and you lose the protection that limits prosecution to the offences in the request. Talk to a lawyer before you consent.

Our services:
- Defence at the extradition arrest and detention hearing
- Appeals to the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court
- Arguing the grounds for refusal — political persecution, risk of torture
- Filing for asylum within the deadline
- Submissions to the Minister of Justice
- Defence in English, Russian and Georgian

### Does Georgia extradite to the US?
There is no extradition treaty in force between Georgia and the US that we know of; extradition then needs a separate agreement for the individual case, and every refusal ground still applies. Georgian citizens are not extradited.

### Does Georgia extradite to the UK?
Yes, it can — both are parties to the European Convention on Extradition. A court reviews each request, and the grounds for refusal apply.

### Is Georgia a non-extradition country?
No. Georgia does extradite foreigners in some cases, including to Russia; only its own citizens are protected. Each case turns on the treaty, the charge and the refusal grounds.

### How long can I be held pending extradition?
Up to 9 months in total — 3 months, extendable twice. Bail or another milder measure is possible.

## Legal help for foreigners in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/

Moving to Georgia, buying property, starting a business or facing a legal problem here? We advise foreigners in English and Russian — at our Tbilisi office or remotely.

### Can I work with you remotely?
Yes. Most matters are handled online and by phone; where a signature is needed in Georgia, we can act for you under a notarised power of attorney.

### Do you work in English and Russian?
Yes. Consultations, documents and correspondence are available in Georgian, English and Russian.

### Do my foreign documents need an apostille?
It depends on the country: documents from some countries need an apostille, others need consular legalisation, and documents from some countries need no extra certification at all. A certified Georgian translation is usually required. We'll tell you what your documents need.

## Criminal defense lawyer for foreigners
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/criminal-defense-for-foreigners/

When a foreigner faces a criminal case in Georgia, language and unfamiliar procedure are the first obstacles. We defend you in English or Russian — from the moment of arrest to trial.

If you are detained, you have the right to a lawyer, to a free interpreter and to have your country's consulate informed. Do not sign documents you don't understand — ask for your lawyer first.
We act at every stage: questioning, preventive measures (including bail or detention), plea agreements, trial and appeal. We also keep family members abroad informed.

- Defense from the moment of arrest
- Interpreter and contact with your consulate
- Challenging bail or detention
- Plea agreements
- Defense at trial and on appeal
- Keeping your family abroad informed

### I'm a foreigner and was detained in Georgia. What are my rights?
You have the right to remain silent, to a lawyer before any questioning, to a free interpreter and to have your consulate informed. Ask for a lawyer immediately and don't sign anything you don't understand.

### Will my consulate be informed?
Yes, if you ask. A detained foreigner has the right to request that the consulate of their country be informed of the detention.

### Can my family hire a lawyer from abroad?
Yes. A family member can contact us by phone or WhatsApp; we sign the engagement remotely and step into the case immediately.

## Immigration lawyer in Tbilisi — entry bans, deportation
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/immigration-lawyer-georgia/

When you are turned away at the border, have overstayed or face deportation, time is very short. We act from day one — in English or Russian, in Georgia or remotely.

In immigration cases deadlines are counted in days: a deportation decision can be appealed in court within 10 days of being served. So the first step is to get a copy of the decision and understand exactly what it is based on.
Often an appeal is not the only answer: we look for a lawful basis to stay — the right type of residence permit, a family tie or another route — and at the same time protect your property, job and family interests.

- Appealing a refusal of entry at the border
- Help after an overstay: the fine, the entry ban and next steps
- Deportation cases and the interview at the Ministry
- Court hearings on placement in the temporary accommodation centre
- Appealing a residence-permit refusal
- A new application on the right basis

### How many days do I have to appeal a deportation decision?
10 days from when it is served. Contact a lawyer right away.

### Can you handle my case if I'm already abroad?
Yes. We act under a power of attorney and keep you informed at every step.

### Does paying the overstay fine cancel the entry ban?
No. For an overstay, the fine and the entry ban are imposed together.

## Buying property in Georgia as a foreigner
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/buying-property-in-georgia/

Foreigners can buy apartments, houses and non-agricultural land in Georgia on the same terms as Georgians. We check the property, prepare the contract and register your ownership — even if you are abroad.

The purchase itself is quick: ownership arises once it is registered with the Public Registry. The risks are elsewhere — a mortgage or seizure on the property, a seller without full authority, or a developer of a new build without the right permits.
If you can't come to Georgia, you can buy through a notarised power of attorney. Depending on the country, documents issued abroad may need an apostille or consular legalisation (documents from some countries need neither) and a certified Georgian translation — we tell you exactly what to prepare.

### Step by step

1. A Public Registry extract: who the owner is and whether there is a mortgage, seizure or ban.
2. Checking the seller: full authority, any co-owners, and whether they are on the debtors' register — if so, selling the property is restricted.
3. The contract: price, payment terms and dates, condition of the property, handover and each side's liability.
4. Payment through a bank, not in cash — the amount must match the contract.
5. Registration in the Public Registry — ownership arises from the moment of registration.

### New builds: what we check

- The building permit and the construction stage
- The developer's rights to the land and any mortgage on it
- The handover date, penalties and refund terms in the contract
- The risk of one flat being sold to two buyers

### Costs and taxes

When buying, you pay the Public Registry registration fee. An individual seller who has owned a flat or house for more than 2 years pays no income tax on the gain from the sale (Tax Code, Article 82).

- Checking title, mortgages and seizures
- Checking developers and permits for new builds
- Purchase, preliminary and lease agreements
- Buying by power of attorney while you're abroad
- Registering ownership in the Public Registry
- Advice on residence permits based on property

### Can foreigners buy property in Georgia?
Yes. Foreign individuals and companies can buy apartments, houses, commercial premises and non-agricultural land. Agricultural land is restricted for foreigners, with limited exceptions set by law.

### Does buying property give me a residence permit?
Owning property can be a basis for a short-term residence permit if its value meets the threshold set by law (since 1 March 2026 — more than USD 150,000). The permit is not automatic — you have to apply for it.

### Can I buy property without coming to Georgia?
Yes. You can give a notarised power of attorney (with an apostille if the country requires it) to your lawyer or a trusted person, who signs and registers the purchase for you.

### Who pays tax when an apartment is bought?
The buyer pays the Public Registry registration fee. An individual seller who has owned the flat for more than 2 years pays no income tax on the gain from the sale.

### Can I buy a flat in Georgia without residence or citizenship?
Yes. A foreigner can buy a flat, house or non-agricultural land without a residence permit or Georgian citizenship. Only agricultural land is restricted.

### Buying an apartment in Batumi off-plan — what should I check?
That the developer owns the land in the Public Registry and the land isn't mortgaged; the construction permit and the number of floors allowed; the developer's finished projects and court cases. Pay in stages tied to construction, and make sure the contract sets a completion date and a penalty for delay. We check all of this before you pay.

## Disputes with property developers in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/disputes-with-developers/

When you buy a flat in a new build, the biggest risk is the developer. We help buyers — including foreigners — get their flat or their money back, through negotiation or in court.

Typical problems are missed completion dates, a flat that differs from the contract, a mortgage on the land or the project, the same flat sold to several people, and an insolvent developer. Each needs a different approach.
First we review the contract, the payments, the Public Registry records and the building permits. Then we choose the strategy: negotiation, a claim for the contractual penalty and damages, terminating the contract and recovering the money, securing the claim — for example, by freezing property — or filing a claim in the developer's insolvency.

- Checking the contract and the developer before you sign
- Claiming the penalty when completion is late
- Terminating the contract and recovering your money
- Disputes over a mortgage or seizure on the flat or land
- Disputes when one flat was sold to two buyers
- Claims when the developer is insolvent

### The developer is late — what can I do?
Depending on the contract, you can claim the penalty, damages, or terminate the contract and get your money back. We start by reviewing the contract.

### Can you handle this while I live abroad?
Yes. We act for you under a power of attorney — in negotiations and in court.

### What should I do before paying for a flat?
Check the developer, the landowner, mortgages and permits, and have a lawyer read the contract. It is the cheapest protection there is.

## How to register a business in Georgia as a foreigner
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/company-registration-in-georgia/

Foreigners can own 100% of a Georgian company and run it from abroad. We register LLCs, branches and individual entrepreneurs, prepare corporate documents and support you with banks, contracts and tax registration.

Registration with the Public Registry is fast — usually one business day once the documents are ready. You need a legal address in Georgia; there is no minimum share capital for an LLC.
Georgia taxes companies on distributed profit (the "Estonian model"), and individual entrepreneurs may qualify for small-business status with a 1% turnover tax. Eligibility depends on the activity and turnover, so we check it before you register.

### Prices

| Service | You are in Georgia | You are abroad |
|---|---|---|
| Company (LLC) registration | 1 800 ₾ | 2 700 ₾ |
| Virtual business address | 500 ₾ / year | 500 ₾ / year |
| Personal bank account | 700 ₾ | 1 050 ₾ |
| Business bank account | 1 000 ₾ | 1 500 ₾ |
| Both accounts together | 1 500 ₾ | 2 250 ₾ |

- Prices are final and include VAT; state fees (at the Public Service Hall) are paid separately
- All prices are one-time except the address; the virtual address is yearly and needed only if you have no property in Georgia
- If you are not in Georgia, we need a copy of your passport with an apostille or notarised — depending on your country — and a power of attorney
- A business account usually requires a personal account first

### Bank accounts — what to know

A bank can refuse to open an account at any time and without giving a reason. We prepare the documents and help you through the whole process, but no one can guarantee that an account will be opened — including us.

- LLC, branch and representative office registration
- Virtual business address
- Individual entrepreneur and small-business status
- Charter and shareholder agreements
- Help with opening a bank account
- Commercial and employment contracts
- Labour disputes of foreign employees
- Changes, share transfers and liquidation

### How much does company registration cost?
1 800 ₾ if you are in Georgia and 2 700 ₾ if registration is done remotely. The price is final and includes VAT; state fees are paid separately.

### Do you guarantee the bank will open an account?
No. The bank decides and can refuse even without giving a reason. We prepare the documents and help make your application as complete as possible.

### Can a foreigner own 100% of a company in Georgia?
Yes. Foreign individuals and companies can be the sole founder and director of a Georgian LLC.

### Do I need to be in Georgia to register a company?
Not necessarily. Registration can be done through a representative with a notarised power of attorney. Opening a bank account usually needs more preparation, as each bank runs its own checks.

### How are companies taxed in Georgia?
Profit tax (15%) is generally paid only when profit is distributed, for example as dividends. Small-business status for individual entrepreneurs offers a 1% turnover tax up to an annual limit. We check which regime fits your activity.

## Work permit and sole trader status for foreigners in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/work-permit-and-sole-trader/

Since 1 March 2026, foreigners need the right to labour activity to work or do business in Georgia. We check whether it applies to you and sort out your status — from the permit to your taxes.

The rule covers both employees and the self-employed — including individual entrepreneurs. Along with the right to work you need a suitable residence permit or a D1 visa, and you can only apply while you are lawfully in Georgia. Foreigners with a permanent residence permit are not covered.
With small business status, tax is 1% of income if annual income does not exceed GEL 500,000. But not every activity qualifies, and working without the right to work can even be a ground for deportation — so we plan everything together.

- Assessing whether you need the right to work
- Applying for the right to labour activity
- The right residence permit or visa
- Registering as an individual entrepreneur and choosing the right activity
- Small business status and monthly declarations
- Appealing refusals and fines

### Do individual entrepreneurs need the right to work?
Yes. A self-employed foreigner, including an individual entrepreneur, needs it to work in Georgia.

### Who is not covered by the rule?
For example, foreigners with a permanent residence permit. We check other exemptions for your case.

### What happens if annual income exceeds GEL 500,000?
From the start of that month until the end of the year, all income is taxed at 3%.

## Residence permit in Georgia — lawyer for foreigners
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/residence-permit-in-georgia/

We prepare and file residence permit applications for foreigners in Georgia, follow them through the Public Service Hall and appeal refusals.

Citizens of many countries can stay in Georgia visa-free for up to a year, but living, working or doing business here long-term usually requires a residence permit. The right type depends on your situation: work, business, property ownership, family, study or investment.
Refusals often come with little explanation. A carefully prepared application avoids most of them — and if you are refused, the decision can be challenged within short deadlines.

### Residence through property and investment

| Type | Condition | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Short-term (property) | Real estate with a market value above USD 150,000 (since 1 March 2026; agricultural land doesn't count) | 1 year, renewable for 1 year each time; you must keep the property |
| Investment | An investment of at least USD 300,000 or real estate worth over USD 300,000; for an investment, annual turnover of USD 50,000–120,000 | 5 years; no separate work permit needed |
| Permanent | After 5 years of investment residence — with final-year turnover of at least USD 120,000 or 5 years of property ownership | Indefinite |

### Renewal — deadlines

- Apply to renew no earlier than 90 days before expiry
- Apply for a new permit at least 40 days before your lawful stay ends
- Staying on an expired permit is an overstay — a fine, and if unpaid, a risk of being refused entry
- If you are abroad, you can apply to renew online

### Processing time and fees

| Processing | Fee |
|---|---|
| Within 30 days | 300 GEL |
| Within 20 days | 450 GEL |
| Within 10 days | 600 GEL |

These fees apply to work, study, investment, family and short-term permits (Public Service Hall tariff from 1 September 2026). IT permit — 500/750/1,000 GEL; spouse of a Georgian citizen — 500 GEL, decided within 90 days. A refusal can be challenged in court within 10 calendar days.

- Choosing the right type of residence permit
- Preparing and filing the application
- Work and business residence permits
- Permits based on property or investment
- Family reunification
- Appeals against refusals

### How long does a residence permit application take?
Standard — 30 days (300 GEL). Expedited — 20 days (450 GEL) or 10 days (600 GEL). An application by a Georgian citizen's spouse — up to 90 days.

### Can a refusal be appealed?
Yes — in court, within 10 calendar days of receiving the decision. The deadline is very short, so contact us as soon as you are refused.

### Do I need a work permit to work in Georgia?
Since 1 March 2026, foreigners need the right to labour activity to work or do business in Georgia — except holders of a permanent residence permit and other cases set by law. We'll check what applies to you before you start work.

### How long can I stay without a visa?
Citizens of listed countries — a full year; others — 90 days in any 180. The old 'Remotely from Georgia' digital-nomad programme is not currently active — for a longer stay you need a residence permit.

## Family lawyer for foreigners in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/family-law-for-foreigners/

Family cases with an international element follow their own rules. We help with divorce, child residence and alimony, and the recognition of foreign court decisions — in English or Russian.

Which country's court is competent and which country's law applies depends on where the marriage was registered and where the spouses and children live — so we assess that first.
Georgia is a party to the Hague Convention on international child abduction, and foreign court decisions are recognised by the Supreme Court of Georgia. Depending on the country, documents issued abroad may need an apostille or consular legalisation (documents from some countries need neither) and a certified Georgian translation.

- Divorce with an international element
- Child residence and contact arrangements
- Alimony, including from a parent living abroad
- Recognition of foreign court decisions
- Returning a child after international abduction (Hague Convention)
- Legalisation and translation of family documents

### Can foreigners divorce in Georgia?
Often yes — especially if the marriage was registered in Georgia or one spouse lives here. Which court is competent and which country's law applies depends on the case, so get advice first.

### Is a foreign court decision valid in Georgia?
Before it can be enforced, a foreign court decision generally has to be recognised in Georgia. Recognition is handled by the Supreme Court of Georgia; we prepare the application and the translated documents.

### What if the other parent took our child abroad?
If a child has been wrongfully removed to or kept in a country that is party to the Hague Convention, you can ask for the child's return. Act quickly — time is critical in these cases.

## IT companies in Georgia: virtual zone, 5% tax, 1%
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/it-companies-in-georgia/

Georgia has no separate immigration law for IT, but it has three tax regimes that IT specialists and companies use. We help you choose the right one, register, obtain the status and sort out the right to work.

A sole trader with small business status pays 1% of turnover — the simplest route for a freelancer. A virtual zone person is an IT company whose profit from supplying the IT it creates outside Georgia is exempt from profit tax. An international company pays 5% profit tax, its employees' salaries are taxed at 5%, and dividends are not taxed.
For comparison: the standard profit tax is 15% (on distributed profit), and personal income is taxed at 20%.

### The three regimes at a glance

|   | Sole trader 1% | Virtual zone | International company |
|---|---|---|---|
| For | Freelancers | IT company (LLC) | IT company with a team |
| Tax | 1% of turnover | 0% on supplies abroad | 5% profit, 5% salaries |
| Granted by | Revenue Service | Financial-Analytical Service | Government of Georgia |
| Timing | — | 10 working days | By government ordinance |

### Virtual zone person

- Only for legal entities — a sole trader can't get this status
- Apply online on the Ministry of Finance website; status within 10 working days, certificate within 2 more
- Profit from IT supplied abroad is not taxed; supplies within Georgia are taxed as usual
- No licences or permits are needed for the activity
- What counts as a 'supply abroad' is checked by the Revenue Service under its own practice — contracts should be reviewed in advance

### International company

- At least 2 years of experience in a permitted IT activity — of the company itself, the foreign company it represents, or shareholders holding over 50%
- The work must really be done in Georgia: qualified staff and operating costs
- Apply to the Revenue Service; the Government decides; the status has no end date
- Other income must not exceed 2% of income from permitted activities in a year
- If these conditions are broken, the status is cancelled from the date it was granted — so tax is recalculated for the whole period

### The right to work — from 2026

Since 1 March 2026, a foreigner working in Georgia as a sole trader or employee also needs the right to work — and a suitable residence permit or visa. Registering a company or a sole trader alone is no longer enough. The rule does not apply to holders of a permanent residence permit.

- Choosing a regime: sole trader, virtual zone or international company
- Registering an LLC or sole trader
- Obtaining virtual zone status
- Preparing the international company application
- Right to work and residence permit
- Disputes with the Revenue Service

### Which is better — a 1% sole trader or the virtual zone?
For a freelancer working alone, the 1% sole trader is the simplest. The virtual zone is for companies and makes sense when you mainly supply IT abroad and plan to distribute profit. The right choice depends on income, clients and plans.

### Can a newly formed company get international company status?
Yes, if the 2 years of IT experience belong to the foreign company it represents, or to shareholder companies holding over 50%. The work must still really be done in Georgia.

### How long does virtual zone status take?
No later than 10 working days from the application, and the certificate within 2 working days of the status being granted.

### Is registering as a sole trader enough to work in Georgia?
Not since 1 March 2026. You also need the right to work and a suitable residence permit or visa.

## Gambling licence in Georgia — casino, betting, online
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/gambling-licence-georgia/

In Georgia, organising any game of chance or prize game — from a casino to online betting — requires a permit issued by the Revenue Service. Permits are issued only to businesses registered in Georgia. We help register the company, choose and obtain the right permit, and then comply with the permit conditions.

Permits are needed for casinos, slot halls, gambling clubs, betting (totalisator), lotto, bingo, promotional draws and their online forms, and for supplying games to other operators. Operating without a permit or breaching permit conditions leads to sanctions.
For online casinos and slot games, one permit covers only one website on one domain name. There are also separate 'international' online permits — Georgian citizens may not take part in games run under them.

### Key conditions

- The Revenue Service issues permits and supervises operators; inspections can happen at any time during the year
- Permits are issued only to businesses registered in Georgia — a foreign company needs a Georgian company
- A casino must have at least 5 gaming tables
- Gambling is not allowed in children's, medical and educational institutions, places of worship, libraries, museums, government buildings or zones banned by the municipality

### Player checks

- Georgian citizens under 25 and foreigners under 18 may not play — the operator must check age against an ID document
- People on the dependent or banned persons lists may not be admitted; the Revenue Service gives operators this information
- Information collected about players is kept for 5 years and is confidential

- Choosing the permit type — land-based, online or international
- Registering a Georgian company for a foreign investor
- Preparing the permit application for the Revenue Service
- Setting up age and list checks for players
- Representation during inspections and appeals against fines
- Contracts with game suppliers and partners

### Can a foreign company get a permit?
Not directly. Permits are issued only to businesses registered in Georgia, so a Georgian company has to be registered first — we can handle that.

### What is an 'international' online permit?
It is an online casino, slots or betting permit under which Georgian citizens may not be admitted to play.

### How many websites does one online permit cover?
For online casino and slot games, one permit covers only one website on one domain name.

## Georgian citizenship for foreigners — how to get it
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/georgian-citizenship-for-foreigners/

A foreigner can become a Georgian citizen in several ways — through residence, marriage, birth in Georgia or an exceptional grant. The President of Georgia decides; applications go to the Public Service Development Agency or a consulate. We choose the right route for you, prepare the documents and defend your interests if you are refused.

Since a 2025 amendment, the ordinary route requires lawful, continuous residence in Georgia for the last 10 years (it used to be 5). Residence stops being continuous if you spend more than 90 days in total abroad in a year — study (up to 2 years) and medical treatment don't count.
Georgia allows dual citizenship only as an exception. For ordinary or marriage-based grants, the decree takes effect only once you prove you have given up your other citizenship. Keeping your own citizenship is possible with an exceptional grant.

### Routes to citizenship

| Route | Conditions | Dual citizenship |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary route (Article 12) | Lawful, continuous residence for the last 10 years; knowledge of Georgian, Georgian history and basic law; a job, real estate, a business or a share in a Georgian company | No — you must give up your citizenship |
| Marriage to a Georgian citizen (Article 14) | Lawful, continuous residence in Georgia for the last 5 years; language, history and law tests | No — you must give up your citizenship |
| Exceptional grant (Article 17) | Special merit or state interest: a significant investment, success in sport, science or art, or Georgian roots | Yes |
| People born in Georgia (Articles 30², 31¹) | A person born in Georgia who doesn't meet the Article 30² conditions, with the language and history/law tests; open until 1 January 2027 | Needs to be checked case by case |

### How the process works

1. The language, history and basic law tests are taken before applying; a pass is valid for 1 year.
2. You apply to the Public Service Development Agency or a Georgian consulate abroad — in person or through a representative.
3. The Agency and the Citizenship Commission review the application and the President decides — within 3 months.
4. On being granted citizenship, you take an oath of loyalty in Georgian.

### When applications are refused

Grounds for refusal include involvement in international or especially grave crimes, state security interests, being wanted, or extradition proceedings. After a refusal you can reapply on the same ground after 6 months. Following a 2025 Constitutional Court decision, a refusal can also be challenged in court.

- Choosing the right route to citizenship
- Checking your residence period and continuity
- Preparing and filing documents with the Agency or a consulate
- Exceptional-grant applications — for investors and people of Georgian origin
- Citizenship for people born in Georgia before 2027
- Challenging a refusal

### How many years must I live in Georgia to get citizenship?
By the ordinary route — the last 10 years, lawfully and continuously. The spouse of a Georgian citizen — 5 years. A stateless person with status — 5 years.

### Can I keep my own citizenship (dual citizenship)?
Only with an exceptional grant. Through the ordinary route or marriage you must give up your previous citizenship.

### My father is Georgian — am I entitled to citizenship?
If a parent was a Georgian citizen when you were born, you are a citizen by birth. For adults, Georgian roots count only for an exceptional grant.

### I was born in Georgia in the Soviet era — what can I get?
Special rules apply to people born in Georgia, but only until 1 January 2027. The conditions depend on your date of birth, your situation in 1993 and whether you hold another citizenship — contact us in good time.

### How long does the decision take?
By law — 3 months. The President makes the decision.

## Marriage in Georgia for foreigners — requirements
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/marriage-in-georgia-for-foreigners/

Foreigners can register a marriage in Georgia — with a Georgian citizen or with each other, if they are in the country lawfully. There is no mandatory waiting period: a marriage is often registered on the day of application. We prepare the documents, translations and apostilles so you can use the marriage certificate in your own country.

Marriage is a union of a woman and a man, and it has legal effect only once registered with the Public Service Development Agency (Public Service Hall) — a religious ceremony alone does not create a marriage. The minimum age is 18.
The conditions of marriage are governed for each party by the law of their own country, and the form by Georgian law (Law on Private International Law, Article 44). That is why we check in advance whether your country has extra requirements.

### Who cannot marry

- Someone already married to another person
- Close relatives — parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, siblings
- Adoptive parent and adopted child
- Two people of the same sex — a same-sex marriage registered abroad has no legal effect in Georgia

### Documents you need

- Passport — with a notarised Georgian translation
- If previously married — proof of divorce or of the spouse's death, apostilled and translated
- Every document issued abroad needs an apostille (or consular legalisation) and a certified translation
- 2 adult witnesses at the registration

### How registration works

1. You file the application at the Public Service Hall — in person or through a representative. The application is valid for 2 months.
2. The marriage is registered at the time stated in the application — often the same day. Same-day registration can be refused when the office is busy.
3. Both spouses must attend in person with 2 witnesses — you cannot marry through a representative.
4. The marriage certificate is issued in Georgian. To use it abroad, it needs an apostille and a translation.

### Recognition abroad

- A marriage registered in Georgia is generally valid in other countries — unless their law has an impediment to the marriage
- Russia treats such a marriage as valid without re-registration (RF Family Code, Article 158)
- The certificate needs an apostille (at the Public Service Hall, also electronically) and a notarised translation
- For Germany and other EU countries an apostille is enough — no consular legalisation

### New rules from 2026

- Since 1 July 2026, a fictitious marriage is a crime (Criminal Code, Article 344³): marriage between a Georgian citizen and a foreigner to obtain citizenship or residence. Penalty — up to 2 years in prison; for the foreigner, expulsion and an entry ban of 2 to 10 years
- Since 1 September 2026, the spouse of a Georgian citizen first gets a temporary permit — for 1 year, then 2 years at a time, up to 5 years; after that, permanent residence if the marriage continues
- An interagency commission interviews the spouses together and separately and may inspect the home; refusing to cooperate is a ground for refusal

- Checking marriage conditions under your country's law
- Translating, apostilling and preparing documents
- Planning the registration at the Public Service Hall
- Apostilling the marriage certificate for use abroad
- Prenuptial (marriage) agreement
- Residence permit based on marriage

### Can two foreigners marry in Georgia?
Yes, if both are in Georgia lawfully. There is no citizenship requirement.

### How quickly can we get married?
There is no mandatory waiting period. The marriage is registered at the time stated in the application — often the same day.

### Will our marriage be recognised in our country?
Many countries recognise a marriage concluded abroad under local law. The certificate needs an apostille and a translation. The exact recognition rules depend on your country's law — we check them in advance.

### Is a church wedding enough?
No. Only a marriage registered by the state has legal effect.

### Is a marriage in Georgia recognised in Russia?
Yes. Under Article 158 of the RF Family Code, a marriage concluded abroad under local law is valid in Russia without re-registration. The certificate needs an apostille and a notarised Russian translation.

### Is a Georgian marriage valid in Germany, Italy or the UK?
Generally yes — a marriage validly concluded in Georgia is recognised if your home country's law has no impediment, for example an earlier marriage. You will need the certificate with an apostille and a certified translation; some countries let you, or require you to, record the marriage with the local registry office.

## Driving in Georgia on a foreign licence — the rules
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/driving-licence-georgia-foreigners/

A foreigner can drive in Georgia on their national licence, but not indefinitely — for 1 year from their last entry. After that you need to exchange it for a Georgian licence or get a Georgian one. We help prepare the documents and defend you in fine and driving-ban cases.

You can drive on a foreign licence until it expires, but for no more than 1 year from your last entry into Georgia. If the licence isn't in Latin or Georgian letters, you also need a certified translation. A residence permit doesn't change this period.
After the year, driving on a foreign licence can count as driving without a licence — a GEL 500 fine, and within a year repeatedly, GEL 1,500 or up to 15 days' administrative detention (Administrative Offences Code, Article 121).

### Exchanging a foreign licence

- No exam needed — exchange the licence before it expires
- Apply to the MIA Service Agency — in person
- You need: an application, passport or residence card, the foreign licence, a confirmation from the issuing country with an apostille or legalisation, a medical certificate and payment of the fee
- The issuing country's confirmation must be no older than 90 days when submitted
- The foreign licence loses its force and is handed to the Agency
- The category must match the 1949 Geneva or 1968 Vienna Conventions or EU rules

### Getting a Georgian licence

- Theory and practical exams; for category B from age 18 a driving school is not compulsory
- Since 27 May 2025 foreigners are admitted to the exam with a residence card or proof of at least 185 days' lawful stay in Georgia in the last 12 months
- Besides Georgian, the theory test is available in English, Russian, Turkish, Azerbaijani and Armenian

- Documents and apostille for exchanging a foreign licence
- Checking the conditions for a Georgian licence
- Appealing a fine for driving without a licence
- Suspension and withdrawal of driving rights
- Traffic accident cases
- Translating and legalising documents

### Can I drive in Georgia on my own country's licence?
Yes — until it expires, but for no more than 1 year from your last entry into Georgia. A licence not in Latin or Georgian letters needs a certified translation.

### Do I have to take an exam to exchange my licence?
No. The exchange is done without an exam if the licence is valid and you submit the issuing country's confirmation.

### What is the fine for driving without a licence?
GEL 500; repeatedly within a year — GEL 1,500 or up to 15 days' administrative detention.

### In which languages is the theory test available?
Besides Georgian — English, Russian, Turkish, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Abkhaz and Ossetian.

## Opening a bank account in Georgia as a foreigner
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/bank-account-in-georgia-for-foreigners/

A foreigner can open an account at a Georgian bank — sometimes with just a passport. But the bank must understand who you are and where your money comes from, and if it can't, it won't open the account. We prepare the documents, help you deal with the bank and open personal and business accounts.

Under Article 10 of the anti-money-laundering law, a bank must identify and verify the customer and the beneficial owner, the purpose of the relationship and the expected transactions. If it can't, opening the account is prohibited. For high-risk customers the bank also looks into the origin of funds.
That is why refusals often come without an explanation — and that is lawful. We can't promise that a bank will open an account — that is the bank's decision — but properly prepared documents greatly reduce the risk of refusal.

### What to expect

- Usually a passport and a Georgian mobile number; to complete registration you often need to visit a branch
- The bank may ask for documents on the source of income, your business and the purpose of the account
- Some products are available only to citizens of certain countries
- To open a business account you usually need a personal account first
- Remote identification is allowed by law, but not every bank offers it to every customer

### How to reduce the risk of refusal

1. Prepare proof of income — a contract, statements, a tax return.
2. Explain clearly what you need the account for and what transactions you expect.
3. For a business account, prepare the company documents and beneficial-owner information.
4. If one bank refuses, another may assess you differently.

### Deposits for foreigners

- A foreigner can open a deposit just like a Georgian citizen — in GEL, USD or EUR
- Deposits are insured up to GEL 50,000 per depositor per bank, rising to GEL 100,000 from 1 January 2027; payout in GEL within 20 calendar days
- Insurance covers all types of accounts and includes accrued interest
- Interest an individual receives from a bank is not taxed in Georgia (Tax Code, Article 131(5)) — check your home country's tax separately

- Preparing documents for the bank
- Opening a personal account
- Opening a business account for a company or sole trader
- Company registration and account together
- Representing you at the bank under a power of attorney
- Blocked accounts and disputes with banks

### Can a foreigner open an account at a Georgian bank?
Yes. At some banks a passport and a mobile number are enough, though you often need to visit a branch to complete registration.

### Why did the bank refuse me without a reason?
By law a bank must refuse if it can't complete its checks on the customer and the funds, and it doesn't have to explain in detail. Reapplying with the right documents, or at another bank, often succeeds.

### Can I open an account without coming to Georgia?
In some cases — through a power of attorney or remote identification, but it depends on the bank. Often you still need to visit once in person.

### How much does your service cost?
Our prices for opening accounts are listed on the company registration page.

### How much of my deposit is insured?
Up to GEL 50,000 per depositor per bank, rising to GEL 100,000 from 1 January 2027.

## Tax residency in Georgia — 183 days, certificate, HNWI
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/tax-residency-georgia/

You become a Georgian tax resident if you spend 183 days or more in Georgia in any continuous 12-month period. A resident individual's foreign-source income is not taxed in Georgia. We help confirm residency, obtain the certificate, apply for HNWI status and handle disputes with the Revenue Service.

Under Article 34 of the Tax Code, a person is resident for the whole tax year if they are in Georgia 183 days or more in any continuous 12 calendar months ending in that year. Any part of a day counts as a full day. Time abroad for treatment, holidays, business trips or study counts as time in Georgia. The status is determined separately for each year.
A resident individual's income from sources outside Georgia is exempt (Article 82(1)(f)). Income earned in Georgia is generally taxed at 20%, dividends at 5%, and interest from a licensed bank is not taxed (Article 131(5)).

### The residence certificate

- The Revenue Service issues it — you can also request it online
- Decision or certificate within 30 calendar days; up to 30 days to fix any defects
- On request, the Revenue Service sends the certificate directly to the foreign tax authority and signs the other country's form
- You need it for treaty relief, for banks and for CRS purposes

### High-net-worth individual (HNWI)

Residency can also be granted without 183 days to a high-net-worth individual (Article 34(6); Finance Minister Order No. 60 of 2023). The main conditions are assets above GEL 3,000,000 or income above GEL 200,000 in each of the last 3 years, property in Georgia worth at least USD 500,000 and, in addition, a residence permit or at least GEL 25,000 of Georgian-source income in the previous year. The status must be applied for again each tax year.

- Assessing residency and counting days
- Requesting the residence certificate from the Revenue Service
- HNWI status application
- Claiming relief under double tax treaties
- Tax planning for sole traders and companies
- Disputes with the Revenue Service

### Do I become resident automatically after 183 days?
Yes — 183 days in any continuous 12-month period ending in the tax year makes you resident for that whole year. The certificate, however, has to be requested separately.

### As a resident, do I pay Georgian tax on foreign income?
No. A resident individual's foreign-source income is exempt in Georgia. Your home country's law may see it differently — we check that separately.

### Is deposit interest taxed?
Interest an individual receives from a licensed financial institution, such as a bank, is not taxed and is not included in taxable income.

### How long does the certificate take?
Within 30 calendar days. If that isn't possible, the Revenue Service tells you the expected date.

### Is Georgia a tax haven? Will I still pay tax at home?
Georgian taxes are low and simple — 20% personal income tax, profit tax only when profit is distributed, 1% for small businesses, and no Georgian tax on a resident's foreign income or on bank interest. But Georgia is not a secrecy jurisdiction: it has double tax treaties (including with Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the UK) and exchanges financial account information under CRS. Whether you still owe tax at home depends on your home country's residency rules — leave residence there properly.

## Georgia double tax treaties — US, UK, Germany
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/double-tax-treaties-georgia/

If you are connected to two countries, both may try to tax your income. A double tax treaty decides which country taxes it and at what rate. Georgia has 58 such treaties. We help you claim treaty relief and prove your residency.

According to the Ministry of Finance's official list, Georgia has 58 double tax treaties in force — including with every EU country, the UK, Switzerland, Turkey, China, Israel and the UAE. The United States and Russia are not on that list.
If both countries treat you as resident, the treaty resolves it with a sequence of tests: permanent home, centre of vital interests, habitual abode, nationality and, finally, agreement between the two tax authorities.

### Withholding rates

| Country | Dividends | Interest and royalties |
|---|---|---|
| United Kingdom (2004, protocol 2010) | 0% (15% on dividends paid out of property income, e.g. by a REIT) | 0% |
| Germany (2006, protocol 2014) | 0% — company holding ≥50% with over €3m invested; 5% — ≥10% with over €100,000; otherwise 10% | 0% |

### The United States

Georgia's Ministry of Finance does not list a treaty with the US. However, the IRS states officially that the 1973 US–USSR treaty covers Georgia — a treaty much narrower than modern ones. Also, US citizens are taxed by the US on their worldwide income wherever they live, so Georgian tax residency does not end US tax obligations.

- Assessing which country taxes you
- Residence certificates and foreign forms
- Reclaiming tax withheld at source
- Resolving dual residency
- Planning tax on dividends, interest and royalties
- Disputes with the Revenue Service

### How many double tax treaties does Georgia have?
58 according to the Ministry of Finance, including with every EU country and the UK.

### Is there a US–Georgia tax treaty?
Not on Georgia's list, but the IRS considers the 1973 US–USSR treaty to apply to Georgia. In any case, US citizens are taxed by the US on worldwide income.

### How do I use a treaty?
You need a residence certificate from the country where you are resident. The Georgian certificate is issued by the Revenue Service within 30 days.

## Crypto in Georgia — tax and VASP registration
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/crypto-in-georgia/

In Georgia, income an individual receives from supplying crypto assets is exempt from personal income tax — as the Ministry of Finance has ruled. A crypto business — exchange, conversion, transfers, custody — may operate only after registering with the National Bank. We help set up the company, obtain VASP registration and meet AML requirements.

Under the Ministry of Finance's Public Decision No. 201 of 2019, crypto assets have no location, so an individual's income from supplying them is not Georgian-source income and is exempt from personal income tax. Exchanging crypto for money is not subject to VAT. A public decision binds the Revenue Service until the underlying rules change.
A company's profits from crypto, however, are taxed under the usual rules. And mind your home country's law — if you are resident there, you may owe tax there.

### VASP registration with the National Bank

- Only an LLC or JSC registered in Georgia can register
- Registration fee — GEL 5,000
- Minimum capital: GEL 150,000 — exchange or transfers; GEL 250,000 — other services; GEL 350,000 — a trading platform
- The National Bank decides within 60 calendar days (which can be extended)
- Lending virtual assets to individuals is banned, and so are privacy coins
- A VASP is an obliged entity under the AML law: customer identification and automated transaction monitoring are mandatory

- Assessing tax on crypto income
- Registering a crypto company
- VASP registration with the National Bank
- AML policy and customer due diligence rules
- Dealing with banks about crypto income
- Disputes with the Revenue Service and the National Bank

### Do I pay tax on income from selling crypto?
As an individual — no: under the Ministry of Finance's 2019 public decision, this income is exempt from personal income tax. Different rules apply to companies.

### Can I run a crypto exchange as a sole trader?
No. Only an LLC or JSC can register as a VASP.

### How much capital does a VASP need?
From GEL 150,000 to GEL 350,000, depending on the service. Providers registered earlier must meet this by 1 September 2027.

## Checking a Georgian company — registry, debts, courts
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/checking-a-georgian-company/

Before you do business with a Georgian company, buy property or pay an advance, check who stands behind it and what risks it carries. In Georgia, much of this information is public. We check the company in every source and give you a clear report — in English, Russian or Georgian.

Business registry data is public (Law on Entrepreneurs, Article 13): it shows the partners, director and representatives, legal form, status and change history, and the extract also covers tax liens and mortgages, public-law restrictions, pledges over movable property and debtors-register information.
Georgia has no public register of beneficial owners — the registry shows legal owners only. Companies with complex structures therefore need further checks.

### Where we check

| Source | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Business registry (napr.gov.ge) | Partners, director, status (including liquidation), change history, registration documents |
| Movable property and pledges registry | Pledges over company assets, tax liens, leasing |
| Real estate registry | Who owns property, mortgages, seizures |
| Debtors register (National Bureau of Enforcement) | Whether the company has debts in enforcement |
| Court decisions (ecd.court.ge) | Disputes where the company is a party |
| Revenue Service | VAT status, tax debt and tax liens |
| Insolvency cases | Rehabilitation or bankruptcy — published on matsne.gov.ge |
| Public procurement blacklist | Companies banned for dishonest conduct |

- Full company due diligence and report
- Checking partners and directors
- Checking property, mortgages and seizures
- Searching court and enforcement cases
- Drafting contracts that address the risks
- Checks before buying a share or a company

### Is information on Georgian companies public?
Yes. Business registry data and copies of registration documents are public; an official extract is issued for a fee.

### Can I find out who really owns a company?
The registry shows legal owners. Georgia has no public beneficial-ownership register, so complex structures need further checks.

### How long does a check take?
A basic check usually takes a few working days; full due diligence depends on the size of the company.

## Can foreigners buy land in Georgia? Agricultural land
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/can-foreigners-buy-land-in-georgia/

Foreigners can buy flats, houses and non-agricultural land in Georgia. Agricultural land, under the Constitution, may belong only to the state, municipalities and Georgian citizens — with narrow exceptions. We check the land category, choose a lawful route and protect your investment.

Under Article 19(4) of the Constitution, agricultural land may be owned only by the state, a self-governing unit, a Georgian citizen or a union of Georgian citizens. Exceptions are possible only by organic law.
Under the 2019 Organic Law, a foreigner may own agricultural land only through inheritance. A company registered in Georgia whose dominant (over 50%) partner is a foreigner may acquire it only under an investment plan, by Government decision. A dual citizen counts as a Georgian citizen for this law.

### What to know

- Before buying, check the land category on the Public Registry extract — agricultural or non-agricultural
- If investment-plan obligations aren't met, the land must be sold within 1 year or it passes to the state
- A mortgage over agricultural land with transfer to a foreign creditor is banned, as is a change of partners that makes a foreigner the dominant partner
- Financial institutions designated by the Government are exempt
- When agricultural land is sold, co-owners and registered lessees have a pre-emption right — foreigners don't

### Tax on selling property

An individual selling a flat or house (with its land) owned for more than 2 years pays no tax. If owned for less, the gain is taxed at 5%. Other assets, such as a plot of land, are also exempt after 2 years if not used in business.

- Checking the land category and registry
- Buying non-agricultural land as a foreigner
- Investment plan and Government consent for a company
- Inherited agricultural land
- Selling land and tax
- Land and boundary disputes

### Can a foreigner buy land in Georgia?
Non-agricultural land — yes. Agricultural land — only through inheritance, or for a company with a foreign dominant partner, under an investment plan and Government decision.

### I'm a dual citizen — can I buy agricultural land?
Yes. A dual citizen counts as a Georgian citizen under this law.

### Do I pay tax when I sell?
A flat or house you owned for more than 2 years is sold tax-free. Other cases we check individually.

## Working remotely from Georgia — tax, visa, work permit
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/working-remotely-from-georgia/

Many foreigners live in Georgia and work remotely for a foreign employer or foreign clients. Staying is simple — tax is where most people go wrong: pay for work you do while physically in Georgia is Georgian income, even if your employer and your bank are abroad. We assess your situation and set it up correctly.

Georgia has no separate digital nomad visa today. Citizens of the countries on the Government's list (Resolution No. 255 of 2015) can stay visa-free for a full year; others need a visa or a residence permit. If you plan to stay longer or register as a sole trader, plan your residence permit in advance.
Under Article 104 of the Tax Code, income from employment carried out in Georgia is Georgian-source income, and where the money is received does not matter. A foreign employer does not withhold Georgian tax (Article 154), so you must file an annual return yourself by 31 March of the following year and pay 20% (Articles 81 and 153). The exemption for foreign income (Article 82) doesn't help here — it covers only income that is not from a Georgian source.

### Do you need a work permit?

The Labour Migration Law does not apply when a foreigner works for or provides services to a non-resident and the work relates to that person's business outside Georgia (Article 1(4)(l)). So a remote employee of a foreign company usually doesn't need the right to work. A sole trader with clients in Georgia does need it since 1 March 2026; whether a sole trader serving only foreign clients falls under the exception should be checked case by case.

### Your options

| Option | Tax | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| Employee of a foreign company | 20%, annual return by 31 March | Usually no right to work needed; no Georgian pension contributions |
| Sole trader with small business status | 1% up to GEL 500,000, 3% above | Monthly return by the 15th; the 1% doesn't cover salary or consulting |
| Short visit — up to 30 days a year | Salary not taxed in Georgia | If you are non-resident and the employer has no permanent establishment in Georgia (Article 82) |

### The 1% sole trader — what to watch for

- The 1% applies to business income, not salary (Article 90). If you work for one company with fixed hours and under its direction, the Revenue Service may treat it as salary and tax it at 20%
- Consulting, legal, medical, audit, architecture and some other activities can't use the 1% (Government Resolution No. 415)
- Services to foreign businesses are generally outside Georgian VAT — the place of supply is where the client is (Article 162¹)
- Registering as a sole trader gives you neither a residence permit nor tax residency

### Residency and your home country

You become a Georgian tax resident if you spend 183 days or more in Georgia in any 12-month period. Your home country may still treat you as its resident and tax your worldwide income. Where a double tax treaty exists, it decides who taxes what, and a Georgian residence certificate is the proof.

### If you do nothing

- Late return — a penalty of 5% of the tax, 10% if more than 2 months late (Article 274)
- Late payment — interest of 0.05% per day
- Understated tax — a 10% to 50% penalty; large amounts can lead to a criminal case

- Assessing your tax position and residency
- Choosing between employment and sole trader status
- Registering as a sole trader with small business status
- Right to work and residence permit
- Annual and monthly tax returns
- Disputes with the Revenue Service

### Is there a digital nomad visa in Georgia?
Not a separate one today. Citizens of many countries can stay visa-free for a year; for a longer stay you need a residence permit.

### Can I work remotely for a foreign employer while visa-free?
Yes. The Labour Migration Law usually doesn't require the right to work when the work relates to a foreign company's business abroad. Tax, however, is due in Georgia.

### Do digital nomads pay tax in Georgia?
Yes, for work done while in Georgia: 20% through an annual return, or 1% as a sole trader where the activity qualifies. A non-resident who works here 30 days or less a year doesn't pay tax on the salary.

### Can a foreign salary go through a 1% sole trader?
No. Salary is excluded from the 1%. If you genuinely provide services rather than work as an employee, the contract must show it — we review the contract.

### Will I still owe tax in my home country?
Possibly. That depends on your home country's residency rules and on its tax treaty with Georgia. We check both sides.

## Baby born in Georgia to foreign parents — papers, citizenship
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/baby-born-in-georgia/

If your child is born in Georgia, the birth is registered here — whatever the parents' citizenship. But a child does not become a Georgian citizen just by being born here. We help with the documents, the apostille, the child's status and registration in your own country.

Every child born in Georgia has the birth registered (Law on Civil Acts, Article 22) — even if the parents have no legal basis to stay (Article 10). The maternity hospital sends the birth notice electronically within 5 working days; if it doesn't, or the child was born at home, the parents must apply themselves within 1 month. The birth certificate is free and issued in Georgian.
Under Article 10 of the Law on Citizenship, a child is a Georgian citizen by birth if one parent is a Georgian citizen, or if the parents are stateless persons with status in Georgia. If both parents are foreigners, the child takes the parents' citizenship — under the law of their country.

### Step by step

1. Birth registration — based on the hospital's notice; you collect the certificate at a Public Service Hall
2. Entering the parents — by joint application or with the marriage document; a foreign marriage certificate needs an apostille and a notarised translation
3. Apostille and translation of the birth certificate — for use in your country
4. Registering the child at your country's consulate and getting a passport
5. The child's status in Georgia — visa-free stay on their own passport, or a residence permit

### The child's residence permit

A foreigner's minor child is a family member, so if a parent holds a residence permit, the child can get a family reunification permit (Law on the Legal Status of Aliens, Article 15). Investment permits also cover family members.

### Leaving Georgia with the child

Georgian law does not require the other parent's consent for a foreign child to leave; exit can be restricted by a court decision. If the parents are in dispute, the other parent can go to court, and the Hague Convention applies to wrongful removal. Your country or the destination country may require consent — check in advance.

- Birth registration and entering the parents
- Translations and apostilles
- Establishing and acknowledging paternity
- Residence permit for the child
- Citizenship questions
- Disputes over the child's residence and travel

### Does a child born in Georgia become a Georgian citizen?
Not by birth alone. The child is a citizen if one parent is Georgian, or if the parents are stateless persons with status in Georgia.

### How much does a birth certificate cost?
The birth certificate is free. Registration is usually done by the next working day.

### How do I get the certificate recognised in my country?
It needs an apostille and a translation; then you register the child at your country's consulate.

### Do I need the other parent's consent to leave with the child?
For a foreign child, Georgian law doesn't require it unless a court has restricted exit. Your country's rules may differ.

## Foreign car in Georgia — 90 days, insurance, import tax
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/foreigners/foreign-car-in-georgia/

A foreigner can drive their own foreign-registered car in Georgia for 90 days. Overstaying, selling the car or handing it over without customs clearance leads to penalties. We help with the time limit, insurance, customs clearance and fines.

Under Finance Minister Order No. 257, a foreign-registered car or motorcycle brought in by a foreign citizen (including dual citizens) may stay in Georgia for 90 calendar days. Within that time it must leave, be cleared through customs or be placed under temporary import. For longer use, the Customs Code allows temporary import for up to 3 years with partial relief — 3% of the import tax for each month.
Border insurance covering the whole stay is compulsory on entry: for a car, 15 days — GEL 30, 30 days — GEL 50, 90 days — GEL 90, 1 year — GEL 295. Driving without it is fined GEL 100 (Administrative Offences Code, Article 191¹).

### Penalties and risks

| Breach | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Overstaying / late declaration | GEL 50 a day, up to GEL 1,000 (Customs Code, Article 165) |
| Breaking the conditions of a customs procedure | GEL 500, repeat — GEL 1,000 (Article 171) |
| Selling or handing over the car without clearance | 100% of the import duties (Article 172) |
| Driving without border insurance | GEL 100 |

### Customs clearance from 2026

Since 2 April 2026, excise on passenger cars depends on engine size and age (Tax Code, Article 188). A car recorded in the MIA database, or whose shipment began, before 2 April is taxed at the old rates. Importing a passenger car is exempt from VAT.

| Car | Excise |
|---|---|
| 0–6 years old | GEL 1.50 per cm³ |
| Over 6 years old | GEL 4.50 per cm³ |
| Right-hand drive | Three times the rate |
| Hybrid, 0–6 years (left-hand drive) | 60% less |
| Electric (left-hand drive) | Exempt |

Import tax is added: GEL 0.05 per cm³, plus 5% of that amount for each year of use. For example, an 8-year-old car with a 2,000 cm³ engine pays GEL 9,000 excise and GEL 140 import tax.

- Assessing the 90-day limit and temporary import
- Temporary import procedure for up to 3 years
- Customs clearance and tax calculation
- Appealing customs fines
- Selling or transferring the car lawfully
- Border insurance and driving licence questions

### How long can a foreign-registered car stay in Georgia?
90 calendar days. Then it must leave, be cleared or be placed under temporary import — for up to 3 years.

### What is the fine for overstaying 90 days?
GEL 50 a day, up to GEL 1,000.

### Can I sell my foreign-plated car in Georgia?
Only after customs clearance. Selling or handing it over without clearance is fined 100% of the import duties.

### How much is car import tax in Georgia in 2026?
Excise is GEL 1.50 per cm³ for cars up to 6 years old and GEL 4.50 for older ones; right-hand drive pays triple. Import tax is added; there is no VAT.

## Accepting an inheritance in Georgia from abroad
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/georgians-abroad/accepting-an-inheritance/

A family member has died in Georgia and you live abroad? You can accept the inheritance without coming — the key is not to miss the 6-month deadline.

An inheritance must be accepted within 6 months of its opening — as a rule, the date of death. The application to the notary can be filed through a representative. If you missed the deadline for a valid reason, a court can restore it.
We prepare the power of attorney text, gather the documents, obtain the certificate of inheritance and register the property in your name with the Public Registry. If the heirs disagree, we represent you in court.

- Accepting the estate through a notary by power of attorney
- The certificate of inheritance
- Registering the property in your name
- Restoring a missed deadline in court
- Disputes between heirs
- Selling inherited property

### How long do I have to accept an inheritance?
6 months from its opening — as a rule, the date of death.

### Do I need to come to Georgia?
No. The application to the notary can be filed through a representative under a power of attorney.

### I missed the deadline — is it too late?
Not necessarily. If you had a valid reason, a court can restore the deadline.

## Selling or buying property in Georgia from abroad
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/georgians-abroad/selling-property-from-abroad/

Living abroad and need to sell, buy or rent out property in Georgia? We do it in your name — so that your money and your property stay protected.

Your lawyer checks the buyer or seller, the property's history, mortgages and seizures, prepares the contract, completes the transaction and registers it with the Public Registry. We agree a safe way to receive the money in advance.
You can give the power of attorney at a Georgian consulate, with a local notary or — if you have a Georgian passport — online with a notary in Georgia. We draft it to cover only the powers that are needed.

- Checking the buyer, seller and the property
- Purchase, preliminary and lease agreements
- Completing the deal by power of attorney
- Registration with the Public Registry
- Receiving the money safely
- Fixing errors in the registry

### Can I sell a flat without coming to Georgia?
Yes — with a properly drafted power of attorney, a lawyer completes the deal in your name.

### How do I receive the money safely?
We agree the route in advance — for example, a transfer straight to your own bank account. This should also be written into the power of attorney.

### Can I give a power of attorney online?
Yes, if you have a Georgian passport — with a notary in Georgia by video call, with two witnesses present.

## Debts and enforcement in Georgia while you live abroad
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/georgians-abroad/debts-and-enforcement/

Living abroad and found out you are on Georgia's debtors' register, or your property has been seized? We find out where the debt comes from and find a way out.

A person is entered in the debtors' register as soon as enforcement proceedings start against them. The register is public, and while you are on it, if you register new property or a vehicle, the enforcement bureau is notified and any further sale of that property is blocked.
First we establish the basis of the enforcement — a court decision, a notary's writ or something else — and whether you were properly notified. Then we choose the route: an appeal, negotiating with the creditor, a payment plan, or paying off the debt and getting removed from the register.

- Checking the debtors' register and the case
- Checking the basis of enforcement
- Challenging a decision made in your absence
- Negotiating with the bank or creditor
- Lifting a seizure on property or an account
- Removal from the register after payment

### How do I find out whether I'm on the debtors' register?
The register is public — we can check it and tell you which case and what amount are involved.

### What does being on the register mean?
For example, if you register new property or a vehicle, the enforcement bureau is notified and further sale of that property is blocked until you are removed from the register.

### Can I negotiate a debt from abroad?
Yes. Under a power of attorney we negotiate with the bank or creditor and, if needed, handle the case in court.

### I have an old loan — could it be time-barred?
Possibly. The limitation period for a loan is 3 years, but paying part of it or acknowledging the debt restarts it, and for a debt confirmed by a court it is 10 years. Check the period with a lawyer before paying.

## Restoring and keeping Georgian citizenship
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/georgians-abroad/restoring-georgian-citizenship/

Did you lose Georgian citizenship when you became a citizen of another country? The law gives a temporary chance to get it back until 1 January 2027 — without giving up your other citizenship.

Under Article 32² of the Organic Law on Georgian Citizenship, a former citizen who lost Georgian citizenship because they acquired another one can apply to the Public Service Development Agency until 1 January 2027. The conditions are knowledge of the state language to the set level and the absence of legal obstacles set by the law. Under this route you don't have to give up your foreign citizenship, and your minor children are granted citizenship too.
If you are still a Georgian citizen and are about to acquire another citizenship, you must get consent to keep Georgian citizenship before you acquire the other one. We check your status, prepare the application and documents, and appeal a refusal.

- Restoring citizenship before 1 January 2027
- Keeping citizenship before acquiring another
- Children's citizenship and keeping it until age 18
- Checking your status — whether you are still a citizen
- Preparing the application and documents
- Appealing a refusal

### Will I have to give up my other citizenship?
Not when citizenship is restored under Article 32². This option is open until 1 January 2027.

### What are the conditions?
Knowledge of the state language to the set level and no legal obstacles under the law. The language requirement does not apply to some people with serious health conditions.

### Will my child get it too?
Yes — your minor children are granted citizenship too; a child aged 14 or older, with their consent.

## Crimes and penalties in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/

Short and clear: what each crime means, which article of the Criminal Code covers it, what the penalty is and what to do if you are accused or are a victim.

## Theft in Georgia — Article 177: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/theft-article-177/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 177

Theft is secretly taking someone else's movable property in order to unlawfully keep it (Article 177 of the Criminal Code of Georgia). "Secretly" means the owner or others don't see or realise it is happening.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, house arrest from 6 months to 1 year, or imprisonment from 1 to 3 years
- Significant damage (over GEL 150) or breaking into premises or storage: House arrest from 1 to 2 years or imprisonment from 3 to 5 years
- By a group by prior agreement; repeatedly; by breaking into a home; against a vehicle: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- By an organised group; on a large scale (over GEL 10,000); by a person convicted twice or more: Imprisonment from 6 to 10 years

- Correct valuation of the property — it decides which part of the article applies
- Whether the taking was secret and with intent to keep it
- Video recordings, identification and seizure records
- Compensating the damage and settling with the victim

### What is the penalty for theft in Georgia?
For the basic offence — a fine, house arrest or 1 to 3 years in prison. Significant damage, breaking into a home, acting as a group or a large amount make it harsher — up to 10 years.

### What counts as significant damage?
Property worth more than GEL 150. Over GEL 10,000 counts as a large amount.

### How is theft different from robbery?
Theft is secret; robbery (Article 178) is open — the property is taken while the owner or others see and realise it.

## Robbery in Georgia — Article 178: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/robbery-article-178/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 178

Robbery under Article 178 is openly taking someone else's movable property in order to unlawfully keep it. Unlike theft, the owner or others see and realise what is happening.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment from 3 to 5 years
- Significant damage (over GEL 150) or breaking into premises or storage: Imprisonment from 4 to 6 years
- By a group by prior agreement; repeatedly; by breaking into a home; with violence not dangerous to life or health, or the threat of it; against a vehicle: Imprisonment from 5 to 8 years
- By an organised group; on a large scale (over GEL 10,000); by a person convicted twice or more: Imprisonment from 7 to 11 years

- Whether the taking was really open — or is it theft
- Whether there was violence and how dangerous it was — this separates robbery from violent robbery
- Valuation of the property
- Reliability of identification, video and witness statements

### What is the penalty for robbery in Georgia?
For the basic offence — a fine, house arrest or 3 to 5 years in prison. With aggravating circumstances — up to 11 years.

### How is it different from violent robbery?
In robbery any violence used is not dangerous to life or health. If the violence is dangerous, or such violence is threatened, it is violent robbery under Article 179.

### Is snatching a phone from someone's hand robbery?
Often yes, because the taking is open. The exact assessment depends on the facts.

## Violent robbery in Georgia — Article 179
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/violent-robbery-article-179/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 179

Violent robbery under Article 179 is an attack to unlawfully take someone else's movable property, committed with violence dangerous to life or health or the threat of such violence. It is one of the most serious property crimes.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: Imprisonment from 5 to 7 years
- Breaking into premises or storage; as a group; against a vehicle: Imprisonment from 6 to 9 years
- Repeatedly; by breaking into a home; to take property on a large scale: Imprisonment from 8 to 12 years
- By an organised group; by a person convicted twice or more: Imprisonment from 11 to 15 years

- Whether the violence or threat was really dangerous — if not, the charge may be reduced to robbery
- The purpose of the attack — was it to take property
- The forensic medical report
- Reliability of identification and witness statements

### What is the penalty for violent robbery?
For the basic offence — 5 to 7 years in prison; with aggravating circumstances — up to 15 years.

### Can the charge be reduced to robbery?
Yes, if it is established that the violence or threat was not dangerous to life or health. That is why this question is central to the defence.

### Can a fine be imposed?
No. Every part of Article 179 provides only for imprisonment.

## Extortion in Georgia — Article 181: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/extortion-article-181/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 181

Extortion under Article 181 is demanding someone else's property, a property right or a financial benefit, combined with a threat — of violence, destroying or damaging property, or spreading discrediting or other harmful information. The threat can be aimed at the victim or a close relative.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine or imprisonment from 2 to 4 years
- As a group; repeatedly; to obtain property on a large scale: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- By an organised group; by a person convicted twice or more: Imprisonment from 6 to 9 years

- Whether the demand was lawful — for example, recovering a real debt
- What the threat said and how real it was
- Messages and recordings, and whether they were lawfully obtained
- Lawfulness of covert investigative actions
