### Is demanding a debt extortion?
Not by itself. But demanding repayment with threats of violence or other threats can be treated as extortion or another offence. It is safer to claim a debt through the courts.

### Someone threatens to post my photos unless I pay — what should I do?
Don't pay and don't delete the messages. Keep the evidence and go to the police — this is extortion.

### What is the penalty for extortion?
For the basic offence — a fine or 2 to 4 years in prison; with aggravating circumstances — up to 9 years.

## Embezzlement in Georgia — Article 182: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/embezzlement-article-182/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 182

Misappropriation or embezzlement under Article 182 is when a person unlawfully keeps or spends someone else's property or property right that was lawfully entrusted to them — for example, at work, under a contract or for safekeeping.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment from 3 to 5 years
- By a group by prior agreement; repeatedly; causing significant damage (over GEL 150); by abusing one's position: A fine or imprisonment from 4 to 7 years, with a ban on holding office or the activity for up to 3 years
- By an organised group; on a large scale (over GEL 10,000); by a person convicted twice or more: Imprisonment from 7 to 11 years, with a ban on holding office or the activity for up to 3 years

- Whether the property was really entrusted and on what terms
- Whether it is a crime or a civil dispute — for example, about settling accounts
- Accounting records and the audit or expert report
- The exact amount of the damage and its compensation

### How is embezzlement different from theft?
In embezzlement the property was lawfully entrusted to the person — at work or under a contract. In theft it was secretly taken from someone else's possession.

### Is a shortfall at work always a crime?
No. Sometimes it is an accounting error or a civil dispute. What matters is whether there was intent to misappropriate.

### Does paying back the damage end the case?
Not automatically, but it can significantly affect the outcome. Decide when and how with your lawyer.

## Damage to property in Georgia — Article 187
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/property-damage-article-187/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 187

Under Article 187 it is a crime to damage or destroy someone else's property where this causes significant damage — over GEL 150. Smaller damage is not a crime under this article; in that case compensation is usually claimed through a civil claim.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence — significant damage: A fine, 100–180 hours of community service, corrective labour for up to 1 year, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment from 1 to 5 years
- By arson, explosion or another generally dangerous method; repeatedly; as a group: Imprisonment from 3 to 6 years
- The same, negligently causing a person's death or another grave consequence: Imprisonment from 6 to 10 years
- The same, causing the death of two or more people: Imprisonment from 9 to 12 years

- Valuation of the damage — under GEL 150 it is not a crime under this article
- Whether the damage was intentional
- The expert report on the cause and cost of the damage
- Compensation and settlement with the victim

### Someone damaged my car — is that a crime?
If it was intentional and the damage exceeds GEL 150 — yes, it is a crime under Article 187. Go to the police and keep photos and video.

### What if the damage is under GEL 150?
It is not a crime under this article. You can claim compensation through a civil claim.

### What is the penalty for damaging someone's property?
For the basic offence — from a fine up to 5 years in prison; by arson, explosion or as a group — 3 to 6 years.

## Bodily harm in Georgia — Articles 117, 118, 120
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/bodily-harm/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 117, 118, 120

Intentional bodily harm has three levels: minor (Article 120), less serious (Article 118) and serious (Article 117). The level is set by a forensic medical examination — and that decides which article and which penalty apply.

### Possible penalties

- Minor harm — short-term damage to health (Art. 120): A fine, corrective labour for up to 6 months, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment from 1 to 3 years
- Minor harm with aggravating circumstances — e.g. against a family member, as a group, out of hooligan motives: Imprisonment from 3 to 5 years
- Less serious harm — long-term damage to health (Art. 118): Corrective labour for up to 18 months, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment from 2 to 4 years
- Less serious harm with aggravating circumstances: Imprisonment from 4 to 6 years
- Serious harm — dangerous to life, or loss of an organ or its function (Art. 117): Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- Serious harm causing death: Imprisonment from 5 to 8 years
- Serious harm with aggravating circumstances: Imprisonment from 9 to 13 years; if it caused death — 10 to 14 years

- The forensic medical report — severity and cause of the injury; an alternative examination if needed
- Self-defence — whether you were protecting yourself or someone else
- Who started the conflict: video and witnesses
- Whether the aggravating circumstance is well founded

### What do minor, less serious and serious harm mean?
Minor harm causes short-term damage to health, less serious harm long-term damage, and serious harm is dangerous to life or causes, for example, the loss of an organ or its function. A forensic examination decides the level.

### I was defending myself — will I still be punished?
Harm caused within the limits of necessary self-defence is not a crime. The key is that the defence was proportionate to the attack — a lawyer proves this with evidence.

### What should a victim of a beating do?
See a doctor and go to the police straight away — recording the injuries and the forensic examination are decisive for the case.

## Hooliganism in Georgia — Article 239: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/hooliganism-article-239/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 239

Hooliganism under Article 239 is an act that grossly breaches public order, shows open disrespect for society and is committed with violence or the threat of violence. A similar act without violence is usually petty hooliganism — an administrative offence.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, 120–180 hours of community service, corrective labour for up to 1 year, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment for up to 1 year
- By a group by prior agreement; against a public official or a person stopping the hooliganism; by a person convicted of hooliganism: A fine, 180–200 hours of community service, corrective labour for 1 to 2 years, or imprisonment from 2 to 5 years
- Using a firearm or another object as a weapon: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years

- Whether there was violence or a threat — without it this is usually an administrative matter
- Whether it showed disrespect for society, or was a personal conflict
- Video and witnesses
- The object used — whether it counts as a weapon

### How is hooliganism different from petty hooliganism?
Under Article 239 hooliganism is committed with violence or the threat of it. Disturbing public order without violence — for example, swearing in a public place — is usually petty hooliganism, punished as an administrative offence.

### Is a street fight hooliganism?
It can be. If the fight comes from a personal conflict, it may be treated as bodily harm; if it grossly breaches public order, as hooliganism. The classification matters a lot for the defence.

### What is the penalty for hooliganism?
For the basic offence — from a fine up to 1 year in prison; using a weapon or an object as a weapon — 4 to 7 years.

## Traffic accident in Georgia — Article 276: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/traffic-accident-article-276/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 276

A driver who breaks road safety rules and thereby causes less serious or serious injury or death faces criminal liability under Article 276. Driving under the influence of drugs is a crime as well. Alcohol or drugs make the penalty much harsher.

### Possible penalties

- Part 1 — driving under the influence of narcotic or psychotropic substances: A fine, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, community service or up to 3 years in prison
- Part 2 — breaking the rules, causing less serious injury: A fine, house arrest or up to 3 years in prison
- Part 3 — the same, under the influence of alcohol or drugs: Imprisonment from 2 to 5 years
- Part 4 — serious injury: A fine or imprisonment from 3 to 5 years
- Part 5 — the same, under the influence of alcohol or drugs: Imprisonment from 4 to 6 years
- Part 6 — a person's death: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- Part 7 — the same, under the influence of alcohol or drugs: Imprisonment from 6 to 9 years
- Part 8 — the death of two or more people: Imprisonment from 6 to 10 years
- Part 9 — the same, under the influence of alcohol or drugs: Imprisonment from 8 to 12 years

- The accident reconstruction report — who broke the rules and whether the accident could have been avoided
- The severity of injuries — the forensic medical report
- Lawfulness and results of the alcohol or drug test
- Video, witnesses and the accident diagram
- Compensation and settlement with the victim

### I injured someone in an accident — will I go to prison?
Not necessarily. For less serious injury a fine or house arrest is possible. Much depends on the expert reports and whether alcohol or drugs were involved.

### A drunk driver caused an accident — how harsh is the penalty?
Alcohol or drugs make it harsher in every case: serious injury — 4 to 6 years, a death — 6 to 9 years, two or more deaths — 8 to 12 years.

### Will I lose my driving licence?
If committed under the influence of alcohol, the court can additionally ban the activity — including driving — for up to 3 years.

## Bribe-taking in Georgia — Article 338: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/bribe-taking-article-338/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 338

Bribe-taking is an official, or a person treated as one, receiving or demanding money, property, a financial benefit or another undue advantage — or accepting a promise of it — to act or not act for someone in the exercise of their duties (Article 338). It is one of the most severely punished corruption crimes.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: Imprisonment from 6 to 9 years
- By a holder of a political state office; on a large scale (over GEL 10,000); as a group: Imprisonment from 7 to 11 years
- By a person convicted of bribery; repeatedly; by extortion; by an organised group; on an especially large scale (over GEL 30,000): Imprisonment from 11 to 15 years

- Whether the person is an official or treated as one
- Whether the benefit was linked to an official act
- Lawfulness of covert recordings and sting operations
- Whether there was entrapment
- Correct valuation of the bribe

### What is the penalty for bribe-taking?
For the basic offence — 6 to 9 years in prison. On a large scale or by a political office holder — 7 to 11 years; by extortion or on an especially large scale — up to 15 years.

### Is just demanding a bribe a crime?
Yes. The law punishes taking, demanding and accepting a promise of a bribe.

### What counts as a large bribe?
Over GEL 10,000; an especially large bribe is over GEL 30,000.

## Bribe-giving in Georgia — Article 339: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/bribe-giving-article-339/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 339

Bribe-giving is promising, offering or giving money, property or another undue advantage to an official, or a person treated as one, so that they act in someone's favour in their duties (Article 339). The law punishes not only giving — an offer is enough.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, corrective labour up to 2 years, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or up to 3 years in prison
- To get an unlawful act done: A fine or imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- By an organised group: Imprisonment from 5 to 8 years

- A voluntary report — releases from liability
- Whether the offer was really linked to an official act
- Signs of extortion or entrapment
- Lawfulness of covert recordings

### I was asked for a bribe and paid — what now?
By law, a bribe-giver is released from criminal liability if they voluntarily report it to the investigating authority. Assess the situation with a lawyer before making the report.

### I only offered it — is that a crime too?
Yes. Article 339 punishes promising, offering and giving.

### What is the penalty for giving a bribe?
For the basic offence — from a fine up to 3 years in prison; to get an unlawful act done — 4 to 7 years; by an organised group — 5 to 8 years.

## Trading in influence in Georgia — Article 339¹
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/trading-in-influence-article-339-1/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 339¹

Trading in influence is when someone claims they can unlawfully influence an official's decision and demands or takes money or another benefit for it — or when someone offers such a person a benefit (Article 339¹). It is a crime even if no influence was exerted and nothing came of it.

### Possible penalties

- Part 1 — offering, promising or giving a benefit to a person claiming influence: A fine, corrective labour up to 2 years, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or up to 2 years in prison
- Part 2 — demanding or taking a benefit in exchange for 'influence': Imprisonment from 3 to 5 years
- Part 3 — Part 2 committed by an organised group: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years

- A voluntary report — releases from liability under Part 1
- Whether it was really about unlawful influence rather than a lawful service
- Lawfulness and context of covert recordings
- Who took the initiative

### What is trading in influence, simply?
Buying and selling 'connections': one person says they have sway over an official and takes money for it, the other pays.

### If no influence happened, is it still a crime?
Yes. By law it doesn't matter whether influence was exerted or the desired result was achieved.

### Can someone be released from liability?
The person who offered or gave the benefit (Part 1) is released if they voluntarily reported it to the investigating authority.

## Prohibited gifts to officials in Georgia — Article 340
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/prohibited-gift-article-340/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 340

An official, or a person treated as one, accepting a gift prohibited by law commits a crime (Article 340) — even where there are no signs of a bribe. What counts as a prohibited gift is set by the public service legislation.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, 100–300 hours of community service, a ban on holding office for up to 3 years, house arrest or up to 2 years in prison
- Repeatedly: A fine, 200–400 hours of community service, a ban on holding office for up to 3 years, or 2 to 4 years in prison

- Whether the gift was really prohibited by law
- Whether the person is an official or treated as one
- Whether this is a disciplinary rather than a criminal matter

### Is any gift to an official a crime?
No. The crime is accepting a gift prohibited by law. What is prohibited is set by the public service legislation.

### How is it different from a bribe?
A bribe is taken in exchange for an official act. A prohibited gift doesn't need that link.

### What is the penalty?
From a fine up to 2 years in prison; repeatedly — up to 4 years.

## Official forgery in Georgia — Article 341
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/official-forgery-article-341/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 341

Official forgery is an official, or a person treated as one, entering false information in an official document or register, drawing up or issuing a false document, or falsifying a document in an organisation's file — for gain or another personal motive (Article 341).

### Possible penalties

- Official forgery: A fine, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years, or imprisonment from 2 to 4 years

- Whether the entry was really false — or a mistake
- Whether there was gain or another personal motive — without it there is no crime
- Who made the entry and on whose instructions
- Handwriting and document examination

### I made a mistake in a document — is that forgery?
No. Official forgery requires a false entry made knowingly, for gain or another personal motive.

### Does it apply only to public officials?
It applies to officials and persons treated as such, including some employees of public legal entities.

### What is the penalty?
A fine, house arrest or 2 to 4 years in prison.

## Disobeying the police — Article 173 (admin.)
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/disobeying-police-article-173/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 173

Article 173 of the Code of Administrative Offences punishes disobeying a lawful order or demand of a police officer, another law-enforcement officer or a person treated as one, as well as verbally insulting or swearing at them. It is an administrative case, but the outcome can be up to 60 days of detention — so a lawyer matters here too.

### Possible penalties

- Part 1 — disobeying a lawful demand of a law-enforcement officer: A fine of GEL 2,000–5,000 or up to 60 days of administrative detention
- Part 2 — verbally insulting, swearing at or otherwise insulting an officer: A fine of GEL 2,000–5,000 or up to 60 days of administrative detention
- Part 3 — repeated after an administrative penalty: A fine of GEL 3,500–6,000 or 7 to 60 days of administrative detention
- In addition: Loss of the right to carry a weapon for up to 3 years; for a foreigner — possible expulsion and an entry ban of up to 3 years

- Whether the police demand was lawful — disobeying an unlawful demand is not an offence
- Video — body cameras, phones, witnesses
- Accuracy of the record and respect for detention time limits
- Unpaid fines: on a repeat, detention is imposed instead of a fine — this must be considered

### What is the penalty under Article 173?
A fine of GEL 2,000–5,000 or up to 60 days of administrative detention. On a repeat — GEL 3,500–6,000 or 7 to 60 days.

### How long can they hold me before court?
A person detained administratively must be brought before a court within 24 hours; to gather evidence this can be extended once by 24 hours.

### Can I appeal?
Yes. The court's decision can be appealed within 10 days of receiving it.

## Petty hooliganism in Georgia — Article 166 (admin.)
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/petty-hooliganism-article-166/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 166

Petty hooliganism is swearing in a public place, insultingly accosting people and similar acts that disturb public order or people's peace (Article 166 of the Code of Administrative Offences). A similar act committed with violence or the threat of violence is criminal hooliganism (Article 239).

### Possible penalties

- Part 1 — petty hooliganism: A fine of GEL 500–3,000 or up to 20 days of administrative detention
- Part 2 — repeated after an administrative penalty: A fine of GEL 3,000–5,000 or 5 to 60 days of administrative detention
- In addition: Loss of the right to carry a weapon for up to 3 years; for a foreigner — possible expulsion and an entry ban of up to 3 years

- Whether the place was public and public order was disturbed
- Video and witnesses
- Accuracy of the record — which words and actions were written down
- A personal conflict or a breach of public order

### What is the penalty under Article 166?
A fine of GEL 500–3,000 or up to 20 days of administrative detention. On a repeat — GEL 3,000–5,000 or 5 to 60 days.

### How is it different from criminal hooliganism?
Criminal hooliganism (Article 239) involves violence or the threat of violence. Without it, it is usually petty hooliganism.

### Can I appeal?
Yes. The court's decision can be appealed within 10 days of receiving it.

## Account hacking in Georgia — Article 284: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/hacking-article-284/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 284

Unauthorised access to a computer system is a crime under Article 284. A computer system means any device that processes data with a program — including a mobile phone. So getting into someone else's Facebook, email or phone without permission falls under this article too.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: A fine, corrective labour or up to 2 years in prison
- As a group; by abusing one's position; repeatedly; causing significant damage (over GEL 2,000): A fine, corrective labour up to 2 years, or 2 to 5 years in prison
- Against an operator of a critical information system: Imprisonment from 3 to 6 years

- Whether access was really 'unauthorised' — for example, the password was given to you
- Who actually logged in — IP addresses, devices, logs
- Lawfulness of how digital evidence was obtained and examined
- The amount of damage — over GEL 2,000 changes the part of the article

### Is logging into someone else's Facebook a crime?
Yes, if the owner didn't give you access. Under Article 284 that is unauthorised access to a computer system.

### My account was hacked — what should I do?
Regain access, change passwords, turn on two-factor authentication and keep every message. Then go to the police — if you lost money, contact your bank immediately too.

### What is the penalty for hacking an account?
For the basic offence — from a fine up to 2 years in prison; with significant damage, as a group or repeatedly — up to 5 years. If done for financial gain, Article 286¹ may apply.

## Phishing and online theft in Georgia — Article 286¹
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/phishing-online-theft-article-286-1/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 286¹

Article 286¹ punishes unauthorised access to a computer system, altering data or interfering with a system to obtain money or another financial benefit, where it causes someone financial loss. Phishing and transferring money with someone else's card details or online banking are often charged this way.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: Community service, corrective labour, house arrest, or 2 to 4 years in prison
- As a group by prior agreement; significant loss (over GEL 150): Imprisonment from 5 to 7 years
- By abusing one's position; large loss (over GEL 10,000); by an organised group; repeatedly: Imprisonment from 6 to 10 years
- Against a critical information system; by a person convicted twice or more: Imprisonment from 7 to 11 years

- Who really made the transaction — often the accused is only the account holder
- Bank records, IP addresses and devices
- The amount of loss — the GEL 150 and 10,000 thresholds
- Lawfulness of the digital forensics
- Compensating the loss

### I lost money to phishing — what should I do?
Call your bank immediately and block the card, keep the messages and links, and go to the police. The faster you act, the better the chance of recovering the money.

### Someone else's money came into my account and I sent it on — am I at risk?
Possibly. If you 'lend' your account or help with transfers, you may end up accused as a participant or of money laundering. Contact a lawyer straight away.

### What is the penalty under Article 286¹?
Basic offence — 2 to 4 years; loss over GEL 150 — 5 to 7 years; over GEL 10,000 — 6 to 10 years; for repeat offenders — up to 11 years.

## Sharing private photos in Georgia — Articles 157, 157¹
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/private-photos-article-157/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 157, 157¹

Unlawfully obtaining, keeping or spreading information about someone's private life or their personal data is a crime under Article 157 where it causes significant harm. Violating the secret of private life — intimate photos, for example — is a more serious crime under Article 157¹ and is punished even without harm. Spreading it on social media makes the penalty harsher.

### Possible penalties

- 157 — obtaining, keeping or spreading private information or data (with significant harm): A fine, corrective labour up to 2 years, or up to 3 years in prison
- 157 — the same, via the internet or social media: A fine, corrective labour or up to 4 years in prison
- 157¹ — obtaining, keeping or spreading the secret of private life: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- 157¹ — the same, via the internet or social media: Imprisonment from 5 to 8 years
- 157¹ — for gain or repeatedly: Imprisonment from 6 to 9 years
- 157¹ — by a person obliged to protect the secret, or by abusing one's position: Imprisonment from 7 to 10 years

- What the information is — a secret of private life (157¹) or other private information (157)
- Whether obtaining or sharing was really unlawful — for example, with consent
- Who spread it — accounts, devices, digital traces
- Under Article 157 — whether there was significant harm

### Someone threatens to post my intimate photo — what should I do?
Don't pay and don't delete the messages. Keep the evidence and go to the police: threats, extortion and spreading the secret are separate crimes. A lawyer will also help get the content removed.

### What is the penalty for sharing private photos?
For spreading a secret of private life — 4 to 7 years, via social media — 5 to 8 years, for gain — 6 to 9 years.

### Is making a secret recording a crime too?
Recording or eavesdropping on a private conversation without permission is punished under Article 158. There is an exception if the recording was handed to investigators with information about another crime.

## Domestic violence in Georgia — Article 126¹: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/domestic-violence-article-126-1/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 126¹

Domestic violence is violence, systematic insults, blackmail or humiliation by one family member against another, causing physical pain or suffering (Article 126¹). If health is harmed, the act is assessed under the bodily harm articles. In such cases the police usually also issue a restraining order.

### Possible penalties

- Basic offence: 80–150 hours of community service or up to 2 years in prison, with or without restrictions on weapon rights
- Against a minor, a helpless or disabled person or a pregnant woman; in a minor's presence; against two or more people; as a group; repeatedly: 200–400 hours of community service or 1 to 3 years in prison, with or without restrictions on weapon rights
- Breaching a restraining or protective order (Article 381¹): A fine, 180–240 hours of community service or up to 1 year in prison; repeatedly — 1 to 3 years

- Whether the parties are 'family members' under the law
- Whether there was physical pain or suffering and how it is proven
- Systematic conduct — a one-off conflict or a pattern
- Witnesses, recordings and medical records
- Strictly complying with any order while the case is ongoing

### What is the penalty for domestic violence?
For the basic offence — community service or up to 2 years in prison; with aggravating circumstances — 1 to 3 years.

### Who counts as a family member?
A spouse and children, as well as parents, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren, the spouse's parents, an unmarried partner and a former spouse.

### Does reconciliation end the case?
Not automatically. The state investigates domestic violence, and reconciliation doesn't by itself cancel an order if there is still a threat.

## Murder in Georgia — Articles 108, 109: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/murder-article-108-109/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 108

Intentional murder is the most serious charge: under Article 108 — 10 to 15 years; with aggravating circumstances (Article 109) — 16 to 20 years or life imprisonment. Much depends on how the act is classified: intentional or negligent, self-defence or a state of sudden, strong emotional disturbance. That is why the defence has to start from the first interview.

### Possible penalties

- 108 — intentional murder: Imprisonment from 10 to 15 years
- 109 — intentional murder with aggravating circumstances: for example, as a group, of a family member, a pregnant woman or a minor, of two or more people, for gain or to order, with particular cruelty: Imprisonment from 16 to 20 years or life imprisonment
- 111 — murder in a state of sudden, strong emotional disturbance caused by the victim's violence, grave insult or other grossly immoral conduct: House arrest from 6 months to 1 year or 1 to 3 years in prison; of two or more people — house arrest from 1 to 2 years or 2 to 5 years in prison
- 113 — murder exceeding the limits of self-defence: Corrective labour up to 2 years, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years or 1 to 3 years in prison
- 116 — causing death by negligence: House arrest from 6 months to 2 years or 2 to 4 years in prison; of two or more people — 3 to 5 years
- Attempted murder: Charged under the same article as the completed murder; life imprisonment cannot be imposed for an attempt

- Self-defence — acting to protect yourself or someone else is not a crime (Article 28)
- Intent or negligence — this decides the article and the penalty
- Strong emotional disturbance caused by the victim's conduct (Article 111)
- Forensic medical examination — the cause of death and its link to the act
- Whether the arrest, search and questioning were lawful
- Jury selection and presenting the case to a jury

### What is the penalty for intentional murder?
Under Article 108 — 10 to 15 years. With aggravating circumstances (Article 109) — 16 to 20 years or life imprisonment.

### I was defending myself — is it still murder?
If it was self-defence, it is not a crime. If the defence was clearly out of proportion to the attack, it is murder exceeding the limits of self-defence (Article 113) — up to 3 years. This is proven with evidence, so you need a lawyer from day one.

### Are murder cases heard by a jury?
Yes — completed murder (Articles 108 and 109) is heard by a jury unless the accused asks for the case to be heard by a judge. Our lawyer, Mariam Madzgharashvili, is a member of the Georgian Bar Association's Jury Trial Committee.

### How is murder different from causing death by negligence?
Murder is intentional. If the person did not want the death and did not foresee it, although they should have, it is causing death by negligence (Article 116) — up to 4 years.

## Illegal firearms in Georgia — Article 236: penalties
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/crimes/illegal-firearms-article-236/ — Criminal Code of Georgia, Article 236

Illegally acquiring, keeping, carrying, making or selling a firearm, ammunition or explosives is a crime under Article 236. Carrying is punished most harshly — 4 to 7 years. Anyone who voluntarily hands the weapon in is released from liability, unless they committed another crime.

### Possible penalties

- Part 1 — illegally acquiring or keeping a hunting or sports firearm or its ammunition: A fine, house arrest from 6 months to 2 years or up to 2 years in prison
- Part 2 — the same, as a group or repeatedly: Imprisonment from 2 to 5 years
- Part 3 — illegally acquiring or keeping another firearm (for example, a pistol), ammunition, explosives or an explosive device: Imprisonment from 3 to 6 years
- Part 4 — illegally carrying a firearm, ammunition or explosives: Imprisonment from 4 to 7 years
- Part 5 — illegally making, transporting, sending or selling: Imprisonment from 6 to 9 years
- Part 6 — acts under Parts 3–5 committed as a group or by someone previously convicted of them: Imprisonment from 8 to 11 years

- Whether the item is a firearm or ammunition at all — ballistic examination
- Whose weapon it was and whether you knew it was there
- Whether the search and seizure were lawful
- Voluntary surrender — release from liability
- Keeping or carrying — the right part of the article changes the penalty

### I have an old gun at home — what should I do?
If you hand it in voluntarily, you are released from criminal liability, as long as there are no signs of another crime. Contact us before you do — we'll tell you how to do it properly.

### Does this article cover hunting shotguns?
Smoothbore hunting shotguns are not covered by Article 236. Illegally keeping other hunting or sports firearms falls under Part 1 — from a fine up to 2 years.

### What is the penalty for carrying a pistol?
Illegally carrying a firearm is punished with 4 to 7 years in prison; as a group or by a repeat offender — 8 to 11 years.

## LLC or sole trader in Georgia — which to choose
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/llc-vs-sole-trader-georgia/ — published 2026-10-14

In short: an individual entrepreneur (sole trader) is you, registered as a business — simple, but you are liable for debts with all your personal property. An LLC is a separate company — more formalities, but your personal property is protected and profit is taxed only when you take it out. For a small business, the sole trader's 1% regime is the cheapest — if your activity qualifies.

### The main differences

|   | Sole trader | LLC |
|---|---|---|
| Liability | With all your personal property | Partners are not personally liable (except abuse) |
| What it is | You yourself, registered as a business | A separate legal entity |
| Partners | One person only | One or several, with shares |
| Registration | ID/passport and an address | Also a charter and a director |
| Accounting | Minimal | Bookkeeping and annual reports |
| Standard tax | 20% on profit | 15% profit tax only when distributed + 5% on dividends |
| Special regime | 1% of turnover up to GEL 500,000 (3% above) | None |
| VAT | Above GEL 100,000 — registration, 18% | The same |

### Taxes — an example

Say the annual profit is GEL 100,000. A sole trader without the 1% status pays 20% — GEL 20,000. An LLC that pays out all the profit as dividends pays GEL 15,000 profit tax and GEL 4,250 on the dividends — GEL 19,250 in total; if half the profit stays in the company, tax is due only on the part paid out. A sole trader with small business status pays 1% of turnover — GEL 1,000 on GEL 100,000 of turnover.

### The 1% regime isn't for everyone

- Small business status is only for individual entrepreneurs; annual turnover up to GEL 500,000, 3% above
- A return and payment every month, by the 15th of the following month
- Excluded: activities that need a licence or permit, making excise goods, currency exchange, medical, architectural, legal, notarial, audit and consulting work, gambling business, staffing (Government Resolution No. 415)
- The 1% doesn't cover rent, loan interest, dividends, selling real estate or a car, or salary

### When to choose a sole trader

- You work alone and your activity qualifies for the 1%
- Annual turnover stays under GEL 500,000
- The risk of debts or claims is small
- You want minimal paperwork

### When to choose an LLC

- You have a partner or an investor
- Your activity doesn't qualify for the 1%
- You sign large contracts or carry real risk and need to protect your personal property
- You keep part of the profit in the business — tax only when it is paid out
- Banks and large clients prefer to deal with a company

### For foreigners

A foreigner can register either form, also remotely — with a notarised, apostilled power of attorney and a Georgian translation. Since 1 March 2026, a foreigner working in Georgia — as a sole trader or as an LLC director — needs the right to work. Registration itself does not give a residence permit.

## Foreigner arrested in Georgia: rights and first steps
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/foreigner-arrested-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-11

When a foreigner is arrested in Georgia, the language, an unfamiliar procedure and distance from family make everything harder. The first hours matter most.

### Your rights

- A lawyer — from the first contact with the investigating authority
- A free interpreter if you don't speak Georgian — in that case a lawyer is also mandatory
- The right to remain silent — you don't have to give a statement
- Having your country's consulate informed — ask for it
- Having a relative informed of your arrest

### What happens after the arrest

You must be charged within 48 hours of the arrest, or released. Within the next 24 hours after the charge, a court decides on a preventive measure — for example, bail or pre-trial detention.

### Why the risk is higher for a foreigner

The prosecution often argues that a foreigner may leave the country, so the risk of a detention request is high. The lawyer's job is to show the court your ties to Georgia — home, job, family, business — and to propose a less severe measure.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Don't sign any document you don't understand
- Don't give explanations without your lawyer — not even in an "informal chat"
- Don't agree to a plea agreement before reviewing the evidence with your lawyer

### Expulsion as a consequence

For a foreigner, a criminal case can have an extra consequence: the court can impose expulsion from Georgia and an entry ban as a penalty. Expulsion can also come up after a sentence has been served. So the defence strategy has to take this risk into account.

### If your family is abroad

A family member can contact us by phone or WhatsApp — we sign the engagement remotely and step into the case right away. We keep the family informed in a language they understand.

## Deportation from Georgia: grounds, deadlines and appeal
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/deportation-from-georgia/ — published 2026-10-11

Expulsion is decided by the competent body of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Deadlines are very short, so it pays to contact a lawyer on the very first day.

### When a foreigner can be expelled

Under Article 51 of the Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, grounds include a foreigner who:

- Entered Georgia without a lawful basis
- No longer has a lawful basis to stay — for example, their period expired or a residence permit was refused
- Is believed to threaten state or public security
- Systematically breaks the law
- Obtained the right to stay using a false document
- Is serving or has served a sentence for a crime, or has a suspended sentence
- Worked without the right to labour activity — a ground that matters especially since 2026

### How the procedure works

1. Within 10 working days of discovering the ground, the Ministry considers expulsion.
2. You are interviewed — you are notified of the date 2 working days in advance.
3. The decision must be translated into a language you understand and must state how to appeal.
4. As a rule, you are given a period to leave voluntarily — from 7 to 30 calendar days.

### Appeal — only 10 days

The decision can be appealed in court within 10 days of being served. Appealing does not by itself give you a residence permit or postpone your obligation to leave, so a lawyer often looks for other routes at the same time.

### The temporary accommodation centre

Before or after the expulsion decision, a detained foreigner can be placed in a temporary accommodation centre for 3 months — a court decides this: the foreigner must be brought before a court within 48 hours of detention, and is released if no decision is made within the next 24 hours. A court can extend this by up to 6 more months — 9 months in total at most.

### What a lawyer does

- Checks whether the decision has a lawful basis
- Represents you at the interview and gathers evidence — family, job, property
- Files the appeal in court on time
- Looks for a lawful basis to stay — for example, the right type of residence permit

## Recognising a foreign court decision in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/recognition-of-foreign-judgments-georgia/ — published 2026-10-11

Divorced abroad, or a foreign court ordered alimony or a debt to be paid? For that decision to work in Georgia — for example, for the divorce to be registered here or the alimony enforced — it usually has to be recognised in Georgia first.

### Who recognises it

Under Article 68 of the Law on Private International Law, Georgia recognises foreign court decisions that have entered into force. Recognition is decided by the Supreme Court of Georgia.

### When recognition is not needed

A decision in a marriage case does not need recognition if, when it was made, both spouses were citizens of the country whose authority made it. If at least one spouse is a Georgian citizen, recognition is usually needed.

### When recognition can be refused

- The case falls under Georgia's exclusive jurisdiction
- A party was not properly summoned to court, or there were other procedural violations
- A Georgian court has already decided the same dispute, or the same case is pending in Georgia
- Under Georgian law the foreign court was not competent to hear the case
- That country does not recognise Georgian court decisions
- The decision contradicts the fundamental principles of Georgian law

### The documents you need

- A copy of the court decision
- Proof that the decision has entered into force
- Proof that the other party was properly summoned
- An apostille or consular legalisation, depending on the country (documents from some countries need neither)
- A certified Georgian translation

### Recognition and enforcement

Recognition and enforcement are different things. If the decision requires money to be paid — alimony or a debt, for example — enforcement is a separate step. A lawyer plans both together so no time is lost.

## Divorce from abroad: without coming to Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/divorce-from-abroad-georgia/ — published 2026-10-11

Many Georgians living abroad think they have to come to Georgia to divorce. Often they don't — the route depends on whether you both agree.

### If you both agree

Under Article 1123 of the Civil Code, if there is no dispute between the spouses, the divorce is registered with the civil registry — without a court. Abroad, a divorce can also be registered at a Georgian consulate on the spouses' joint application. Check with your consulate which documents it requires.

### If there is a dispute

If one spouse objects, or there is a dispute about a child, alimony or property, a court decides on the divorce. A lawyer can run this case under a power of attorney — you don't need to be in Georgia. The court may give the spouses time to reconcile, no longer than 6 months.

### Power of attorney

You can give a power of attorney at a Georgian consulate, with a local notary (with an apostille or legalisation, depending on the country) or, if you have a Georgian passport, online — with a notary in Georgia by video call, with two witnesses present.

### If you already divorced abroad

If a foreign court granted the divorce and at least one spouse is a Georgian citizen, the decision usually has to be recognised in Georgia by the Supreme Court. Until then, you are still considered married in Georgia.

### Children and property

When granting a divorce, the court can also decide where the child lives, alimony and the division of property. If the property is in Georgia, it is often simpler to settle these questions here.

## Refused entry to Georgia: reasons and what to do
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/refused-entry-to-georgia/ — published 2026-10-11

Being turned away at the border is a shock — especially if you have family, a home or a business in Georgia. The decision is made by the Border Police, and the person is sent back. Here is what the reason may be and what you can do.

### Why entry can be refused

Under Article 11 of the Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, entry can be refused if:

- You don't have the documents required for entry
- You are banned from entering Georgia or haven't paid a fine for overstaying
- You haven't paid another fine imposed in Georgia
- You gave incomplete or false information to obtain a visa
- You have no insurance or not enough money to stay and return
- There are grounds to believe your stay would threaten state security or public order
- Your stay is unacceptable for foreign-policy reasons
- There is reason to suspect you will stay on unlawfully after your permitted period
- You refuse to give, or give false, information about who you are and why you are travelling

### Why you often don't get the exact reason

When a refusal is based on security, public order or foreign-policy grounds, the law says the competent authority's conclusion is not reasoned. So you often receive only a general wording. A lawyer then tries to find out what is behind the decision and whether it has a real basis.

### What to do at the border

1. Stay calm — arguing at the border will not change the decision.
2. Ask for the written decision and keep a copy or a photo of it.
3. Don't sign anything you don't understand — ask for a translation.
4. Write down the date, time, border crossing and your flight or route.
5. Contact a lawyer as soon as possible.

### Can you appeal?

Yes. The law gives a foreigner who was refused permission to cross the border the right to appeal the decision. Deadlines are short and usually run from the date of the decision, so don't wait. A lawyer can run the case while you are abroad.

### When to try again

If the reason was technical — a document, insurance or an unpaid fine — fix it first: pay the fine, prepare the documents and only then try again. If the reason relates to security, trying again without getting the decision changed will most likely end in another refusal.

### If you have family, property or a business in Georgia

A refusal doesn't freeze your other affairs. With a power of attorney, a lawyer can handle your property, company, bank and court matters while the entry issue is being resolved.

### How we help and what it costs

- Finding out the reason for the refusal and gathering information
- Contacting the authorities on your behalf
- Requesting official information in writing

Service fee: 1 300 ₾. All three services are included in the price.

## Overstaying in Georgia: fines and entry bans
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/overstay-in-georgia-fines/ — published 2026-10-11

Citizens of many countries can stay in Georgia visa-free for up to a year. If you stay after that period — or after your residence permit expires — you are breaking the law, and since 2025 the penalties are much stricter.

### The fines now

Under Article 191 of the Code of Administrative Offences (as amended in 2025):

- Overstay of up to 3 months — GEL 1,000 and a 6-month ban on entering Georgia
- Overstay of up to 1 year — GEL 2,000 and a 2-year entry ban
- Overstay of more than 1 year — GEL 3,000 and a 3-year entry ban

The fine and the ban are imposed together — paying the fine does not cancel the ban. Until the fine is paid, you won't be issued a visa or allowed to enter.

### How to avoid it

- Check in advance how long citizens of your country may stay
- If you are staying long-term, apply for a residence permit while you are still lawfully in Georgia
- If you have a residence permit, watch its expiry date and renew it in time
- Since 2026, working or running a business also requires a separate right to work

### If your residence permit was refused

A refusal can be appealed in court, but under the law an appeal does not by itself stop the authorities from considering your expulsion. Contact a lawyer as soon as you receive the refusal — they will assess whether to appeal or to file a new application on another basis.

### If you have already overstayed

Don't wait — the longer the overstay, the higher the fine and the longer the ban. Before you go to the border, review your situation with a lawyer: how many days you have overstayed, whether you have other unpaid fines, and what happens to your property, job or family matters in Georgia.

## Work permit in Georgia for foreigners from 2026
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/work-permit-georgia/ — published 2026-10-11

Since 1 March 2026 the rules for foreigners working in Georgia have changed. Visa-free status or a residence permit no longer gives you the right to work on its own — for that you need a "right to labour activity", in practice a work permit.

### What the right to work is

Under the Law on Labour Migration, it is issued by the Ministry of Labour, Health and Social Affairs. It allows a foreigner to work for a local employer or to carry out work or business activity independently in Georgia.

### Who it applies to

- Foreigners employed by a Georgian company or organisation
- Self-employed foreigners — including individual entrepreneurs
- Freelancers who provide services to clients in Georgia

The rule does not apply to foreigners with a permanent residence permit or in certain other cases set by law. Whether you need it if you only work remotely for a foreign company depends on the details — check before you rely on it.

### What you need

- The right to labour activity
- A suitable residence permit (for example, a work residence permit) or a D1 visa
- For employees — a written fixed-term employment contract in Georgian and in a language you understand

You can only apply while you are lawfully in Georgia.

### If you were already working before 2026

Foreigners registered in the labour-migration database (labourmigration.moh.gov.ge) as of 1 March 2026 get a transitional period under the law. Check whether it applies to you and by when you need to regularise your status.

### The risks

Working without the right can lead to fines for both the foreigner and the employer. It can also cause problems when you renew your residence permit or cross the border. If you have also overstayed, a separate fine and entry ban apply.

### How we help

- We assess whether you need the right to work in your case
- We prepare the documents and the application
- We help you get the right residence permit
- We appeal a refusal if it has no proper basis

## Individual entrepreneur in Georgia: the 1% tax for foreigners
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/individual-entrepreneur-georgia-1-percent-tax/ — published 2026-10-11

An individual entrepreneur (IE) with small business status is the simplest way to start a business in Georgia, so it is popular with foreigners — especially freelancers. But there are details you should know in advance.

### Registration

1. You register as an individual entrepreneur at the Public Service Hall — you need your passport and a legal address in Georgia.
2. If the address isn't yours, you need the owner's consent.
3. After registration, you apply to the Revenue Service for small business status.

### How the 1% works

- With small business status, the tax is 1% of income if your annual income does not exceed GEL 500,000
- If your annual income passes GEL 500,000, all your income is taxed at 3% from the start of that month until the end of the year
- You file a declaration and pay the tax every month, by the 15th of the following month

### What the 1% doesn't cover

Not every activity qualifies — the Government keeps a list of excluded activities. Rent, interest, dividends and similar income are not taxed at 1% either. Choosing the wrong activity is a common reason for losing the status and paying extra tax.

### What changed in 2026

Since 1 March 2026, a foreign individual entrepreneur, as a self-employed person, also needs the right to labour activity — and a suitable residence permit or visa — to work in Georgia. Registering as an IE alone is no longer enough.

### Tax residency

You become a Georgian tax resident if you spend 183 days or more in Georgia in any continuous 12-month period. Residency affects where and how your income is taxed, so it should be assessed together with the rules of your home country.

### When the small business status is lost

- If income exceeded GEL 500,000 in each of 2 consecutive calendar years — from the start of the next year
- If you carry out an activity the status doesn't cover — from the start of the current year
- If you were fined at least 3 times in a year for breaking cash register rules
- If you ask for it yourself — from the 1st of the next month

### VAT — when registration is mandatory

If your VAT-taxable transactions exceed GEL 100,000 in any continuous 12 months, you must apply to the Revenue Service for VAT registration within 2 working days (Tax Code, Article 165). Services to foreign clients may not count towards this amount — it depends on the type of service and should be checked in advance.

### Can you register remotely?

Yes. You don't have to come to Georgia: your representative registers you under a power of attorney. The power of attorney must be notarised abroad, apostilled (or legalised by a consulate) and translated into Georgian. Opening a bank account, however, usually requires you to attend in person.

### Pitfalls to watch for

- Above GEL 500,000, all income is taxed at 3% until the end of the year — not just the excess
- Not every activity qualifies for 1% — check the activity code before registering
- A declaration every month by the 15th of the next month — even a zero one
- A bank may refuse to open an account — prepare documents on the source of your income
- Registering as a sole trader doesn't give you residence or the right to work — since 2026 that is needed separately
- A sole trader doesn't automatically become a tax resident — that takes 183 days in Georgia

### How we help

- Choosing the right activity and registering
- Getting small business status
- The right to work and a residence permit
- Disputes with the Revenue Service

## Power of attorney from abroad for use in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/power-of-attorney-from-abroad/ — published 2026-10-11

Living abroad and need to sell a flat in Georgia, accept an inheritance or run a court case? You don't have to travel — a properly drafted power of attorney is enough.

### Three ways

- At a Georgian consulate — the consul certifies the power of attorney and it is valid in Georgia without further certification
- At a local notary — then, depending on the country, it needs an apostille or consular legalisation (documents from some countries need neither) and, in Georgia, a certified Georgian translation
- Online with a notary in Georgia — if you have a Georgian passport: by video call, with two witnesses present at the notary's office

### What the power of attorney should say

- Full details of both parties — names and ID or passport numbers
- Specific powers: for example, which property (by cadastral code) to sell, at what price and into whose account the money is paid
- For court — which case and which powers: filing a claim, settling, appealing
- How long it is valid and whether the representative may delegate the powers to someone else

### Why a "general" power of attorney is risky

A very broad power of attorney lets the representative deal with almost all your property. It is safer to give one for a specific matter and a reasonable period. You can revoke a power of attorney at any time — and you should notify both the representative and third parties.

### How we work

1. We send you the text in Georgian and your language, tailored to your matter.
2. You sign at the consulate, with a notary or online and, if needed, send us the original.
3. We arrange the translation and certification if needed and start the work.

## Free criminal lawyer in Georgia: who qualifies
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/free-lawyer-legal-aid-georgia/ — published 2026-10-09

Everyone has the right to a lawyer in a criminal case. If you can't afford one, in some cases the state pays for your defence — through the Legal Aid Service (legalaid.ge).

### When you are entitled to a free lawyer

Under Article 46 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the state pays for the defence in two situations:

- You are unable to pay and ask for a lawyer to be appointed
- Your case is one of mandatory defence and you have no private lawyer

### Who counts as unable to pay

Mainly a member of a family registered in the database of socially vulnerable families with a rating score of 70,000 or less. For some groups the threshold is 100,000. The detailed rules are set by Government Resolution No. 424.

### Mandatory defence — when a lawyer is required

Under Article 45, the accused must have a lawyer in cases including when they:

- Are a minor
- Don't speak the language of the proceedings
- Cannot defend themselves because of a disability
- Have been ordered to undergo a forensic psychiatric examination
- Face a possible life sentence
- Are negotiating a plea agreement
- Are tried by a jury

In these cases, if you have no private lawyer, the state appoints one regardless of your income.

### How to get a free lawyer

1. Ask for a lawyer as soon as you are arrested or before any questioning — tell the investigator, prosecutor or judge.
2. The prosecution and the judge must immediately contact the Legal Aid Service.
3. You can also apply to the Legal Aid Service yourself.

### Free or private lawyer

Many state-appointed lawyers are experienced professionals. The main difference is that you choose a private lawyer yourself — their experience, specialisation and how much time they give your case. You can hire a private lawyer at any stage, even if the case started with a state-appointed one.

## How to choose a good lawyer in Georgia: 6 tips
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/how-to-choose-a-lawyer-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-09

Choosing the right lawyer directly affects the outcome of your case. You can check a lawyer in a few simple steps — before you sign anything.

### 1. Check that they really are a lawyer

Every advocate in Georgia is listed in the Georgian Bar Association registry at gba.ge, with their name, specialisation and contact details. If someone isn't in the registry, they are not an advocate and cannot defend you in a criminal case.

### 2. Check the specialisation

A lawyer may have a general licence or one field — criminal, civil or administrative law. For a criminal case, choose a lawyer with a criminal or general specialisation; this is shown in the registry too.

### 3. Ask about experience

- How many years they have worked in this field
- Whether they have handled cases like yours — for example drugs, fraud or violence
- Whether they will work on the case personally or pass it on
- Whether they can be reached quickly — for example after an arrest

### 4. What to ask at the first meeting

- How they assess the case and what risks they see
- What they will do first
- How they will keep you informed
- What it costs and what the fee includes

### 5. The fee — upfront and in writing

A good lawyer tells you the price in advance and puts it in a contract: the cost, what it covers and how payment works. The fee depends on the complexity, stage and scope of the case.

### 6. Watch for warning signs

- They promise a guaranteed result — an honest lawyer never does
- They talk about “connections” in the court, prosecutor's office or police
- They ask for money “to pass on to someone” — that is a crime
- They won't sign a written contract
- They push you to decide and pay right now

### When there is no time

If a relative has just been arrested, you can't check everything. At minimum: check the lawyer in the registry, ask about their criminal case experience and agree the fee in writing.

## Fraud charges in Georgia: penalties and your defence
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/fraud-charges-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-06

Fraud is punished under Article 180 of the Criminal Code. It often starts from a debt, business or contract dispute — so a lawyer should assess early whether it is a crime or a civil dispute.

### What counts as fraud

Taking someone's property or obtaining a property right by deception, with the aim of appropriating it. The key question is whether there was an intent to deceive from the start. Simply failing to perform an obligation is not always a crime.

### The penalty depends on the damage

- Basic case — from a fine up to 2–4 years' imprisonment
- Significant damage (over GEL 150) or by a group — 4 to 7 years
- A large amount (over GEL 10,000), abuse of position, or repeat offences — 6 to 9 years
- By an organised group — 7 to 10 years

### What we check in your defence

- Whether there was intent to deceive from the start
- Whether the damage was calculated correctly
- Whether this is really a civil dispute
- What correspondence, contracts and transfers show

### What to do

1. Give no statement without a lawyer.
2. Keep all contracts, messages and payment records.
3. Compensating the damage can affect the sentence — decide this with your lawyer.

## Theft charges in Georgia: penalties and your rights
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/theft-charges-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-06

Theft is the secret taking of someone else's movable property with the aim of appropriating it — Article 177 of the Criminal Code. The penalty depends mainly on the value and the circumstances.

### Possible penalties

- Basic case — a fine, house arrest, or 1 to 3 years' imprisonment
- Significant damage (over GEL 150) or breaking into premises — 3 to 5 years
- By a group, repeatedly, breaking into a home, or stealing a vehicle — 4 to 7 years
- A large amount (over GEL 10,000) or by an organised group — 6 to 10 years

### What matters for the defence

- A correct valuation of the property — it decides which part of the article applies
- Whether the taking was secret and aimed at appropriation
- Video footage, identification and seizure records
- Compensating the damage and reaching agreement with the victim

### If you are arrested

Use your right to remain silent and ask for a lawyer. You must be charged within 48 hours of arrest, and within the following 24 hours a court decides on a preventive measure.

## Domestic violence charges in Georgia: what to know
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/domestic-violence-charges-georgia/ — published 2026-10-06

Domestic violence is punished under Article 126¹ of the Criminal Code. Many other crimes against a family member are also treated as "family crimes".

### Who counts as a family member

By law this includes not only a spouse and children, but parents, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren, the spouse's parents, a partner in an unregistered marriage, and a former spouse.

### What counts as domestic violence

Violence, systematic insults, blackmail or humiliation by one family member against another that caused physical pain or suffering.

### Possible penalties

- Community service of 80–150 hours or imprisonment of up to 2 years
- Against a minor, a pregnant woman or a person with a disability, in front of a minor, against two or more people, by a group or repeatedly — 1 to 3 years
- In both cases the court may also restrict weapons-related rights

### If you are accused

- Don't contact the victim — it can aggravate the charge or become a reason for detention
- Comply with any restraining or protective order
- Give no statement without a lawyer

### If you are a victim

Call 112. The police can issue a restraining order against the abuser. A lawyer can help you apply for a protective order and protect your interests in the criminal case.

## Drunk driving in Georgia: fines, licence, prison
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/drunk-driving-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-06

Driving under the influence of alcohol is, as a rule, an administrative offence (Article 116 of the Code of Administrative Offences). It becomes a crime when someone is hurt, or when a person drives under the influence of drugs.

### Licence suspension

- 0.3 to 0.7 per mille — 6 months
- Over 0.7 per mille — 1 year
- Refusing a test — the same as over 0.7: 1 year

### When it gets more serious

- Drunk driving during a suspension — GEL 2,000, administrative detention of 5–15 days and the suspension extended by 1 year
- Drunk driving that causes minor damage to a vehicle, property or health — GEL 2,000 and a 3-year suspension
- Repeat offences or driving without a licence — fines up to GEL 3,000 and administrative detention

### When it is a crime

- Driving under the influence of drugs is a criminal offence (Article 276)
- A drunk driver causes less serious harm to someone's health — 2 to 5 years
- Serious harm — 4 to 6 years
- A death — 6 to 9 years

Much in these cases depends on how the test was done. A lawyer checks whether the test and the record were correct. Fines and suspensions can be appealed.

## Bail or pre-trial detention in Georgia: how courts decide
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/bail-and-pretrial-detention-georgia/ — published 2026-10-06

A preventive measure is what the court imposes on an accused before trial — for example bail or detention. The decision is made in the first days of a case and is often the most important one for the family.

### When it is decided

A person must be charged within 48 hours of arrest, and within the following 24 hours the court decides on a preventive measure. The lawyer needs to start preparing for this hearing immediately.

### Types of preventive measures

- Bail — at least GEL 1,000, or real estate
- An agreement not to leave and to behave properly
- Personal guarantee
- Detention

The court can also add obligations: reporting to the police, electronic monitoring, a ban on meeting certain people, or surrendering a passport.

### Detention only as a last resort

By law, detention is used only when it is the only way to prevent the accused from absconding, interfering with evidence or committing a new crime. The prosecutor must justify why a milder measure is not enough. Total pre-trial detention may not exceed 9 months.

### What the court considers

- The accused's character, age and health
- Family and financial situation, employment
- Compensation of damage
- Any earlier breach of a preventive measure

### Appeal

The ruling can be appealed once to the Court of Appeals within 48 hours. So your lawyer must be ready as soon as the decision is made.

## Plea agreements in Georgia: when they're worth it
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/plea-agreement-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-06

A plea agreement is made between the prosecution and the accused. The accused admits guilt and in return agrees with the prosecutor on the sentence, a lighter charge or partial dropping of charges. The court then gives its verdict without a full trial.

### Who can propose it

Either the accused or the prosecutor can propose an agreement. The accused may also agree to cooperate or to compensate the damage.

### What to know before you sign

- It is a guilty verdict — you will have a criminal record
- The court no longer examines the evidence in detail
- It doesn't release you from civil liability — the victim can still claim damages in court
- The prosecutor must explain all the consequences to you

### What the court checks

The court checks whether the charge is well-founded and whether the sentence is lawful and fair. If not, it can refuse to approve the agreement.

### The victim

The prosecutor must consult the victim before the agreement. The victim cannot appeal the agreement but keeps the right to file a civil claim.

### When it's worth it

It depends on the strength of the evidence and what is being offered. Sometimes an agreement is the right decision, sometimes defending at trial is. Don't sign until your lawyer has reviewed the case file.

## Arrested for drugs in Georgia: what to do
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/arrested-for-drugs-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-05

Drug arrests happen fast, and a mistake in the first hours can decide the case. Here is what you need to know.

### Your rights when arrested

- The right to remain silent — you don't have to give a statement without a lawyer
- The right to a lawyer from the moment of arrest
- The right to have a family member informed
- The right to read the record and add your comments

### Search and seizure

Watch who is present at the search, what is taken and how it is packed. If the record doesn't match what happened, don't sign it — or add a note.

### Drug testing

Police may ask for a test if they have sufficient grounds. Avoiding a test is itself an administrative offence — a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or administrative detention of up to 60 days.

### Deadlines

You must be charged within 48 hours of arrest, and within the next 24 hours a court decides on a preventive measure. Your lawyer should already be involved by then.

### Possible penalties

- First-time use or possession of a small amount — as a rule, an administrative penalty
- The same again after an administrative penalty — a criminal offence
- Buying and possession — imprisonment of up to 6 years; more for large amounts
- Sale and import — serious crimes with long sentences

### Mistakes to avoid

- "Explaining" without a lawyer
- Signing a record without reading it
- Giving your phone password without legal advice
- Accepting a plea agreement without a lawyer's advice

## Marijuana law in Georgia: what gets you fined?
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/marijuana-law-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-05

Many people think marijuana is allowed in Georgia in every case. It isn't — the law punishes many acts with fines or criminal liability.

### Small amounts: a fine

Buying, possessing, transporting or sending a small amount of marijuana is an administrative offence — a GEL 500 fine.

### Where using it is punished

- In any building except a private home — GEL 500–1,000
- On the street, in parks, cafés, public transport and other public places — GEL 800–1,200
- In front of minors or near schools — GEL 1,000–1,500
- Repeat offences — higher fines

### Under 18s

Use by a person under 18 is fined GEL 500–1,000, and more for a repeat offence.

### When it becomes a crime

- More than a small amount — for example, over 5 grams of dried marijuana
- Selling or giving it to someone — even for free
- Bringing it into or out of Georgia
- Growing the plant

The amounts are set in an annex to the law. If you were fined or a case was opened against you, contact a lawyer — fines can be appealed too.

## Unfairly dismissed in Georgia? What to do
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/unlawful-dismissal-georgia/ — published 2026-10-05

Losing your job is stressful, but if your employer broke the law you can protect your rights. The key is to act quickly and correctly.

### Step 1: Ask for the written grounds

Ask your employer to explain the grounds for your dismissal in writing. This document matters, because it is exactly what gets examined later.

### Step 2: Keep every document

- Employment contract and amendments
- The dismissal order
- Correspondence with your employer — emails, messages
- Salary statements

### Step 3: Don't miss the deadlines

Deadlines for challenging a dismissal are short, so contact a lawyer as soon as possible — ideally as soon as you receive the written grounds.

### What you can claim

- Reinstatement
- Pay for the period you were forced out of work
- Compensation if reinstatement is impossible or you don't want it

### Mistakes to avoid

- Signing a "voluntary resignation" under pressure
- Deleting documents and correspondence
- Missing the deadline

## Accepting an inheritance in Georgia from abroad
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/inheritance-from-abroad/ — published 2026-10-05

If you live abroad and a family member in Georgia has died, you can accept the inheritance without coming — through a power of attorney.

### The key point: the 6-month deadline

An inheritance must be accepted within 6 months of its opening — as a rule, the date of death. The application to the notary can be filed by your representative.

### How to issue a power of attorney

- At a Georgian embassy or consulate — no further certification needed
- With a local notary — depending on the country, an apostille or legalisation may be needed, plus a certified Georgian translation
- Online with a notary in Georgia — if you have a Georgian passport: you join by video call, with two witnesses present at the notary

Prepare the text with your lawyer in advance so it covers all the powers needed.

### Documents you'll need

- Death certificate
- Proof of kinship
- Your ID document
- Property documents or a Public Registry extract

### If you missed the deadline

If you missed it for a valid reason, a court can extend it. Contact a lawyer as soon as possible.

### What happens next

The notary issues a certificate of inheritance, and the property is registered in your name with the Public Registry. You can then sell or rent it out — also by power of attorney.

## Scammed online? How to try to get your money back
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/online-fraud-what-to-do/ — published 2026-10-05

With online fraud, time is everything. The faster you act, the better your chances of getting the money back.

### The first hours: what to do

1. Contact your bank immediately — block the card and dispute the payment.
2. Change your passwords and turn on two-factor authentication.
3. Keep everything — messages, links, account numbers, transactions and screenshots.
4. Contact a lawyer — they will prepare the complaint to the police.

### Common scams

- Fake online shops and listings
- A "bank employee" calling to ask for codes or card details
- Investment and crypto "opportunities"
- Fake links by SMS or messenger

### Beware of "money recovery" services

After a scam, services often appear promising to recover your money for an upfront fee. As a rule, this is another scam.

### Can the money be recovered?

Sometimes, yes — especially if you contact the bank quickly or the offender is identified. A lawyer helps you prepare the evidence correctly and protects your interests as a victim.

## How to appeal a fine in Georgia
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/how-to-appeal-a-fine/ — published 2026-10-05

A fine is an administrative decision and can be appealed — if it is groundless or was imposed in breach of the law.

### Step 1: Read the decision carefully

The decision usually states who fined you, on what grounds, where it can be appealed and within what deadline. Note when you received it — the deadline runs from that day.

### Step 2: Gather evidence

- Photos and video recordings
- Witnesses' contact details
- Receipts, tickets, permits — anything that supports your position

### Step 3: File a complaint or lawsuit

Depending on the type of fine, it can be appealed to a superior body or in court. A lawyer will assess which route is faster and more effective.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Missing the deadline — it's short
- Not recording the date you received the decision
- Complaining without evidence
- Ignoring notices

## Buying an apartment in Georgia: what to check
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/buying-an-apartment-checklist/ — published 2026-10-05

Buying an apartment is one of the biggest financial decisions. A few checks in advance protect you from big problems.

### 1. Public Registry extract

Check who the owner is, the size of the apartment, and whether there is a mortgage, seizure or prohibition. Get an up-to-date extract.

### 2. The seller

- Check the seller's ID and that they are the owner
- If the apartment was bought during a marriage, the spouse's consent may be needed
- If there are several owners, all of them must agree
- If the seller acts under a power of attorney, check it

### 3. New builds

- Does the developer have a construction permit?
- What stage is construction at?
- In the contract: the completion date and liability for delays

### 4. Debts and payment

Check for utility debts. Pay in a way that is documented — and only after signing the contract or through a secure mechanism.

### 5. Registration

Ownership arises on registration with the Public Registry. Until registration is complete, the apartment isn't legally yours.

## Registering an LLC in Georgia: what you need
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/how-to-register-llc-in-georgia/ — published 2026-10-05

An LLC is the most common business form in Georgia. Registration is fast if the documents are prepared correctly.

### What you need

- A company name
- Details of the partners and the director
- A charter
- A legal address in Georgia — with the owner's consent

### How registration works

The company is registered with the Public Registry, usually within one business day. It is registered as a taxpayer at the same time.

### Can a foreigner do it?

Yes. Foreign individuals and companies can be an LLC's sole partner and director. Depending on the country, documents issued abroad may need an apostille or consular legalisation (documents from some countries need neither) and a certified Georgian translation.

### After registration

- Opening a bank account
- Setting up accounting and understanding your tax obligations
- Signing a shareholder agreement if there are several partners

### Mistakes to avoid

- Using a template charter without adapting it
- Having no written agreement between partners
- Mixing personal and company money

## Residence permits in Georgia: which type do you need?
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/residence-permit-types-georgia/ — published 2026-10-05

Citizens of many countries can stay in Georgia visa-free for up to a year, but living, working or doing business here long-term usually requires a residence permit.

### The main types

- Work — for employment in Georgia
- Business — for running your own business in Georgia
- Property — if you own property whose value meets the legal threshold
- Family — to join a family member
- Study — for studying in Georgia
- Investment — for an investment of the amount set by law

### How to choose the right type

The right type depends on why you need to live in Georgia and which documents can prove it. Choosing the wrong type is a common reason for refusal.

### Where to apply

Applications are filed at the Public Service Hall. Depending on the country, documents issued abroad may need an apostille or consular legalisation (documents from some countries need neither) and a certified Georgian translation.

### If you are refused

A refusal is an administrative decision and can be appealed. Deadlines are short, so contact a lawyer as soon as you receive it.

## Police search in Georgia: your rights and what to do
URL: https://mmlaw.ge/en/blog/police-search-your-rights/ — published 2026-10-04

A search is stressful, but acting correctly protects you from mistakes that can make your case harder later. Here is a short, practical guide.

### On what basis is a search carried out

As a rule, a search is carried out on the basis of a court order. In urgent cases it can be done without one, but a court must then review whether it was lawful. You have the right to see the document on which the search is based.

### Your rights during a search

- To see the basis for the search — the court order or decision
- To contact your lawyer and ask for them to come
- Not to give a statement — you have the right to remain silent
- To read the search record, write your remarks and receive a copy
- To have every item taken listed in the record

### What to do

1. Stay calm and do not physically resist.
2. Ask for the document and read carefully which address it covers and what it is for.
3. Call your lawyer immediately.
4. Don't discuss the details of the case during the search.
5. Sign the record only after reading it; if anything is inaccurate, write your objection.

### Mistakes to avoid

- Physically resisting — this creates separate liability
- Hiding or destroying items
- Giving "explanations" without a lawyer
- Signing the record without reading it

## Child support (alimony) in Georgia: how the amount is set
